DC57EDA0DFE60131B15268A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the impact of rhymes and other repetitions of sounds (e.g., alliteration) on a specific verse or stanza of a poem or section of a story or drama.

DC5739F0DFE60131B15068A86D17958E.description: Analyze how particular elements of a story or drama interact (e.g., how setting shapes the characters or plot).

DC56DE10DFE60131B14F68A86D17958E.description: Determine a theme or central idea of a text and analyze its development over the course of the text; provide an objective summary of the text.

DC568E60DFE60131B14E68A86D17958E.description: Cite several pieces of textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

DC5592C0DFE60131B14B68A86D17958E.description: Respond to literature by employing knowledge of literary language, textual features, and forms to read and comprehend, reflect upon, and interpret literary texts from a variety of genres and a wide spectrum of American and world cultures.

DC54B3F0DFE60131B14968A86D17958E.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

DC5461A0DFE60131B14868A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

DC540CC0DFE60131B14768A86D17958E.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

DC53B9C0DFE60131B14668A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

DC535A10DFE60131B14568A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.
comments: Please see "Research to Build and Present Knowledge" in Writing and "Comprehension and Collaboration" in Speaking and Listening for additional standards relevant to gathering, assessing, and applying information from print and digital sources.

DC52BBF0DFE60131B14368A86D17958E.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

DC5269F0DFE60131B14268A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

DC521A00DFE60131B14168A86D17958E.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

DC5169C0DFE60131B13F68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

DC511990DFE60131B13E68A86D17958E.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

DC50BFD0DFE60131B13D68A86D17958E.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

DC5002C0DFE60131B13B68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Reading

document.title: Learning Standards for The Arts

E4A4C740DFE60131C18E68A86D17958E.description: create art works that reflect a particular historical period of a culture

E4A47C10DFE60131C18D68A86D17958E.description: demonstrate the ways in which some particular art works and artifacts reflect important aspects of the diverse cultures of the United States

E4A42660DFE60131C18C68A86D17958E.description: demonstrate how art works and artifacts from diverse world cultures reflect aspects of those cultures

E4A3E1C0DFE60131C18B68A86D17958E.description: Students will explore art and artifacts from various historical periods and world cultures to discover the roles that art plays in the lives of people of a given time and place and to understand how the time and place influence the visual characteristics of the art work. Students will explore art to understand the social, cultural, and environmental dimensions of human society.

E4A39D50DFE60131C18A68A86D17958E.description: explain how drama/theatre experiences relate to themselves and others

E4A35500DFE60131C18968A86D17958E.description: create intercultural celebrations using props, settings, and costumes

E4A302A0DFE60131C18868A86D17958E.description: improvise scenes based on information about various cultures

E4A2AC40DFE60131C18768A86D17958E.description: Students will gain knowledge about past and present cultures as expressed through theatre. They will interpret how theatre reflects the beliefs, issues, and events of societies past and present.

E4A24F80DFE60131C18668A86D17958E.description: in performing ensembles, read and perform repertoire in a culturally authentic manner

E4A20B70DFE60131C18568A86D17958E.description: discuss the current and past cultural, social, and political uses for the music they listen to and perform

E4A1C570DFE60131C18468A86D17958E.description: identify from a performance or recording the titles and composers of well-known examples of classical concert music and blues/jazz selections

E4A17BC0DFE60131C18368A86D17958E.description: identify the cultural contexts of a performance or recording and perform (with movement, where culturally appropriate) a varied repertoire of folk, art, and contemporary selections from the basic cultures that represent the peoples of the world

E4A130E0DFE60131C18268A86D17958E.description: Students will develop a performing and listening repertoire of music of various genres, styles, and cultures that represent the peoples of the world and their manifestations in the United States. Students will recognize the cultural features of a variety of musical compositions and performances and understand the functions of music within the culture.

E4A0E870DFE60131C18168A86D17958E.description: show how specific dance forms are related to the culture from which they come

E4A09A40DFE60131C18068A86D17958E.description: identify some of the major dance artists from diverse cultures

E4A056E0DFE60131C17F68A86D17958E.description: identify the major dance forms of specific world cultures past and present

E4A00FE0DFE60131C17E68A86D17958E.description: Students will know dances from many cultures and times and recognize their relationship to various cultural, social, and historic contexts. Students will recognize that dance is performed in many different cultural settings and serves many functions in diverse societies.

E49FC640DFE60131C17D68A86D17958E.description: Students will develop an understanding of the personal and cultural forces that shape artistic communication and how the arts in turn shape the diverse cultures of past and present society.

E49F8180DFE60131C17C68A86D17958E.description: Understanding the Cultural Dimensions and Contributions of the Arts

E49F35A0DFE60131C17B68A86D17958E.description: compare the ways ideas, themes, and concepts are communicated through the visual arts in other disciplines, and the various ways that those ideas, themes, and concepts are manifested within the discipline

E49EE650DFE60131C17A68A86D17958E.description: compare the ways ideas and concepts are communicated through visual art with the various ways that those ideas and concepts are manifested in other art forms

E49EA320DFE60131C17968A86D17958E.description: identify, analyze, and interpret the visual and sensory characteristics that they discover in natural and human-made forms

E49E6010DFE60131C17868A86D17958E.description: discuss and write their analyses and interpretations of their own works of art and the art of others, using appropriate critical language

E49E18D0DFE60131C17768A86D17958E.description: Students will reflect on, interpret, and evaluate works of art, using the language of art criticism. Students will analyze the visual characteristics of the natural and built environment and explain the social, cultural, psychological, and environmental dimensions of the visual arts. Students will compare the ways in which a variety of ideas, themes, and concepts are expressed through the visual arts with the ways they are expressed in other disciplines.

E49DC970DFE60131C17668A86D17958E.description: explain how drama/theatre experiences relate to other literary and artistic events

E49D7E10DFE60131C17568A86D17958E.description: examine and discuss the use of other art forms in a theatre production

E49D1800DFE60131C17468A86D17958E.description: use the techniques and vocabulary of theatre criticism, both written and oral, to discuss theatre experiences and improve individual and group performances

E49CD220DFE60131C17368A86D17958E.description: Students will reflect on, interpret, and evaluate plays and theatrical performances, both live and recorded, using the language of dramatic criticism. Students will analyze the meaning and role of theatre in society. Students will identify ways in which drama/theatre connects to film and video, other arts, and other disciplines.

E49C8B10DFE60131C17268A86D17958E.description: use terminology from music and other arts to analyze and compare the structures of musical and other artistic and literary works

E49C4080DFE60131C17168A86D17958E.description: use basic scientific concepts to explain how music-related sound is produced, transmitted through air, and perceived

E49BEBF0DFE60131C17068A86D17958E.description: use appropriate terms to reflect a working knowledge of social-musical functions and uses (appropriate choices of music for common ceremonies and other events)

E49B8830DFE60131C16F68A86D17958E.description: demonstrate a basic awareness of the technical skills musicians must develop to produce an aesthetically acceptable performance

E49B3BF0DFE60131C16E68A86D17958E.description: use appropriate terms to reflect a working knowledge of the musical elements

E49AF630DFE60131C16D68A86D17958E.description: through listening, analyze and evaluate their own and others' performances, improvisations, and compositions by identifying and comparing them with similar works and events

E49AAC60DFE60131C16C68A86D17958E.description: Students will demonstrate the capacity to listen to and comment on music. They will relate their critical assertions about music to its aesthetic, structural, acoustic, and psychological qualities. Students will use concepts based on the structure of music's content and context to relate music to other broad areas of knowledge. They will use concepts from other disciplines to enhance their understanding of music.

E49A6620DFE60131C16B68A86D17958E.description: express to others their understanding of specific dance performances, including perceptions, descriptions, analyses, interpretations, and evaluations

E49A1E60DFE60131C16A68A86D17958E.description: demonstrate knowledge of choreographic principles and processes

E499CC20DFE60131C16968A86D17958E.description: demonstrate knowledge of the technical language used in discussing dance performances

E4997AE0DFE60131C16868A86D17958E.description: Students will express through written and oral language their understanding, interpretation, and evaluation of dances they see, do, and read about. Students will acquire the critical vocabulary to talk and write about a variety of dance forms.

E4993690DFE60131C16768A86D17958E.description: Students will respond critically to a variety of works in the arts, connecting the individual work to other works and to other aspects of human endeavor and thought.

E498E830DFE60131C16668A86D17958E.description: Responding to and Analyzing Works of Art

E4989A20DFE60131C16568A86D17958E.description: understand the variety of careers related to the visual arts and the skills necessary to pursue some of them

E4983850DFE60131C16468A86D17958E.description: take advantage of community opportunities and cultural institutions to learn from professional artists, look at original art, and increase their understanding of art

E497E2D0DFE60131C16368A86D17958E.description: use the computer and other electronic media as designing tools and to communicate visual ideas

E4979F00DFE60131C16268A86D17958E.description: develop skills with a variety of art materials and competence in at least one medium

E49755E0DFE60131C16168A86D17958E.description: Students will know and use a variety of visual arts materials, techniques, and processes. Students will know about resources and opportunities for participation in visual arts in the community (exhibitions, libraries, museums, galleries) and use appropriate materials (art reproductions, slides, print materials, electronic media). Students will be aware of vocational options available in the visual arts.

E4970800DFE60131C16068A86D17958E.description: discuss vocations/avocations with theatre professionals and identify the skills and preparation necessary for theatre vocations/avocations

E496C2D0DFE60131C15F68A86D17958E.description: know about local theatrical institutions, attend performances in school and in the community, and demonstrate appropriate audience behavior

E4967830DFE60131C15E68A86D17958E.description: use the school or community library/media centers and other resources to develop information on various theatre-related topics

E4960890DFE60131C15D68A86D17958E.description: visit theatre technology facilities, including the local high school facility, and interact with professionals and theatre students to learn about theatre technology (e.g., lighting, staging, sound, etc.)

E495B220DFE60131C15C68A86D17958E.description: Students will know the basic tools, media, and techniques involved in theatrical production. Students will locate and use school, community, and professional resources for theatre experiences. Students will understand the job opportunities available in all aspects of theatre.

E4956D00DFE60131C15B68A86D17958E.description: investigate some career options related to their musical interests

E49525F0DFE60131C15A68A86D17958E.description: demonstrate appropriate listening and other participatory responses to music of a variety of genres and cultures

E494E040DFE60131C15968A86D17958E.description: identify a community-based musical interest or role and explain the skills, knowledge, and resources necessary to pursue the interest or adopt the role

E4949320DFE60131C15868A86D17958E.description: use current technology to create, produce and record/playback music

E4944930DFE60131C15768A86D17958E.description: use school and community resources to develop information on music and musicians

E493FEC0DFE60131C15668A86D17958E.description: use traditional or nontraditional sound sources, including electronic ones, in composing and performing simple pieces

E493AA80DFE60131C15568A86D17958E.description: Students will use traditional instruments, electronic instruments, and a variety of nontraditional sound sources to create and perform music. They will use various resources to expand their knowledge of listening experiences, performance opportunities, and/or information about music. Students will identify opportunities to contribute to their communities' music institutions, including those embedded in other institutions (church choirs, industrial music ensembles, etc.). Students will know the vocations and avocations available to them in music.

E4935F90DFE60131C15468A86D17958E.description: demonstrate knowledge of differences in performance venue and the events presented in each

E492FF00DFE60131C15368A86D17958E.description: demonstrate knowledge of audience/performer responsibilities and relationships in dance

E492B220DFE60131C15268A86D17958E.description: demonstrate knowledge of how human structure and function affect movement in parts of dances and dances that they know or have choreographed

E49271B0DFE60131C15168A86D17958E.description: demonstrate knowledge of how human structure and function affect movement in parts of dances and dances that they know or have choreographed

E4923020DFE60131C15068A86D17958E.description: demonstrate knowledge of sources for understanding dance technologies: live, print, video, computer, etc.

E491ED60DFE60131C14F68A86D17958E.description: Students will know how to access dance and dance-related material from libraries, resource centers, museums, studios, and performance spaces. Students will know various career possibilities in dance and recreational opportunities to dance. Students will attend dance events and participate as appropriate within each setting.

E491A770DFE60131C14E68A86D17958E.description: Students will be knowledgeable about and make use of the materials and resources available for participation in the arts in various roles.

E4916230DFE60131C14D68A86D17958E.description: Knowing and Using Arts Materials and Resources

E4911880DFE60131C14C68A86D17958E.description: identify and use, in individual and group experiences, some of the roles and means for designing, producing, and exhibiting art works and discuss ways to improve them

E490BE10DFE60131C14B68A86D17958E.description: during the creative process, reflect on the effectiveness of selected mediums or techniques to convey intended meanings

E4906B90DFE60131C14A68A86D17958E.description: use the elements and principles of art to communicate specific meanings to others in their art work

E4901010DFE60131C14968A86D17958E.description: know and use a variety of sources for developing and conveying ideas, images, themes, symbols, and events in their creation of art

E48FCA80DFE60131C14868A86D17958E.description: produce a collection of art works, in a variety of mediums, based on a range of individual and collective experiences

E48F83D0DFE60131C14768A86D17958E.description: Students will make works of art that explore different kinds of subject matter, topics, themes, and metaphors. Students will understand and use sensory elements, organizational principles, and expressive images to communicate their own ideas in works of art. Students will use a variety of art materials, processes, mediums, and techniques, and use appropriate technologies for creating and exhibiting visual art works.

E48F3B60DFE60131C14668A86D17958E.description: identify and use, in individual and group experiences, some of the roles, processes, and actions for performing and creating theatre pieces and improvisational drama within the school/community, and discuss ways to improve them

E48EE590DFE60131C14568A86D17958E.description: create props, scenery, and costumes through individual and group effort

E48EA560DFE60131C14468A86D17958E.description: use language, voice, gesture, movement and observation to create character and interact with others in improvisation, rehearsal, and performance

E48E6480DFE60131C14368A86D17958E.description: imitate various experiences through pantomime, play making, dramatic play, story dramatization, storytelling, role playing, improvisation and guided play writing

E48E2340DFE60131C14268A86D17958E.description: use improvisation and guided play writing to communicate ideas and feelings

E48DE020DFE60131C14168A86D17958E.description: Students will create and perform theatre pieces as well as improvisational drama. They will understand and use the basic elements of theatre in their characterizations, improvisations, and play writing. Students will engage in individual and group theatrical and theatre-related tasks, and will describe the various roles and means of creating, performing, and producing theatre.

E48D9B90DFE60131C14068A86D17958E.description: identify and use, in individual and group experiences, some of the roles, processes, and actions for performing and composing music of their own and others, and discuss ways to improve them

E48D4EE0DFE60131C13F68A86D17958E.description: in performing ensembles, read moderately easy/moderately difficult music (New York State School Music Association [NYSSMA] level III-IV) and respond appropriately to the gestures of the conductor

E48CFD30DFE60131C13E68A86D17958E.description: improvise short musical compositions that exhibit cohesiveness and musical expression

E48CBB80DFE60131C13D68A86D17958E.description: sing and/or play, alone and in combination with other voice or instrument parts, a varied repertoire of folk, art, and contemporary songs, from notation, with a good tone, pitch, duration, and loudness

E48C7920DFE60131C13C68A86D17958E.description: compose simple pieces that reflect a knowledge of melodic, rhythmic, harmonic, timbrel, and dynamic elements

E48C2890DFE60131C13B68A86D17958E.description: Students will compose original music and perform music written by others. They will understand and use the basic elements of music in their performances and compositions. Students will engage in individual and group musical and music-related tasks, and will describe the various roles and means of creating, performing, recording, and producing music.

E48BD950DFE60131C13A68A86D17958E.description: demonstrate the ability to take various roles in group productions and performances

E48B8120DFE60131C13968A86D17958E.description: create or improvise dance phrases, studies, and dances, alone and/or in collaboration with others, in a variety of contexts

E48B2CB0DFE60131C13868A86D17958E.description: dance a range of forms from free improvisation to structured choreography

E48AD3F0DFE60131C13768A86D17958E.description: know and demonstrate a range of movement elements and skills (such as balance, alignment, elevation, and landing) and basic dance steps, positions, and patterns

E48A6330DFE60131C13668A86D17958E.description: Students will perform set dance forms in formal and informal contexts and will improvise, create, and perform dances based on their own movement ideas. They will demonstrate an understanding of choreographic principles, processes, and structures and of the roles of various participants in dance productions.

E48A1130DFE60131C13568A86D17958E.description: Students will actively engage in the processes that constitute creation and performance in the arts (dance, music, theatre, and visual arts) and participate in various roles in the arts.

D7724290DFE60131A8FD68A86D17958E.description: Graph the solutions to a linear inequality in two variables as a half-plane (excluding the boundary in the case of a strict inequality), and graph the solution set to a system of linear inequalities in two variables as the intersection of the corresponding half-planes.

D771E4E0DFE60131A8FC68A86D17958E.description: Explain why the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations y = f(x) and y = g(x) intersect are the solutions of the equation f(x) = g(x); find the solutions approximately, e.g., using technology to graph the functions, make tables of values, or find successive approximations. Include cases where f(x) and/or g(x) are linear, polynomial, rational, absolute value, exponential, and logarithmic functions.
comments: Modeling is best interpreted not as a collection of isolated topics but in relation to other standards. Making mathematical models is a Standard for Mathematical Practice, and specific modeling standards appear throughout the high school standards indicated by a star symbol (★). The star symbol sometimes appears on the heading for a group of standards; in that case, it should be understood to apply to all standards in that group.

D7718DC0DFE60131A8FB68A86D17958E.description: Understand that the graph of an equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions plotted in the coordinate plane, often forming a curve (which could be a line).

D7712D30DFE60131A8FA68A86D17958E.description: Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically

D770CBF0DFE60131A8F968A86D17958E.description: (+) Find the inverse of a matrix if it exists and use it to solve systems of linear equations (using technology for matrices of dimension 3 × 3 or greater).

D7707190DFE60131A8F868A86D17958E.description: (+) Represent a system of linear equations as a single matrix equation in a vector variable.

D7701CD0DFE60131A8F768A86D17958E.description: Solve a simple system consisting of a linear equation and a quadratic equation in two variables algebraically and graphically.
comments: For example, find the points of intersection between the line y = -3x and the circle x² + y² = 3.

D76FC600DFE60131A8F668A86D17958E.description: Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately (e.g., with graphs), focusing on pairs of linear equations in two variables.

D76F5660DFE60131A8F568A86D17958E.description: Prove that, given a system of two equations in two variables, replacing one equation by the sum of that equation and a multiple of the other produces a system with the same solutions.

Recognize when the quadratic formula gives complex solutions and write them as a ± bi for real numbers a and b.

D76E1CB0DFE60131A8F268A86D17958E.description: Use the method of completing the square to transform any quadratic equation in x into an equation of the form (x - p)² = q that has the same solutions. Derive the quadratic formula from this form.

comments: Modeling is best interpreted not as a collection of isolated topics but in relation to other standards. D7690700DFE60131A8E468A86D17958E.description: (+) Understand that rational expressions form a system analogous to the rational numbers, closed under addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division by a nonzero rational expression; add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational expressions.

D768A0A0DFE60131A8E368A86D17958E.description: Rewrite simple rational expressions in different forms; write <sup>a(x </sup>/<sub>b(x)</sub> in the form q(x) + <sup>r(x)</sup>/<sub>b(x)</sub>, where a(x), b(x), q(x), and r(x) are polynomials with the degree of r(x) less than the degree of b(x), using inspection, long division, or, for the more complicated examples, a computer algebra system.

D7666E40DFE60131A8DD68A86D17958E.description: Know and apply the Remainder Theorem: For a polynomial p(x) and a number a, the remainder on division by x - a is p(a), so p(a) = 0 if and only if (x - a) is a factor of p(x).

D765BA00DFE60131A8DB68A86D17958E.description: Understand that polynomials form a system analogous to the integers, namely, they are closed under the operations of addition, subtraction, and multiplication; add, subtract, and multiply polynomials.

D76501D0DFE60131A8D968A86D17958E.description: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions

D7649160DFE60131A8D868A86D17958E.description: Derive the formula for the sum of a finite geometric series (when the common ratio is not 1), and use the formula to solve problems.

D7629D00DFE60131A8D368A86D17958E.description: Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems

D7623B70DFE60131A8D268A86D17958E.description: Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it.
comments: For example, see x<sup>4</sup> — y<sup>4</sup> as (x²)² — (y²)², thus recognizing it as a difference of squares that can be factored as (x² — y²)(x² + y²).

comments: For example, interpret P(1+r)<sup>n</sup> as the product of P and a factor not depending on P.

comments: Modeling is best interpreted not as a collection of isolated topics but in relation to other standards. Making mathematical models is a Standard for Mathematical Practice, and specific modeling standards appear throughout the high school standards indicated by a star symbol (★). The star symbol sometimes appears on the heading for a group of standards; in that case, it should be understood to apply to all standards in that group.

35C2D94EA2984081BF6F4DE49F3CE630.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.
comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.

BDAA094192FD48D88483430AA64D3128.description: Look for and make use of structure.
comments: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.

Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

635CB87E9B2B47208F36D7976D310DC7.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.
comments: Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.

Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

71CF436F655E4368A86D7AE3554DC698.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
comments: Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.

DE636F80DFE60131B57F68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that individual letters have associated sounds

DE631000DFE60131B57E68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and name automatically all uppercase and lowercase manuscript letters

DE626AF0DFE60131B57C68A86D17958E.description: Identify the parts of a book and their functions (e.g., front cover, back cover, and title page)

DE6211E0DFE60131B57B68A86D17958E.description: Track print by pointing to written words when texts are read aloud by self or others

DE612960DFE60131B57868A86D17958E.description: Follow left-to-right and top-to-bottom direction when reading English

DE60D410DFE60131B57768A86D17958E.description: Understand the purpose of print is to communicate

DE602650DFE60131B57568A86D17958E.description: Substitute one phoneme for another to make a new word ("The word is rug. Change /g/ to /n/. What is the new word?")—Phoneme Substitution

DE5FD630DFE60131B57468A86D17958E.description: Make a new word by adding a phoneme to an existing word ("What word do you have if you add /s/ to mile?"—Phoneme Addition

DE5F85E0DFE60131B57368A86D17958E.description: Recognize the remaining word when a phoneme is removed ("What is cat without the /k/?")—Phoneme Deletion

DE5F3390DFE60131B57268A86D17958E.description: Segment spoken words into component sounds using manipulatives (e.g., counters) to represent each sound ("How many sounds are there in big? Move three counters.")—Phoneme Segmentation

DE5EDD20DFE60131B57168A86D17958E.description: Blend spoken phonemes to form words using manipulatives (e.g., counters) to represent each sound: /b/ /i/ /g/—Phoneme Blending

DE5E8730DFE60131B57068A86D17958E.description: Categorize the word in a set of three or four words that has a different sound ("Which word doesn't belong: doll, dish, pill?")—Phoneme Categorization

DE5E15F0DFE60131B56F68A86D17958E.description: Identify the same sounds in different spoken words ("What sound is the same in sit, sip, and sun?")—Phoneme Identity

DE5D9EB0DFE60131B56E68A86D17958E.description: Isolate individual sounds within spoken words ("What is the first sound in can?")—Phoneme Isolation

DE5D51D0DFE60131B56D68A86D17958E.description: Count or tap the number of syllables in spoken words

DE5D0420DFE60131B56C68A86D17958E.description: Blend beginning sound (onset) with ending sound (rime) to form known words in rhyming word families (k-it, s-it, b-it)

DE5C05B0DFE60131B56968A86D17958E.description: Use computer software to support early reading development

DE5BA920DFE60131B56868A86D17958E.description: Read aloud with expression and fluency

DE5B4330DFE60131B56768A86D17958E.description: Monitor own reading by applying strategies (e.g., sounding out letters; using context, grammar, and picture clues; and rereading) to determine meaning

DE5A6B40DFE60131B56568A86D17958E.description: Recognize that words consist of a combination of sounds

DE59CFC0DFE60131B56368A86D17958E.description: Recognize own name and the names of friends and family in print

DE598450DFE60131B56268A86D17958E.description: Recognize the singular and plural of frequently used words

DE593450DFE60131B56168A86D17958E.description: Point to words in a text or on a chart when read aloud, matching spoken word to print

DE58DA10DFE60131B56068A86D17958E.description: Recognize the different sounds that make up a word

DE588D00DFE60131B55F68A86D17958E.description: Use beginning and ending consonants, as well as vowel sounds, to identify words

DE583C80DFE60131B55E68A86D17958E.description: Distinguish the difference between vowels and consonants

DE57F2E0DFE60131B55D68A86D17958E.description: Alphabetize high-frequency words according to the first letter

DE57A970DFE60131B55C68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and identify letters of the alphabet

DE570550DFE60131B55A68A86D17958E.description: Follow left-to-right and top to bottom direction when reading

DE56B7B0DFE60131B55968A86D17958E.description: Recognize the difference between letters and words

document.title: Learning Standards for Mathematics, Science, and Technology - Standard 5

E6D2FD50DFE60131C4D468A86D17958E.description: speculate on and model possible technological solutions that can improve the safety and quality of the school or community environment.

E6D33C10DFE60131C4D568A86D17958E.description: participate in small group projects and in structured group tasks requiring planning, financing, production, quality control, and follow-up.

E6D2BD80DFE60131C4D368A86D17958E.description: Project management is essential to ensuring that technological endeavors are profitable and that products and systems are of high quality and built safely, on schedule, and within budget.

E6D228B0DFE60131C4D168A86D17958E.description: describe how technology can have positive and negative effects on the environment and on the way people live and work.

E6D1DE70DFE60131C4D068A86D17958E.description: Technology can have positive and negative impacts on individuals, society, and the environment and humans have the capability and responsibility to constrain or promote technological development.

E6D13FD0DFE60131C4CE68A86D17958E.description: identify technological developments that have significantly accelerated human progress.

E6D0FBC0DFE60131C4CD68A86D17958E.description: Technology has been the driving force in the evolution of society from an agricultural to an industrial to an information base.

E6D06EA0DFE60131C4CB68A86D17958E.description: understand that larger systems are made up of smaller component subsystems.

E6D031B0DFE60131C4CA68A86D17958E.description: assemble and operate simple technological systems, including those with interconnecting mechanisms to achieve different kinds of movement.

E6CFF380DFE60131C4C968A86D17958E.description: identify familiar examples of technological systems that are used to satisfy human needs and wants, and select them on the basis of safety, cost, and function.

E6CFB400DFE60131C4C868A86D17958E.description: Technological systems are designed to achieve specific results and produce outputs, such as products, structures, services, energy, or other systems.

E6CEE880DFE60131C4C568A86D17958E.description: model and simulate the design of a complex environment by giving direct commands.

E6CE3AA0DFE60131C4C368A86D17958E.description: control computerized devices and systems through programming.

E6CF3180DFE60131C4C668A86D17958E.description: use the computer as a tool for generating and drawing ideas.

E6CE8830DFE60131C4C468A86D17958E.description: identify and describe the function of the major components of a computer system.

E6CDFD00DFE60131C4C268A86D17958E.description: Computers, as tools for design, modeling, information processing, communication, and system control, have greatly increased human productivity and knowledge.

E6CD8300DFE60131C4C068A86D17958E.description: use appropriate graphic and electronic tools and techniques to process information.

E6CD42C0DFE60131C4BF68A86D17958E.description: use simple manufacturing processes (e.g., assembly, multiple stages of production, quality control) to produce a product.

E6CCFD40DFE60131C4BE68A86D17958E.description: develop basic skill in the use of hand tools.

E6CC6770DFE60131C4BC68A86D17958E.description: understand the importance of safety, cost, ease of use, and availability in selecting tools and resources for a specific purpose.

E6CCA6B0DFE60131C4BD68A86D17958E.description: explore, use, and process a variety of materials and energy sources to design and construct things.

E6CC2920DFE60131C4BB68A86D17958E.description: Technological tools, materials, and other resources should be selected on the basis of safety, cost, availability, appropriateness, and environmental impact; technological processes change energy, information, and material resources into more useful forms.

E6CB2400DFE60131C4B768A86D17958E.description: discuss how best to test the solution; perform the test under teacher supervision; record and portray results through numerical and graphic means; discuss orally why things worked or didn't work; and summarize results in writing, suggesting ways to make the solution better.

E6CBAB70DFE60131C4B968A86D17958E.description: plan and build, under supervision, a model of the solution using familiar materials, processes, and hand tools.

E6CADA90DFE60131C4B668A86D17958E.description: generate ideas for possible solutions, individually and through group activity; apply age-appropriate mathematics and science skills; evaluate the ideas and determine the best solution; and explain reasons for the choices.

E6CB6B40DFE60131C4B868A86D17958E.description: investigate prior solutions and ideas from books, magazines, family, friends, neighbors, and community members.

E6CA9640DFE60131C4B568A86D17958E.description: describe objects, imaginary or real, that might be modeled or made differently and suggest ways in which the objects can be changed, fixed, or improved.

E6CA3FB0DFE60131C4B468A86D17958E.description: Engineering design is an iterative process involving modeling and optimization used to develop technological solutions to problems within given constraints.

E6C97240DFE60131C4B268A86D17958E.description: Students will apply technological knowledge and skills to design, construct, use, and evaluate products and systems to satisfy human and environmental needs.

document.title: New York State K-8 Social Studies Framework

04CB49705AD146B296DEC76983209D2C.description: Students will examine decisions that people make about spending and saving money.

BD8BC491833748C7A8A6ED1F7B777A70.description: Students will provide examples of scarcity by identifying wants that exceed resources.

0D12402D7E854E5BBC7A905AB68E83BE.description: Scarcity means that people's wants exceed their limited resources.

B235B3B990564F1B9B63F11329689116.description: People have many economic wants and needs, but limited resources with which to obtain them.

ADFE8D664AF74EEF975FA0872F0DFCD2.description: Students will describe the main characters and qualities after listening to biographies and legends.

3A579D656B1F42AAA72A0E8AC394690E.description: Students will interview family members to learn about their family history. Students will develop a family time line as an extension of their personal time line.

D691FCFEA73B4CDC8208E853B50B4765.description: Oral histories, biographies, and family time lines relate family histories.

26E1C4A66CC341CDAC3AC8544424FCF9.description: Students will be exposed to various historical sources, including artifacts, letters, maps, photographs, and newspapers.

6BE07C2D6BC9433AB485548A6504ADB2.description: Various historical sources exist to inform people about life in the past, including artifacts, letters, maps, photographs, and newspapers.

33FD0238EAAD4EEBA24082FC4C86F31B.description: Historical sources reveal information about how life in the past differs from the present.

05E1CC6D105C4036854344BB1A663D92.description: Students will use sequence and chronological terms when describing family events.

188C193CEB784803B21B1B59FCFC22E1.description: Sequence and chronology can be identified in terms of days, weeks, months, years, and seasons when describing family events and histories.

09A25FFCED204463ACFFD429D4AA9136.description: Families of long ago have similarities and differences with families today.

D920D0F7C21C41A3A2339844937EBDB5.description: Students will examine the changes in their family over time and how the family growth and change could be documented and recorded.

497D9731F1C048E89CC516BD6A42566F.description: Families change over time, and family growth and change can be documented and recorded.

165F0FA000BD48F289A8F453AAA33915.description: Students will create personal time lines of their life, school year, and family events with the help of family members. Students will demonstrate an understanding of sequence and chronology and share their time lines with each other.

51355081AC204452AFE6E38F0E611D8E.description: Personal and family history is a source of information for individuals about the people and places around them.

D90D7958542C4634A3C81F00678C7737.description: Families have a past and change over time. There are different types of documents that relate family histories.
comments: NOTE: Teachers will use their professional judgment and demonstrate sensitivity regarding the varied family structures of their students and availability of information.

BB158302D93A4855B0BC20D26A811095.description: Students will identify positive and negative effects that human interaction can have on the physical environment.

9BDF969106F94EAE811067136BDB0AB7.description: People interact with their physical environment in ways that may have a positive or a negative effect.

492CF9FB5238473489664F033CF1D2BC.description: Students will identify how the physical environment of their community has been modified to meet needs and wants.

16D6BCBC00FF4966A44B9CA4EF862F1D.description: Roads, dams, bridges, farms, parks, and dwellings are all examples of how people modify the physical environment to meet needs and wants.

622BE8C883B64FDE829B5ACE454E5337.description: Students will identify natural resources required to meet basic needs.

4A9C5C76BCB14B4C9DC596428242C33E.description: People and communities depend on the physical environment for natural resources.

488C6FFDDB924839B480330285DC819C.description: People and communities depend on and modify their physical environment in order to meet basic needs.

2A6CE5DBDA4A452AA9C323D6FD952558.description: Students will closely read maps making use of the legends to understand symbols and what they represent.

A0739BD0DA9242EA9B58A8A767EA3471.description: Symbols are used to represent physical features and man-made structures on maps and globes.

E93F50C0D4C747ECB490AB70C1527780.description: Students will use a map of the community and provide directions to another student on how to get from the school to another place identified on the map.

41C0CB373D874B209A59B8506DB867D6.description: Maps are used to locate important places in the community, state, and nation such as capitals, monuments, hospitals, museums, schools, and cultural centers.

8EBF9BD62F254304A59A6E36902033B5.description: Students will use cardinal directions within the classroom to describe the location of objects (e.g., desks, bookcases) and create a map of the classroom using symbols to represent objects.

EB1319669A8646629BFF1A799809484E.description: Maps and map tools, such as legends and cardinal directions, can help us navigate from one place to the next, provide directions, or trace important routes.

63969AC9374040B78B0C5177B5BA7F72.description: The location and place of physical features and man-made structures can be described and interpreted using symbols and geographic vocabulary.

8B6506121134497386312A72E82A739F.description: Students will be given opportunities to solve problems, make decisions, and resolve conflicts.

FCA1E6D7BCD14EF6B73EE83DC78E3FAC.description: Children can participate in problem solving, decision making, and conflict resolution within their home, school, and community.

4DC3CEF828F9433F9C720AC495B402FE.description: Students will begin to identify that there are local, state, and national levels of government and will identify some actions that the government takes.

82F2811E91014D95BB3756D510D2ED46.description: Rules and laws are developed to protect people's rights and the safety and welfare of the community.

2522155937724B0EB82650A52CAE2BBD.description: People create governments in order to create peace and establish order. Laws are created to protect the rights and define the responsibilities of individuals and groups.

465EAE8881B34E3D825669C9E6EE3D52.description: Students will discuss ways that they can protect and respect our world and its people.

9AF9AE1D990B4A4EB94E0B6895A2754A.description: As global citizens, we are connected to people and cultures beyond our own community and nation, and we have a shared responsibility to protect and respect our world.

70997EA52A18476B93801A471BB2BA64.description: Students will explain the traits of a responsible citizen and model actions of responsible citizens.

89F5157237AC441F931E29E5337F5990.description: Traits of a responsible citizen include respecting others, behaving honestly, helping others, obeying rules and laws, being informed, and sharing needed resources.
comments: According to the Dignity for All Students Act, "others" include but not limited to people of different races, weights, national origins, ethnic groups, religions, religious practices, mental or physical abilities, sexual orientations, gender identity, and sexes.

83FE670C0F61476D9646E3764EB488BB.description: Students will participate in group activities and contribute to the work of the group.

126967EBB9564D398ACC82DA8E1AEE5B.description: An engaged and active citizen participates in the activities of the group or community and makes positive contributions.

E6AAD57B970246D09C326C40542015C2.description: A citizen is a member of a community or group. Students are citizens of their local and global communities.

46B35747AEE8467E8B872F8BDE3BD390.description: Students will be able to recite the Pledge of Allegiance, to begin to understand its purpose and its general meaning, and to sing patriotic songs such as America the Beautiful, America ("My Country 'Tis of Thee"), and The Star Spangled Banner and begin to understand the general meaning of the lyrics.

78D33845EC7B40428D04CFBDC5FD52A5.description: The Pledge of Allegiance and patriotic songs play an important role in understanding and examining the nation's history, values, and beliefs.

AA7518D16E3345719047FF30C2B9DE0D.description: There are significant individuals, historical events, and symbols that are important to American cultural identity.

F6CBE326F07841F783A9F072F732FF15.description: Students will compare the cultural similarities and differences for various ethnic and cultural groups found in New York State.

B0DC014869254991916912BAF545A9B4.description: Awareness of America's rich diversity fosters intercultural understanding.

A8892322CED341E6944F6031250C8559.description: Students will identify traditions that are associated with their families and tell why the tradition is important.

ECA91985CB574768A95F78672E21C0B2.description: People and families of diverse racial, religious, national, and ethnic groups share their beliefs, customs, and traditions which creates a multicultural community.

C9AD4E2007004EC789C1F2EF3A1C6D4D.description: Students will listen to stories about different families and will identify characteristics that are the same and different.

7A18D4D3CD1C4B54B575D3D1FE2AC16C.description: Families are a basic unit of all societies and different people define family differently.

0B37B219B27242819010C7B580A503CD.description: Language, beliefs, customs, and traditions help shape the identity and culture of a family and a community.

3CB7CC1557664695930634DB3444602E.description: My Family and Other Families, Now and Long Ago

These units represent five of the unifying themes of social studies and may be presented in any order.

890D81754BE445BF832AC32AA945E718.description: Develop the connections of an interdependent community by engaging in the political process as it relates to a local context.

31054EB8ECE04DACB634AA8D114159A7.description: Identify rights and responsibilities within the classroom and school.

3F19DF81DD814B45B0397AAD8AC74BB8.description: Identify the president of the United States and the school principal and their leadership responsibilities.

24E3C902DC794731B5031CFB4AA79C3F.description: Identify situations in which social actions are required.

FA7FF70D4CDE4BF1AADF44A8927B83CF.description: Show respect in issues involving differences and conflict; participate in the resolution of differences and conflict.

B4D48B0533E747D98F82AB5F49AAD404.description: Identify the role of the individual in classroom and school participation.

6EDA0A184B4A4B5FBCBC4C9A87FCC35C.description: Participate in activities that focus on a classroom or school issue or problem.

8AF19BF8DDA240798EB5FD75E4AC37D5.description: Demonstrate respect for the rights of others in discussions regardless of whether one agrees with the other viewpoint.

A21924344A2D47C193EF3E53A9DCD9AB.description: Explain how people earn money and other ways people receive money.

B441014751C14EFF932BBBFFC83E0D8A.description: Distinguish between a consumer and a producer and their relationship to goods and services.

1C2E8F68D6514DD4968644A6100D5FA5.description: Explain how scarcity affects choices made by families and communities and identify costs and benefits associated with these choices.

351E1F8DB3304B8482CB58B0DE0592A2.description: Describe how human activities alter places.

C6F4C8D0C7B84DEF9DFE4332661DA0A4.description: Identify a pattern and a process.

1CC2665A6BFE42B8B8142F56BCD902C0.description: Describe how environment affects his/her and other people's activities.

F43E8402BA4C46C4999E77146785CE34.description: Identify human activities and human-made features; identify natural events or physical features.

24E46A71675F49E3A5376040325C1D72.description: Ask geographic questions about where places are located and why they are located there using geographic representations such as maps and models. Describe where places are in relation to each other.

D9E5E515862B4AAB8790C882837BD492.description: Understand the concepts of geography, economics, and history that apply to his/her family.

358EFCDDB1A84A0E8B231D429A7DBEC5.description: Describe an event in his/her family.

5B4B5F0113624EEAAB5F58D63774B735.description: Identify similarities and/or differences between him/her and others with detail.

23A7993971714363824B373788C6BB5E.description: Identify similarities and differences between neighborhoods.

4AF83F16A2C44890980CEEE00D0D1CFD.description: Recognize and identify patterns of continuity in his/her family.

3527051576E244DFB14659EB7AE4B87C.description: Identify events of the past, present, and future in his/her family life.

53145EEFC57140B29E2AD829F8ACCDE7.description: Identify causes and effects using examples from his/her family life.

C8C393B8314346ED80F36A9CED273AF2.description: Recognize different forms of evidence used to make meaning in social studies (including sources such as art and photographs, artifacts, oral histories, maps, and graphs).

document.title: Learning Standards for Mathematics, Science, and Technology - Standard 4

E4FCBC70DFE60131C23B68A86D17958E.description: identify ways in which humans have changed their environment and the effects of those changes.

E4FBC250DFE60131C23868A86D17958E.description: describe the relationship of the sun as an energy source for living and nonliving cycles.

E4F99850DFE60131C23068A86D17958E.description: The continuity of life is sustained through reproduction and development.

E4F8E460DFE60131C22D68A86D17958E.description: Individual organisms and species change over time.
