They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.

document.title: New York State P-12 Common Core Learning Standards for Mathematics

D7349100DFE60131A89368A86D17958E.description: Describe qualitatively the functional relationship between two quantities by analyzing a graph (e.g., where the function is increasing or decreasing, linear or nonlinear). Sketch a graph that exhibits the qualitative features of a function that has been described verbally.

D7344610DFE60131A89268A86D17958E.description: Construct a function to model a linear relationship between two quantities. Determine the rate of change and initial value of the function from a description of a relationship or from two (x, y) values, including reading these from a table or from a graph. Interpret the rate of change and initial value of a linear function in terms of the situation it models, and in terms of its graph or a table of values.

D7340390DFE60131A89168A86D17958E.description: Use functions to model relationships between quantities.

D733B9D0DFE60131A89068A86D17958E.description: Interpret the equation y = mx + b as defining a linear function, whose graph is a straight line; give examples of functions that are not linear.
comments: For example, the function A = s² giving the area of a square as a function of its side length is not linear because its graph contains the points (1,1), (2,4) and (3,9), which are not on a straight line.

D7337710DFE60131A88F68A86D17958E.description: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions).
comments: For example, given a linear function represented by a table of values and a linear function represented by an algebraic expression, determine which function has the greater rate of change.

D7333430DFE60131A88E68A86D17958E.description: Understand that a function is a rule that assigns to each input exactly one output. The graph of a function is the set of ordered pairs consisting of an input and the corresponding output.
comments: Function notation is not required in Grade 8.

D7325120DFE60131A88B68A86D17958E.description: Understand that patterns of association can also be seen in bivariate categorical data by displaying frequencies and relative frequencies in a two-way table. Construct and interpret a two-way table summarizing data on two categorical variables collected from the same subjects. Use relative frequencies calculated for rows or columns to describe possible association between the two variables.
comments: For example, collect data from students in your class on whether or not they have a curfew on school nights and whether or not they have assigned chores at home. Is there evidence that those who have a curfew also tend to have chores?

D731FD40DFE60131A88A68A86D17958E.description: Use the equation of a linear model to solve problems in the context of bivariate measurement data, interpreting the slope and intercept.
comments: For example, in a linear model for a biology experiment, interpret a slope of 1.5 cm/hr as meaning that an additional hour of sunlight each day is associated with an additional 1.5 cm in mature plant height.

D731ACA0DFE60131A88968A86D17958E.description: Know that straight lines are widely used to model relationships between two quantitative variables. For scatter plots that suggest a linear association, informally fit a straight line, and informally assess the model fit by judging the closeness of the data points to the line.

D7315980DFE60131A88868A86D17958E.description: Construct and interpret scatter plots for bivariate measurement data to investigate patterns of association between two quantities. Describe patterns such as clustering, outliers, positive or negative association, linear association, and nonlinear association.

D7310A30DFE60131A88768A86D17958E.description: Investigate patterns of association in bivariate data.

D7307A90DFE60131A88568A86D17958E.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems leading to two linear equations in two variables.
comments: For example, given coordinates for two pairs of points, determine whether the line through the first pair of points intersects the line through the second pair.

D7303700DFE60131A88468A86D17958E.description: Solve systems of two linear equations in two variables algebraically, and estimate solutions by graphing the equations. Solve simple cases by inspection.
comments: For example, 3x + 2y = 5 and 3x + 2y = 6 have no solution because 3x + 2y cannot simultaneously be 5 and 6.

D72FF170DFE60131A88368A86D17958E.description: Understand that solutions to a system of two linear equations in two variables correspond to points of intersection of their graphs, because points of intersection satisfy both equations simultaneously.

D72FA060DFE60131A88268A86D17958E.description: Analyze and solve pairs of simultaneous linear equations.

D72F3CB0DFE60131A88168A86D17958E.description: Solve linear equations with rational number coefficients, including equations whose solutions require expanding expressions using the distributive property and collecting like terms.

D72EEC40DFE60131A88068A86D17958E.description: Give examples of linear equations in one variable with one solution, infinitely many solutions, or no solutions. Show which of these possibilities is the case by successively transforming the given equation into simpler forms, until an equivalent equation of the form x = a, a = a, or a = b results (where a and b are different numbers).

D72EA7B0DFE60131A87F68A86D17958E.description: Solve linear equations in one variable.

D72E6660DFE60131A87E68A86D17958E.description: Analyze and solve linear equations and pairs of simultaneous linear equations.

D72E24C0DFE60131A87D68A86D17958E.description: Use similar triangles to explain why the slope m is the same between any two distinct points on a non-vertical line in the coordinate plane; derive the equation y = mx for a line through the origin and the equation y = mx + b for a line intercepting the vertical axis at b.

D72DE070DFE60131A87C68A86D17958E.description: Graph proportional relationships, interpreting the unit rate as the slope of the graph. Compare two different proportional relationships represented in different ways.
comments: For example, compare a distance-time graph to a distance-time equation to determine which of two moving objects has greater speed.

D72D9860DFE60131A87B68A86D17958E.description: Understand the connections between proportional relationships, lines, and linear equations.

D72D41A0DFE60131A87A68A86D17958E.description: Perform operations with numbers expressed in scientific notation, including problems where both decimal and scientific notation are used. Use scientific notation and choose units of appropriate size for measurements of very large or very small quantities (e.g., use millimeters per year for seafloor spreading). Interpret scientific notation that has been generated by technology.

D72CEA90DFE60131A87968A86D17958E.description: Use numbers expressed in the form of a single digit times an integer power of 10 to estimate very large or very small quantities, and to express how many times as much one is than the other.
comments: For example, estimate the population of the United States as 3 × 10<sup>8</sup> and the population of the world as 7 × 10<sup>9</sup>, and determine that the world population is more than 20 times larger.

D72C93E0DFE60131A87868A86D17958E.description: Use square root and cube root symbols to represent solutions to equations of the form x² = p and x³ = p, where p is a positive rational number. Evaluate square roots of small perfect squares and cube roots of small perfect cubes. Know that √2 is irrational.

D72C4220DFE60131A87768A86D17958E.description: Know and apply the properties of integer exponents to generate equivalent numerical expressions.
comments: For example, 3² × 3<sup>-5</sup> = 3<sup>-3</sup> = 1/3³ = 1/27.

D72BFD30DFE60131A87668A86D17958E.description: Work with radicals and integer exponents.

D72B65C0DFE60131A87468A86D17958E.description: Use rational approximations of irrational numbers to compare the size of irrational numbers, locate them approximately on a number line diagram, and estimate the value of expressions (e.g., π²).
comments: For example, by truncating the decimal expansion of √2, show that √2 is between 1 and 2, then between 1.4 and 1.5, and explain how to continue on to get better approximations.

D72B22F0DFE60131A87368A86D17958E.description: Know that numbers that are not rational are called irrational. Understand informally that every number has a decimal expansion; for rational numbers show that the decimal expansion repeats eventually, and convert a decimal expansion which repeats eventually into a rational number.

D72AE0F0DFE60131A87268A86D17958E.description: Know that there are numbers that are not rational, and approximate them by rational numbers.

D72A5450DFE60131A87068A86D17958E.description: Know the formulas for the volumes of cones, cylinders, and spheres and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

D729F150DFE60131A86F68A86D17958E.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving volume of cylinders, cones, and spheres.

D729A150DFE60131A86E68A86D17958E.description: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to find the distance between two points in a coordinate system.

D72961E0DFE60131A86D68A86D17958E.description: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to determine unknown side lengths in right triangles in real-world and mathematical problems in two and three dimensions.

D7292340DFE60131A86C68A86D17958E.description: Explain a proof of the Pythagorean Theorem and its converse.

D728E270DFE60131A86B68A86D17958E.description: Understand and apply the Pythagorean Theorem.

D7289E30DFE60131A86A68A86D17958E.description: Use informal arguments to establish facts about the angle sum and exterior angle of triangles, about the angles created when parallel lines are cut by a transversal, and the angle-angle criterion for similarity of triangles.
comments: For example, arrange three copies of the same triangle so that the sum of the three angles appears to form a line, and give an argument in terms of transversals why this is so.

D72854E0DFE60131A86968A86D17958E.description: Understand that a two-dimensional figure is similar to another if the second can be obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections, translations, and dilations; given two similar two-dimensional figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the similarity between them.

D7280590DFE60131A86868A86D17958E.description: Describe the effect of dilations, translations, rotations, and reflections on two-dimensional figures using coordinates.

D727BE20DFE60131A86768A86D17958E.description: Understand that a two-dimensional figure is congruent to another if the second can be obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections, and translations; given two congruent figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the congruence between them.

D72769A0DFE60131A86668A86D17958E.description: Parallel lines are taken to parallel lines.

D72724A0DFE60131A86568A86D17958E.description: Angles are taken to angles of the same measure.

D726DDF0DFE60131A86468A86D17958E.description: Lines are taken to lines, and line segments to line segments of the same length.

D7269620DFE60131A86368A86D17958E.description: Verify experimentally the properties of rotations, reflections, and translations:

D72649F0DFE60131A86268A86D17958E.description: Understand congruence and similarity using physical models, transparencies, or geometry software.

D725B760DFE60131A86068A86D17958E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.
comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.

D7255800DFE60131A85F68A86D17958E.description: Look for and make use of structure.
comments: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.

Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

D723C890DFE60131A85B68A86D17958E.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.
comments: Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.

Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

D7232DC0DFE60131A85968A86D17958E.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
comments: Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.

document.title: New York State P-12 Common Core Learning Standards for English Language Arts & Literacy

DB978B70DFE60131B05768A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal contrast, addition, and other logical relationships (e.g., however, although, nevertheless, similarly, moreover, in addition).

DB973250DFE60131B05668A86D17958E.description: Use the relationship between particular words (e.g., synonyms, antonyms, homographs) to better understand each of the words.

DB96D6D0DFE60131B05568A86D17958E.description: Recognize and explain the meaning of common idioms, adages, and proverbs.

DB968BB0DFE60131B05468A86D17958E.description: Interpret figurative language, including similes and metaphors, in context.

DB963210DFE60131B05368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

DB95DE30DFE60131B05268A86D17958E.description: Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation and determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.

DB959540DFE60131B05168A86D17958E.description: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek and Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., photograph, photosynthesis).

DB954BA0DFE60131B05068A86D17958E.description: Use context (e.g., cause/effect relationships and comparisons in text) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

DB950030DFE60131B04F68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 5 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

DB945330DFE60131B04D68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the varieties of English (e.g., dialects, registers) used in stories, dramas, or poems.

DB93FD00DFE60131B04C68A86D17958E.description: Expand, combine, and reduce sentences for meaning, reader/listener interest, and style.

DB93A720DFE60131B04B68A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

DB931020DFE60131B04968A86D17958E.description: Spell grade-appropriate words correctly, consulting references as needed.

DB92C0E0DFE60131B04868A86D17958E.description: Use underlining, quotation marks, or italics to indicate titles of works.

DB926630DFE60131B04768A86D17958E.description: Use a comma to set off the words yes and no (e.g., Yes, thank you), to set off a tag question from the rest of the sentence (e.g., It's true, isn't it?), and to indicate direct address (e.g., Is that you, Steve?).

DB921B60DFE60131B04668A86D17958E.description: Use a comma to separate an introductory element from the rest of the sentence.

DB91CD70DFE60131B04568A86D17958E.description: Use punctuation to separate items in a series.

DB917260DFE60131B04468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

DB90A830DFE60131B04268A86D17958E.description: Recognize and correct inappropriate shifts in verb tense.

DB905E70DFE60131B04168A86D17958E.description: Use verb tense to convey various times, sequences, states, and conditions.

DB901430DFE60131B04068A86D17958E.description: Form and use the perfect (e.g., I had walked; I have walked; I will have walked) verb tenses.

DB8FC8A0DFE60131B03F68A86D17958E.description: Explain the function of conjunctions, prepositions, and interjections in general and their function in particular sentences.

DB8F77E0DFE60131B03E68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

DB8E5D90DFE60131B03B68A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

DB8E1430DFE60131B03A68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

DB8DC8B0DFE60131B03968A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

DB8D2970DFE60131B03768A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

DB8C9140DFE60131B03568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

DB8C42A0DFE60131B03468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

DB8B5780DFE60131B03268A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

DB8B0C40DFE60131B03168A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, using formal English when appropriate to task and situation.

DB8ABF70DFE60131B03068A86D17958E.description: Include multimedia components (e.g., graphics, sound) and visual displays in presentations when appropriate to enhance the development of main ideas or themes.

DB8A6EB0DFE60131B02F68A86D17958E.description: Report on a topic or text or present an opinion, sequencing ideas logically and using appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details to support main ideas or themes; speak clearly at an understandable pace.

DB89D460DFE60131B02D68A86D17958E.description: Summarize the points a speaker makes and explain how each claim is supported by reasons and evidence.

DB897940DFE60131B02C68A86D17958E.description: Summarize a written text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

DB8920B0DFE60131B02B68A86D17958E.description: Use their experience and their knowledge of language and logic, as well as culture, to think analytically, address problems creatively, and advocate persuasively.

DB88C960DFE60131B02A68A86D17958E.description: Seek to understand and communicate with individuals from different perspectives and cultural backgrounds.

DB887DF0DFE60131B02968A86D17958E.description: Review the key ideas expressed and draw conclusions in light of information and knowledge gained from the discussions.

DB882B00DFE60131B02868A86D17958E.description: Pose and respond to specific questions by making comments that contribute to the discussion and elaborate on the remarks of others.

DB87D060DFE60131B02768A86D17958E.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions and carry out assigned roles.

DB877360DFE60131B02668A86D17958E.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation and other information known about the topic to explore ideas under discussion.

DB871A50DFE60131B02568A86D17958E.description: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 5 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.

DB8600C0DFE60131B02268A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

DB85B150DFE60131B02168A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

DB856570DFE60131B02068A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

DB84C810DFE60131B01E68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

DB847AD0DFE60131B01D68A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

DB842210DFE60131B01C68A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

DB839380DFE60131B01A68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

DB834A90DFE60131B01968A86D17958E.description: Recognize and illustrate social, historical, and cultural features in the presentation of literary texts.

DB82FEC0DFE60131B01868A86D17958E.description: Create and present an original poem, narrative, play, art work, or literary critique in response to a particular author or theme studied in class.

DB8245C0DFE60131B01668A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

DB8198B0DFE60131B01468A86D17958E.description: Apply grade 5 Reading standards to informational texts (e.g., "Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text, identifying which reasons and evidence support which point[s]").

DB813DE0DFE60131B01368A86D17958E.description: Apply grade 5 Reading standards to literature (e.g., "Compare and contrast two or more characters, settings, or events in a story or a drama, drawing on specific details in the text [e.g., how characters interact]").

DB80ECC0DFE60131B01268A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

DB809020DFE60131B01168A86D17958E.description: Recall relevant information from experiences or gather relevant information from print and digital sources; summarize or paraphrase information in notes and finished work, and provide a list of sources.

DB803560DFE60131B01068A86D17958E.description: Conduct short research projects that use several sources to build knowledge through investigation of different aspects of a topic.

DB7FC7E0DFE60131B00F68A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

DB7F7D90DFE60131B00E68A86D17958E.description: With some guidance and support from adults, use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing as well as to interact and collaborate with others; demonstrate sufficient command of keyboarding skills to type a minimum of two pages in a single sitting.

DB7F3090DFE60131B00D68A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

DB7ED750DFE60131B00C68A86D17958E.description: Produce text (print or nonprint) that explores a variety of cultures and perspectives.

DB7E8920DFE60131B00B68A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.
comments: (Grade-specific expectations for writing types are defined in standards 1—3 above.)

DB7DF640DFE60131B00968A86D17958E.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from the narrated experiences or events.

DB7DA8D0DFE60131B00868A86D17958E.description: Use concrete words and phrases and sensory details to convey experiences and events precisely.

DB7D5300DFE60131B00768A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of transitional words, phrases, and clauses to manage the sequence of events.

DB7CE9D0DFE60131B00668A86D17958E.description: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, description, and pacing, to develop experiences and events or show the responses of characters to situations.

DB7C95C0DFE60131B00568A86D17958E.description: Orient the reader by establishing a situation and introducing a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally.

DB7C4CC0DFE60131B00468A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, descriptive details, and clear event sequences.

document.title: Learning Standards for Mathematics, Science, and Technology - Standard 4

E52F2F30DFE60131C29068A86D17958E.description: explain how individual choices and societal actions can contribute to improving the environment.

E52EE3D0DFE60131C28F68A86D17958E.description: explain the impact of technological development and growth in the human population on the living and nonliving environment.

E52E9570DFE60131C28E68A86D17958E.description: describe the range of interrelationships of humans with the living and nonliving environment.

E52E4DE0DFE60131C28D68A86D17958E.description: Human decisions and activities have had a profound impact on the physical and living environment.

E52DAD70DFE60131C28B68A86D17958E.description: explain how the living and nonliving environments change over time and respond to disturbances.

E52D6CC0DFE60131C28A68A86D17958E.description: explain the importance of preserving diversity of species and habitats.

E52DF0C0DFE60131C28C68A86D17958E.description: explain factors that limit growth of individuals and populations.

E52D3120DFE60131C28968A86D17958E.description: Plants and animals depend on each other and their physical environment.

E52C7790DFE60131C28668A86D17958E.description: relate processes at the system level to the cellular level in order to explain dynamic equilibrium in multi-celled organisms.

E52CF4B0DFE60131C28868A86D17958E.description: explain disease as a failure of homeostasis.

E52CB710DFE60131C28768A86D17958E.description: explain the basic biochemical processes in living organisms and their importance in maintaining dynamic equilibrium.

E52C2D10DFE60131C28568A86D17958E.description: Organisms maintain a dynamic equilibrium that sustains life.

E52BEE30DFE60131C28468A86D17958E.description: explain how organisms, including humans, reproduce their own kind.

E52BB1C0DFE60131C28368A86D17958E.description: The continuity of life is sustained through reproduction and development.

E52B7490DFE60131C28268A86D17958E.description: explain the mechanisms and patterns of evolution.

E52B3600DFE60131C28168A86D17958E.description: Individual organisms and species change over time.

E52AF4B0DFE60131C28068A86D17958E.description: explain how the technology of genetic engineering allows humans to alter the genetic makeup of organisms.

E52AAD60DFE60131C27F68A86D17958E.description: explain how the structure and replication of genetic material result in offspring that resemble their parents.

E52A5810DFE60131C27E68A86D17958E.description: Organisms inherit genetic information in a variety of ways that result in continuity of structure and function between parents and offspring.

E529D9B0DFE60131C27C68A86D17958E.description: explain how a one-celled organism is able to function despite lacking the levels of organization present in more complex organisms.

E52997F0DFE60131C27B68A86D17958E.description: describe and explain the structures and functions of the human body at different organizational levels (e.g., systems, tissues, cells, organelles).

E52A18B0DFE60131C27D68A86D17958E.description: explain how diversity of populations within ecosystems relates to the stability of ecosystems.

E5295530DFE60131C27A68A86D17958E.description: Living things are both similar to and different from each other and nonliving things.

E5345B70DFE60131C2A368A86D17958E.description: compare energy relationships within an atom's nucleus to those outside the nucleus.

E5349B10DFE60131C2A468A86D17958E.description: explain chemical bonding in terms of the motion of electrons.

E534D8B0DFE60131C2A568A86D17958E.description: explain and predict different patterns of motion of objects (e.g., linear and angular motion, velocity and acceleration, momentum and inertia).

E5341AC0DFE60131C2A268A86D17958E.description: Energy and matter interact through forces that result in changes in motion.

E533D4A0DFE60131C2A168A86D17958E.description: explain the uses and hazards of radioactivity.

E5332EA0DFE60131C29F68A86D17958E.description: explain variations in wavelength and frequency in terms of the source of the vibrations that produce them, e.g., molecules, electrons, and nuclear particles.

E532EF90DFE60131C29E68A86D17958E.description: explain heat in terms of kinetic molecular theory.

E5337C50DFE60131C2A068A86D17958E.description: observe and describe transmission of various forms of energy.

E532AF50DFE60131C29D68A86D17958E.description: Energy exists in many forms, and when these forms change energy is conserved.

E53229E0DFE60131C29B68A86D17958E.description: use kinetic molecular theory to explain rates of reactions and the relationships among temperature, pressure, and volume of a substance.

E5326C80DFE60131C29C68A86D17958E.description: apply the principle of conservation of mass to chemical reactions.

E531E540DFE60131C29A68A86D17958E.description: use atomic and molecular models to explain common chemical reactions.

E5319610DFE60131C29968A86D17958E.description: explain the properties of materials in terms of the arrangement and properties of the atoms that compose them.

E5315810DFE60131C29868A86D17958E.description: Matter is made up of particles whose properties determine the observable characteristics of matter and its reactivity.

E530D6E0DFE60131C29668A86D17958E.description: explain how incoming solar radiations, ocean currents, and land masses affect weather and climate.

E5311860DFE60131C29768A86D17958E.description: use the concepts of density and heat energy to explain observations of weather patterns, seasonal changes, and the movements of the Earth's plates.

E5309980DFE60131C29568A86D17958E.description: Many of the phenomena that we observe on Earth involve interactions among components of air, water, and land.

E5300A60DFE60131C29368A86D17958E.description: describe current theories about the origin of the universe and solar system.

E53058C0DFE60131C29468A86D17958E.description: explain complex phenomena, such as tides, variations in day length, solar insolation, apparent motion of the planets, and annual traverse of the constellations.

E52FC290DFE60131C29268A86D17958E.description: The Earth and celestial phenomena can be described by principles of relative motion and perspective.

E528C580DFE60131C27868A86D17958E.description: Students will understand and apply scientific concepts, principles, and theories pertaining to the physical setting and living environment and recognize the historical development of ideas in science.

Observe the rules of punctuation, capitalization, and spelling
  • punctuation of simple and compound sentences, dialogue, titles of articles
  • capitalization of words such as proper adjectives, titles of persons, and words in quotes
  • spelling of commonly misspelled words, homonyms, content-area vocabulary

E39CACD0DFE60131BF7168A86D17958E.description: Use the writing process (e.g., prewriting, drafting, revising, proofreading, and editing)

E39C4890DFE60131BF7068A86D17958E.description: Use prewriting activities (e.g., brainstorming, freewriting, note taking, outlining, and paragraphing)

E39BDFF0DFE60131BF6F68A86D17958E.description: Use tone and language appropriate to the audience and purpose

E39B3B30DFE60131BF6D68A86D17958E.description: Understand the purpose for writing; the purpose may be to explain, describe, narrate, persuade, or express feelings

E39A6980DFE60131BF6A68A86D17958E.description: Recognize the types of language (e.g., informal vocabulary, culture-specific terminology, jargon, colloquialisms, and email conventions) that are appropriate to social communication

E39A2000DFE60131BF6968A86D17958E.description: Consider the age, gender, social position, and cultural traditions of the writer

E399D100DFE60131BF6868A86D17958E.description: Share reading experiences with a peer or adult; for example, read together silently or aloud, or discuss reactions to texts

E3997F10DFE60131BF6768A86D17958E.description: Students will read, write, listen, and speak for social interaction.

E3993580DFE60131BF6668A86D17958E.description: Make judgments about the quality of literary texts and performances by applying personal and academic criteria, such as that found in literary criticism

E398ED00DFE60131BF6568A86D17958E.description: Select, reject, and reconcile ideas and information in light of beliefs

E398A560DFE60131BF6468A86D17958E.description: Form opinions and make judgments about literary works, by analyzing and evaluating texts from more than one critical perspective, such as cultural and historical

E3985B40DFE60131BF6368A86D17958E.description:
Analyze and evaluate fiction, including
  • the background in which the text is written
  • the effect created by the author's tone or mood

E3980F50DFE60131BF6268A86D17958E.description: Evaluate poetry to recognize the use and effect of verse form

E397C220DFE60131BF6168A86D17958E.description:
Analyze and evaluate poetry in order to recognize the use and effect of
  • sensory imagery
  • figurative language
  • verse form

E3977810DFE60131BF6068A86D17958E.description:
Analyze and evaluate nonfiction texts, including
  • determine the writer's perspectives, purposes, and intended audiences
  • determine the reliability and significance of information
  • recognize the format and its significance to content

E3972510DFE60131BF5F68A86D17958E.description: Generate a list of significant questions to assist with analysis of text

E396D190DFE60131BF5E68A86D17958E.description: Form opinions and make judgments about the validity of persuasive texts

E3966880DFE60131BF5D68A86D17958E.description: Students will read, write, listen, and speak for critical analysis and evaluation.

E395EBC0DFE60131BF5C68A86D17958E.description: Recognize relevance of literature to contemporary and/or personal events and situations

E395A260DFE60131BF5B68A86D17958E.description: Interpret multiple levels of meaning and subtleties in text

E39555D0DFE60131BF5A68A86D17958E.description: Interpret literary texts on the basis of an understanding of the genre and the literary period

E394FAE0DFE60131BF5968A86D17958E.description: Read literary texts aloud to convey an interpretation of the work

E394B260DFE60131BF5868A86D17958E.description: Compare a film, video, or stage version of a literary work with the written version

E3946360DFE60131BF5768A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between different forms of poetry, such as sonnet, lyric, elegy, narrative, epic, and ode, and recognize how the author uses poetic form to convey message or intent

E3940C10DFE60131BF5668A86D17958E.description: Recognize how authors use tone to express their ideas or an attitude toward the subject matter or the audience

E393BE70DFE60131BF5568A86D17958E.description: Read literary criticism to increase comprehension and appreciation of literary texts, with assistance

E3936940DFE60131BF5468A86D17958E.description: Read, view, and respond independently to literary works that represent a range of social, historical, and cultural perspectives

E3931BC0DFE60131BF5368A86D17958E.description:
Read, view, and interpret texts and performances in every medium (e.g., short stories, novels, plays, film and video productions, poems, and essays) from a wide variety of authors, subjects, and genres
  • build background by activating prior knowledge through questioning what they already know about the form in which the story is presented and the period in which it was written

E392CE30DFE60131BF5268A86D17958E.description: Students will read, write, listen, and speak for literary response and expression.

E3927750DFE60131BF5168A86D17958E.description:
Analyze information from different sources, making connections and showing relationships to other texts, ideas, and subjects
  • employ a range of post-reading practices to think about new learning and plan further learning

E3916DD0DFE60131BF4E68A86D17958E.description: Identify and evaluate the reliability and validity of informational sources

E3911EC0DFE60131BF4D68A86D17958E.description:
Skim texts to gain an overall impression and scan texts for particular information
  • focus on key words/phrases to generate questions

E390C3E0DFE60131BF4C68A86D17958E.description:
Read and follow written directions and procedures to solve problems and accomplish tasks
  • use workplace documents

E3904CA0DFE60131BF4B68A86D17958E.description: Use specialized reference sources, such as glossaries, directories, and abstracts

E38FF830DFE60131BF4A68A86D17958E.description:
Locate and use school and public library resources for information and research
  • set purpose for reading by asking questions about what they need to know for their research

E38FB1C0DFE60131BF4968A86D17958E.description: Students will read, write, listen, and speak for information and understanding.

E38F2600DFE60131BF4768A86D17958E.description: Maintain a personal reading list to reflect reading accomplishments

E38EDD30DFE60131BF4668A86D17958E.description: Identify opportunities for improvement of reading comprehension skills; for example, exposure to seek a wider range of writers, topics, and styles

E38E8880DFE60131BF4568A86D17958E.description: Use strategies such as discussing with others, reading guides and summaries, and reading aloud to assist in comprehension

E38E38E0DFE60131BF4468A86D17958E.description: Recognize the organizational format, such as hierarchical, chronological, and cause/effect

E38DE840DFE60131BF4368A86D17958E.description: Identify transitional words or phrases that make text cohesive (e.g., finally, in addition, and in contrast)

E38D9F70DFE60131BF4268A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of punctuation to assist in comprehension

E38D54A0DFE60131BF4168A86D17958E.description: Follow the logic of compound/complex sentence structure

E38D0A80DFE60131BF4068A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between dictionary meaning and implied meaning of the writer's words

E38CA400DFE60131BF3F68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of unfamiliar words by using classroom and other resources

E38C36C0DFE60131BF3E68A86D17958E.description: Adjust the reading rate according to the purpose for reading

document.title: Learning Standards for Mathematics, Science, and Technology - Standard 5

E6ED6DD0DFE60131C4FF68A86D17958E.description: assume leadership responsibilities within a structured group activity.

E6ED26D0DFE60131C4FE68A86D17958E.description: provide examples of products that are well (and poorly) designed and made, describe their positive and negative attributes, and suggest measures that can be implemented to monitor quality during production.

E6ECD3B0DFE60131C4FD68A86D17958E.description: manage time and financial resources in a technological project.

E6EC8D70DFE60131C4FC68A86D17958E.description: Project management is essential to ensuring that technological endeavors are profitable and that products and systems are of high quality and built safely, on schedule, and within budget.

E6EC1180DFE60131C4FA68A86D17958E.description: describe through examples how modern technology reduces manufacturing and construction costs and produces more uniform products.

E6EBCBD0DFE60131C4F968A86D17958E.description: describe how outputs of a technological system can be desired, undesired, expected, or unexpected.

E6EB7D30DFE60131C4F868A86D17958E.description: Technology can have positive and negative impacts on individuals, society, and the environment and humans have the capability and responsibility to constrain or promote technological development.

E6EA9F50DFE60131C4F568A86D17958E.description: describe how new technologies have evolved as a result of combining existing technologies (e.g., photography combined optics and chemistry; the airplane combined kite and glider technology with a lightweight gasoline engine).

E6EA4470DFE60131C4F468A86D17958E.description: understand the contributions of people of different genders, races, and ethnic groups to technological development.

E6EAE5B0DFE60131C4F668A86D17958E.description: describe how the evolution of technology led to the shift in society from an agricultural base to an industrial base to an information base.

E6EA0250DFE60131C4F368A86D17958E.description: Technology has been the driving force in the evolution of society from an agricultural to an industrial to an information base.

E6E926C0DFE60131C4F068A86D17958E.description: describe how system control requires sensing information, processing it, and making changes.

E6E97AB0DFE60131C4F168A86D17958E.description: describe how subsystems and system elements (inputs, processes, outputs) interact within systems.

E6E8DAB0DFE60131C4EF68A86D17958E.description: assemble, operate, and explain the operation of simple open- and closed-loop electrical, electronic, mechanical, and pneumatic systems.

E6E88D90DFE60131C4EE68A86D17958E.description: select appropriate technological systems on the basis of safety, function, cost, ease of operation, and quality of post-purchase support.

E6E83BD0DFE60131C4ED68A86D17958E.description: Technological systems are designed to achieve specific results and produce outputs, such as products, structures, services, energy, or other systems.

E6E7A2B0DFE60131C4EB68A86D17958E.description: use a computer system to monitor and control external events and/or systems.

E6E74980DFE60131C4EA68A86D17958E.description: use a computer as a modeling tool.

E6E707C0DFE60131C4E968A86D17958E.description: use computer hardware and software to draw and dimension prototypical designs.

E6E6CAD0DFE60131C4E868A86D17958E.description: use a computer system to connect to and access needed information from various Internet sites.

E6E68890DFE60131C4E768A86D17958E.description: assemble a computer system including keyboard, central processing unit and disc drives, mouse, modem, printer, and monitor.

E6E647F0DFE60131C4E668A86D17958E.description: Computers, as tools for design, modeling, information processing, communication, and system control, have greatly increased human productivity and knowledge.

E6E5C8A0DFE60131C4E468A86D17958E.description: process energy into other forms and information into more meaningful information.

E6E53830DFE60131C4E268A86D17958E.description: combine manufacturing processes with other technological processes to produce, market, and distribute a product.

E6E4F9E0DFE60131C4E168A86D17958E.description: use a variety of hand tools and machines to change materials into new forms through forming, separating, and combining processes, and processes which cause internal change to occur.

E6E57760DFE60131C4E368A86D17958E.description: choose and use resources for a particular purpose based upon an analysis and understanding of their properties, costs, availability, and environmental impact.

E6E4BC70DFE60131C4E068A86D17958E.description: Technological tools, materials, and other resources should be selected on the basis of safety, cost, availability, appropriateness, and environmental impact; technological processes change energy, information, and material resources into more useful forms.

E6E3F710DFE60131C4DD68A86D17958E.description: in a group setting, test their solution against design specifications, present and evaluate results, describe how the solution might have been modified for different or better results, and discuss tradeoffs that might have to be made.

E6E39EE0DFE60131C4DC68A86D17958E.description: develop plans, including drawings with measurements and details of construction, and construct a model of the solution, exhibiting a degree of craftsmanship.

E6E315C0DFE60131C4DA68A86D17958E.description: consider constraints and generate several ideas for alternative solutions, using group and individual ideation techniques (group discussion, brainstorming, forced connections, role play); defer judgment until a number of ideas have been generated; evaluate (critique) ideas; and explain why the chosen solution is optimal.

E6E43E80DFE60131C4DE68A86D17958E.description: locate and utilize a range of printed, electronic, and human information resources to obtain ideas.

E6E35BA0DFE60131C4DB68A86D17958E.description: identify needs and opportunities for technical solutions from an investigation of situations of general or social interest.

E6E2D160DFE60131C4D968A86D17958E.description: Engineering design is an iterative process involving modeling and optimization used to develop technological solutions to problems within given constraints.

E6E23CF0DFE60131C4D768A86D17958E.description: Students will apply technological knowledge and skills to design, construct, use, and evaluate products and systems to satisfy human and environmental needs.

document.title: New York State P-12 Common Core Learning Standards for Mathematics

D6964890DFE60131A78768A86D17958E.description: Compare two decimals to hundredths by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two decimals refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual model.

D695F6F0DFE60131A78668A86D17958E.description: Use decimal notation for fractions with denominators 10 or 100.
comments: For example, rewrite 0.62 as 62/100; describe a length as 0.62 meters; locate 0.62 on a number line diagram.

D6958F00DFE60131A78568A86D17958E.description: Express a fraction with denominator 10 as an equivalent fraction with denominator 100, and use this technique to add two fractions with respective denominators 10 and 100.
comments: Students who can generate equivalent fractions can develop strategies for adding fractions with unlike denominators in general. But addition and subtraction with unlike denominators in general is not a requirement at this grade.
For example, express 3/10 as 30/100, and add 3/10 + 4/100 = 34/100.

D6954280DFE60131A78468A86D17958E.description: Understand decimal notation for fractions, and compare decimal fractions.

D694EE20DFE60131A78368A86D17958E.description: Solve word problems involving multiplication of a fraction by a whole number, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.
comments: For example, if each person at a party will eat 3/8 of a pound of roast beef, and there will be 5 people at the party, how many pounds of roast beef will be needed? Between what two whole numbers does your answer lie?

D694ADE0DFE60131A78268A86D17958E.description: Understand a multiple of a/b as a multiple of 1/b, and use this understanding to multiply a fraction by a whole number.
comments: For example, use a visual fraction model to express 3 × (2/5) as 6 × (1/5), recognizing this product as 6/5. (In general, n × (a/b) = (n × a)/b.)

D6946900DFE60131A78168A86D17958E.description: Understand a fraction a/b as a multiple of 1/b.
comments: For example, use a visual fraction model to represent 5/4 as the product 5 × (1/4), recording the conclusion by the equation 5/4 = 5 × (1/4).

D69423E0DFE60131A78068A86D17958E.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction by a whole number.

D693DC60DFE60131A77F68A86D17958E.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole and having like denominators, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.

D6939890DFE60131A77E68A86D17958E.description: Add and subtract mixed numbers with like denominators, e.g., by replacing each mixed number with an equivalent fraction, and/or by using properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction.

D6934F10DFE60131A77D68A86D17958E.description: Decompose a fraction into a sum of fractions with the same denominator in more than one way, recording each decomposition by an equation. Justify decompositions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

D692FA70DFE60131A77C68A86D17958E.description: Understand addition and subtraction of fractions as joining and separating parts referring to the same whole.

D692B9A0DFE60131A77B68A86D17958E.description: Understand a fraction a/b with a > 1 as a sum of fractions 1/b.

D6927860DFE60131A77A68A86D17958E.description: Build fractions from unit fractions by applying and extending previous understandings of operations on whole numbers.

D6923540DFE60131A77968A86D17958E.description: Compare two fractions with different numerators and different denominators, e.g., by creating common denominators or numerators, or by comparing to a benchmark fraction such as 1/2. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

D691EEE0DFE60131A77868A86D17958E.description: Explain why a fraction a/b is equivalent to a fraction (n × a)/(n × b) by using visual fraction models, with attention to how the number and size of the parts differ even though the two fractions themselves are the same size. Use this principle to recognize and generate equivalent fractions.

D6919380DFE60131A77768A86D17958E.description: Extend understanding of fraction equivalence and ordering.

comments: Grade 3 expectations in this domain are limited to fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8.
Grade 4 expectations in this domain are limited to fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 100

D690F030DFE60131A77568A86D17958E.description: Recognize a line of symmetry for a two-dimensional figure as a line across the figure such that the figure can be folded along the line into matching parts. Identify line-symmetric figures and draw lines of symmetry.

D6909E10DFE60131A77468A86D17958E.description: Classify two-dimensional figures based on the presence or absence of parallel or perpendicular lines, or the presence or absence of angles of a specified size. Recognize right triangles as a category, and identify right triangles.

D69058C0DFE60131A77368A86D17958E.description: Draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines. Identify these in two-dimensional figures.

D69001E0DFE60131A77268A86D17958E.description: Draw and identify lines and angles, and classify shapes by properties of their lines and angles.

D68F6B50DFE60131A77068A86D17958E.description: Recognize angle measure as additive. When an angle is decomposed into non-overlapping parts, the angle measure of the whole is the sum of the angle measures of the parts. Solve addition and subtraction problems to find unknown angles on a diagram in real world and mathematical problems, e.g., by using an equation with a symbol for the unknown angle measure.

D68F2900DFE60131A76F68A86D17958E.description: Measure angles in whole-number degrees using a protractor. Sketch angles of specified measure.

D68EE420DFE60131A76E68A86D17958E.description: An angle that turns through n one-degree angles is said to have an angle measure of n degrees.

D68E9FD0DFE60131A76D68A86D17958E.description: An angle is measured with reference to a circle with its center at the common endpoint of the rays, by considering the fraction of the circular arc between the points where the two rays intersect the circle. An angle that turns through 1/360 of a circle is called a "one-degree angle," and can be used to measure angles.

D68E4FB0DFE60131A76C68A86D17958E.description: Recognize angles as geometric shapes that are formed wherever two rays share a common endpoint, and understand concepts of angle measurement:

D68E0D10DFE60131A76B68A86D17958E.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of angle and measure angles.

D68CBF90DFE60131A76668A86D17958E.description: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (1/2, 1/4, 1/8). Solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions by using information presented in line plots.
comments: For example, from a line plot find and interpret the difference in length between the longest and shortest specimens in an insect collection.

D68DCB60DFE60131A76A68A86D17958E.description: Apply the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real world and mathematical problems.
comments: For example, find the width of a rectangular room given the area of the flooring and the length, by viewing the area formula as a multiplication equation with an unknown factor.

D68D8960DFE60131A76968A86D17958E.description: Use the four operations to solve word problems involving distances, intervals of time, liquid volumes, masses of objects, and money, including problems involving simple fractions or decimals, and problems that require expressing measurements given in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Represent measurement quantities using diagrams such as number line diagrams that feature a measurement scale.

D68D4690DFE60131A76868A86D17958E.description: Know relative sizes of measurement units within one system of units including km, m, cm; kg, g; lb, oz.; l, ml; hr, min, sec. Within a single system of measurement, express measurements in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Record measurement equivalents in a two column table.
comments: For example, know that 1 ft is 12 times as long as 1 in. Express the length of a 4 ft snake as 48 in. Generate a conversion table for feet and inches listing the number pairs (1, 12), (2, 24), (3, 36), …

D68D04A0DFE60131A76768A86D17958E.description: Solve problems involving measurement and conversion of measurements from a larger unit to a smaller unit.

D68A8E60DFE60131A75F68A86D17958E.description: Find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

D68A3EA0DFE60131A75E68A86D17958E.description: Multiply a whole number of up to four digits by a one-digit whole number, and multiply two two-digit numbers, using strategies based on place value and the properties of operations. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

D689F690DFE60131A75D68A86D17958E.description: Fluently add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.

D689A800DFE60131A75C68A86D17958E.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.

D68BAC40DFE60131A76368A86D17958E.description: Use place value understanding to round multi-digit whole numbers to any place.

D68B6C30DFE60131A76268A86D17958E.description: Read and write multi-digit whole numbers using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form. Compare two multi-digit numbers based on meanings of the digits in each place, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

D68B2950DFE60131A76168A86D17958E.description: Recognize that in a multi-digit whole number, a digit in one place represents ten times what it represents in the place to its right.
comments: For example, recognize that 700 ÷ 70 = 10 by applying concepts of place value and division.

D68ADC80DFE60131A76068A86D17958E.description: Generalize place value understanding for multi-digit whole numbers.

D68965B0DFE60131A75B68A86D17958E.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten
comments: Grade 4 expectations in this domain are limited to whole numbers less than or equal to 1,000,000.

D6889820DFE60131A75868A86D17958E.description: Generate a number or shape pattern that follows a given rule. Identify apparent features of the pattern that were not explicit in the rule itself.
comments: For example, given the rule "Add 3" and the starting number 1, generate terms in the resulting sequence and observe that the terms appear to alternate between odd and even numbers. Explain informally why the numbers will continue to alternate in this way.

D6881930DFE60131A75668A86D17958E.description: Find all factor pairs for a whole number in the range 1—100. Recognize that a whole number is a multiple of each of its factors. Determine whether a given whole number in the range 1—100 is a multiple of a given one-digit number. Determine whether a given whole number in the range 1—100 is prime or composite.

D687D890DFE60131A75568A86D17958E.description: Gain familiarity with factors and multiples.

D68792E0DFE60131A75468A86D17958E.description: Solve multistep word problems posed with whole numbers and having whole-number answers using the four operations, including problems in which remainders must be interpreted. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.

D6873510DFE60131A75368A86D17958E.description: Multiply or divide to solve word problems involving multiplicative comparison, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem, distinguishing multiplicative comparison from additive comparison.

D686DA50DFE60131A75268A86D17958E.description: Interpret a multiplication equation as a comparison, e.g., interpret 35 = 5 × 7 as a statement that 35 is 5 times as many as 7 and 7 times as many as 5. Represent verbal statements of multiplicative comparisons as multiplication equations.

D6868C60DFE60131A75168A86D17958E.description: Use the four operations with whole numbers to solve problems.

D68921B0DFE60131A75A68A86D17958E.description: Duplicate and extend (eg., What comes next?) simple patterns using concrete objects.

D6860360DFE60131A74F68A86D17958E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.
comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.

D685B640DFE60131A74E68A86D17958E.description: Look for and make use of structure.
comments: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.

Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

D6846950DFE60131A74A68A86D17958E.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.
comments: Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.

Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

D683CE80DFE60131A74868A86D17958E.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
comments: Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.
