DD3AFD00DFE60131B32F68A86D17958E.description: Reading Standards for Literacy in History/Social Studies 6—12

DD3A9A70DFE60131B32E68A86D17958E.description:
By the end of grade 9, read and comprehend literary nonfiction in the grades 9—10 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.
By the end of grade 10, read and comprehend literary nonfiction at the high end of the grades 9—10 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

DD3A4BA0DFE60131B32D68A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

DD39F640DFE60131B32C68A86D17958E.description: Read, annotate, and analyze informational texts on topics related to diverse and non-traditional cultures and viewpoints.

DD3998A0DFE60131B32B68A86D17958E.description: Analyze seminal U.S. documents of historical and literary significance (e.g., Washington's Farewell Address, the Gettysburg Address, Roosevelt's Four Freedoms speech, King's "Letter from Birmingham Jail"), including how they address related themes and concepts.

DD394960DFE60131B32A68A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, assessing whether the reasoning is valid and the evidence is relevant and sufficient; identify false statements and fallacious reasoning.

DD38F860DFE60131B32968A86D17958E.description: Analyze various accounts of a subject told in different mediums (e.g., a person's life story in both print and multimedia), determining which details are emphasized in each account.

DD382CF0DFE60131B32768A86D17958E.description: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in a text and analyze how an author uses rhetoric to advance that point of view or purpose.

DD37CF50DFE60131B32668A86D17958E.description: Analyze in detail how an author's ideas or claims are developed and refined by particular sentences, paragraphs, or larger portions of a text (e.g., a section or chapter).

DD3781C0DFE60131B32568A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings; analyze the cumulative impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone (e.g., how the language of a court opinion differs from that of a newspaper).

DD36E800DFE60131B32368A86D17958E.description: Analyze how the author unfolds an analysis or series of ideas or events, including the order in which the points are made, how they are introduced and developed, and the connections that are drawn between them.

DD3698C0DFE60131B32268A86D17958E.description: Determine a central idea of a text and analyze its development over the course of the text, including how it emerges and is shaped and refined by specific details; provide an objective summary of the text.

DD363D10DFE60131B32168A86D17958E.description: Develop factual, interpretive, and evaluative questions for further exploration of the topic(s).

DD35E780DFE60131B32068A86D17958E.description: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

DD34F260DFE60131B31D68A86D17958E.description: Establish and use criteria to classify, select, and evaluate texts to make informed judgments about the quality of the pieces.

DD3490C0DFE60131B31C68A86D17958E.description: Self-select text to respond and develop innovative perspectives.

DD342F30DFE60131B31B68A86D17958E.description: Interpret, analyze, and evaluate narratives, poetry, and drama, aesthetically and ethically by making connections to: other texts, ideas, cultural perspectives, eras, personal events and situations.

DD336740DFE60131B31968A86D17958E.description:
By the end of grade 9, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems, in the grades 9—10 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.
By the end of grade 10, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems, at the high end of the grades 9—10 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

DD3302D0DFE60131B31868A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

DD325580DFE60131B31668A86D17958E.description: Analyze how an author draws on and transforms source material in a specific work (e.g., how Shakespeare treats a theme or topic from Ovid or the Bible or how a later author draws on a play by Shakespeare).

DD320500DFE60131B31568A86D17958E.description: Analyze works by authors or artists who represent diverse world cultures.

DD31B110DFE60131B31468A86D17958E.description: Analyze the representation of a subject or a key scene in two different artistic mediums, including what is emphasized or absent in each treatment (e.g., Auden's "Musée des Beaux Arts" and Breughel's Landscape with the Fall of Icarus).

DD3100C0DFE60131B31268A86D17958E.description: Analyze a particular point of view or cultural experience reflected in a work of literature from outside the United States, drawing on a wide reading of world literature.

DD30AF70DFE60131B31168A86D17958E.description: Analyze how an author's choices concerning how to structure a text, order events within it (e.g., parallel plots), and manipulate time (e.g., pacing, flashbacks) create such effects as mystery, tension, or surprise.

DD305C20DFE60131B31068A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in the text, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the cumulative impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone (e.g., how the language evokes a sense of time and place; how it sets a formal or informal tone).

DD2FB7A0DFE60131B30E68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how complex characters (e.g., those with multiple or conflicting motivations) develop over the course of a text, interact with other characters, and advance the plot or develop the theme.

DD2F5800DFE60131B30D68A86D17958E.description: Determine a theme or central idea of a text and analyze in detail its development over the course of the text, including how it emerges and is shaped and refined by specific details; provide an objective summary of the text.

DD2EED90DFE60131B30C68A86D17958E.description: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

DD2DEB20DFE60131B30968A86D17958E.description: Respond to literature by employing knowledge of literary language, textual features, and forms to read and comprehend, reflect upon, and interpret literary texts from a variety of genres and a wide spectrum of American and world cultures.

DD2D11A0DFE60131B30768A86D17958E.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

DD2C92C0DFE60131B30668A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

DD2C3E20DFE60131B30568A86D17958E.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

DD2BE8C0DFE60131B30468A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

DD2B89A0DFE60131B30368A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.
comments: Please see "Research to Build and Present Knowledge" in Writing and "Comprehension and Collaboration" in Speaking and Listening for additional standards relevant to gathering, assessing, and applying information from print and digital sources.

DD2AEED0DFE60131B30168A86D17958E.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

DD2AA080DFE60131B30068A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

DD2A5100DFE60131B2FF68A86D17958E.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

DD299300DFE60131B2FD68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

DD293B10DFE60131B2FC68A86D17958E.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

DD28E130DFE60131B2FB68A86D17958E.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

DD2830B0DFE60131B2F968A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Reading

D75E5DA0DFE60131A8C768A86D17958E.description: (+) Work with 2 × 2 matrices as transformations of the plane, and interpret the absolute value of the determinant in terms of area.

D75DF730DFE60131A8C668A86D17958E.description: (+) Multiply a vector (regarded as a matrix with one column) by a matrix of suitable dimensions to produce another vector. Work with matrices as transformations of vectors.

D75D9A60DFE60131A8C568A86D17958E.description: (+) Understand that the zero and identity matrices play a role in matrix addition and multiplication similar to the role of 0 and 1 in the real numbers. The determinant of a square matrix is nonzero if and only if the matrix has a multiplicative inverse.

D75FC590DFE60131A8CB68A86D17958E.description: (+) Understand that, unlike multiplication of numbers, matrix multiplication for square matrices is not a commutative operation, but still satisfies the associative and distributive properties.

D75F6550DFE60131A8CA68A86D17958E.description: (+) Add, subtract, and multiply matrices of appropriate dimensions.

D75F0CB0DFE60131A8C968A86D17958E.description: (+) Multiply matrices by scalars to produce new matrices, e.g., as when all of the payoffs in a game are doubled.

D75EB1C0DFE60131A8C868A86D17958E.description: (+) Use matrices to represent and manipulate data, e.g., to represent payoffs or incidence relationships in a network.

D75D1F30DFE60131A8C468A86D17958E.description: Perform operations on matrices and use matrices in applications.

D75CAA40DFE60131A8C368A86D17958E.description: Compute the magnitude of a scalar multiple cv using ||cv|| = |c|v. Compute the direction of cv knowing that when |c|v ? 0, the direction of cv is either along v (for c > 0) or against v (for c < 0).

D75C4F00DFE60131A8C268A86D17958E.description: Represent scalar multiplication graphically by scaling vectors and possibly reversing their direction; perform scalar multiplication component-wise, e.g., as c(v<sub>x</sub>, v<sub>y</sub>) = (cv<sub>x</sub>, cv<sub>y</sub>).

D75BFC70DFE60131A8C168A86D17958E.description: (+) Multiply a vector by a scalar.

D75BA7E0DFE60131A8C068A86D17958E.description: Understand vector subtraction v - w as v + (-w), where -w is the additive inverse of w, with the same magnitude as w and pointing in the opposite direction. Represent vector subtraction graphically by connecting the tips in the appropriate order, and perform vector subtraction component-wise.

D75B4D00DFE60131A8BF68A86D17958E.description: Given two vectors in magnitude and direction form, determine the magnitude and direction of their sum.

D75AD850DFE60131A8BE68A86D17958E.description: Add vectors end-to-end, component-wise, and by the parallelogram rule. Understand that the magnitude of a sum of two vectors is typically not the sum of the magnitudes.

D759C1A0DFE60131A8BB68A86D17958E.description: (+) Solve problems involving velocity and other quantities that can be represented by vectors.

D7596860DFE60131A8BA68A86D17958E.description: (+) Find the components of a vector by subtracting the coordinates of an initial point from the coordinates of a terminal point.

D7590950DFE60131A8B968A86D17958E.description: (+) Recognize vector quantities as having both magnitude and direction. Represent vector quantities by directed line segments, and use appropriate symbols for vectors and their magnitudes (e.g., v, |v|, ||v||, v).

D758B6D0DFE60131A8B868A86D17958E.description: Represent and model with vector quantities.

D757FF10DFE60131A8B668A86D17958E.description: (+) Know the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra; show that it is true for quadratic polynomials.

D7579870DFE60131A8B568A86D17958E.description: (+) Extend polynomial identities to the complex numbers.
comments: For example, rewrite x² + 4 as (x + 2i)(x - 2i).

D7572D20DFE60131A8B468A86D17958E.description: Solve quadratic equations with real coefficients that have complex solutions.

D756DC10DFE60131A8B368A86D17958E.description: Use complex numbers in polynomial identities and equations.

D75689A0DFE60131A8B268A86D17958E.description: (+) Calculate the distance between numbers in the complex plane as the modulus of the difference, and the midpoint of a segment as the average of the numbers at its endpoints.

D7563400DFE60131A8B168A86D17958E.description: (+) Represent addition, subtraction, multiplication, and conjugation of complex numbers geometrically on the complex plane; use properties of this representation for computation.
comments: For example, (-1 + √3 i)³ = 8 because (-1 + √3 i) has modulus 2 and argument 120°.

D755DB80DFE60131A8B068A86D17958E.description: (+) Represent complex numbers on the complex plane in rectangular and polar form (including real and imaginary numbers), and explain why the rectangular and polar forms of a given complex number represent the same number.

D7557480DFE60131A8AF68A86D17958E.description: Represent complex numbers and their operations on the complex plane.

D75518B0DFE60131A8AE68A86D17958E.description: (+) Find the conjugate of a complex number; use conjugates to find moduli and quotients of complex numbers.

D754C3D0DFE60131A8AD68A86D17958E.description: Use the relation i² = -1 and the commutative, associative, and distributive properties to add, subtract, and multiply complex numbers.

D7546990DFE60131A8AC68A86D17958E.description: Know there is a complex number i such that i² = -1, and every complex number has the form a + bi with a and b real.

D7540DF0DFE60131A8AB68A86D17958E.description: Perform arithmetic operations with complex numbers.

D7534E00DFE60131A8A968A86D17958E.description: Choose a level of accuracy appropriate to limitations on measurement when reporting quantities.

D752EC00DFE60131A8A868A86D17958E.description: Define appropriate quantities for the purpose of descriptive modeling.

D75288F0DFE60131A8A768A86D17958E.description: Use units as a way to understand problems and to guide the solution of multi-step problems; choose and interpret units consistently in formulas; choose and interpret the scale and the origin in graphs and data displays.

D7522C70DFE60131A8A668A86D17958E.description: Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems.

comments: Modeling is best interpreted not as a collection of isolated topics but in relation to other standards. Making mathematical models is a Standard for Mathematical Practice, and specific modeling standards appear throughout the high school standards indicated by a star symbol (★). The star symbol sometimes appears on the heading for a group of standards; in that case, it should be understood to apply to all standards in that group.

D7513D20DFE60131A8A468A86D17958E.description: Explain why the sum or product of two rational numbers is rational; that the sum of a rational number and an irrational number is irrational; and that the product of a nonzero rational number and an irrational number is irrational.

D750E490DFE60131A8A368A86D17958E.description: Use properties of rational and irrational numbers.

D7508BE0DFE60131A8A268A86D17958E.description: Rewrite expressions involving radicals and rational exponents using the properties of exponents.

D7502B50DFE60131A8A168A86D17958E.description: Explain how the definition of the meaning of rational exponents follows from extending the properties of integer exponents to those values, allowing for a notation for radicals in terms of rational exponents.
comments: For example, we define 5<sup>1/3</sup> to be the cube root of 5 because we want (5<sup>1/3</sup>)³ = 5(<sup>1/3</sup>)³ to hold, so (5<sup>1/3</sup>)³ must equal 5.

D74FD940DFE60131A8A068A86D17958E.description: Extend the properties of exponents to rational exponents.

D74ECE00DFE60131A89D68A86D17958E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.
comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.

D74E6010DFE60131A89C68A86D17958E.description: Look for and make use of structure.
comments: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.

Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

D74CA360DFE60131A89868A86D17958E.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.
comments: Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.

Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

D74BAD10DFE60131A89668A86D17958E.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
comments: Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.

document.title: New York State P-12 Common Core Learning Standards for English Language Arts & Literacy

DBFFA4C0DFE60131B13968A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases; gather vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

DBFF33E0DFE60131B13868A86D17958E.description: Distinguish among the connotations (associations) of words with similar denotations (definitions) (e.g., stingy, scrimping, economical, unwasteful, thrifty).

DBFED830DFE60131B13768A86D17958E.description: Use the relationship between particular words (e.g., cause/effect, part/whole, item/category) to better understand each of the words.

DBFE8260DFE60131B13668A86D17958E.description: Interpret figures of speech (e.g., personification) in context.

DBFE3120DFE60131B13568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

DBFDDC60DFE60131B13468A86D17958E.description: Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

DBFD8520DFE60131B13368A86D17958E.description: Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning or its part of speech.

DBFD3810DFE60131B13268A86D17958E.description: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek or Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., audience, auditory, audible).

DBFCE7E0DFE60131B13168A86D17958E.description: Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence or paragraph; a word's position or function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

DBFC8D00DFE60131B13068A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 6 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

DBFBC5C0DFE60131B12E68A86D17958E.description: Maintain consistency in style and tone.

DBFB5EF0DFE60131B12D68A86D17958E.description: Vary sentence patterns for meaning, reader/listener interest, and style.

DBFB13C0DFE60131B12C68A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

DBFA2330DFE60131B12968A86D17958E.description: Use punctuation (commas, parentheses, dashes) to set off nonrestrictive/parenthetical elements.

DBF9D730DFE60131B12868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

DBF988B0DFE60131B12768A86D17958E.description: Recognize variations from standard English in their own and others' writing and speaking, and identify and use strategies to improve expression in conventional language.

DBF93B90DFE60131B12668A86D17958E.description: Recognize and correct vague pronouns (i.e., ones with unclear or ambiguous antecedents).

DBF8E7A0DFE60131B12568A86D17958E.description: Recognize and correct inappropriate shifts in pronoun number and person.

DBF83EF0DFE60131B12368A86D17958E.description: Ensure that pronouns are in the proper case (subjective, objective, possessive).

DBF7E970DFE60131B12268A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

DBF64540DFE60131B11E68A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

DBF6ABF0DFE60131B11F68A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

DBF5F680DFE60131B11D68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

DBF5A610DFE60131B11C68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

DBF4F190DFE60131B11A68A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

DBF44BB0DFE60131B11868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

DBF3ED50DFE60131B11768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

DBF31740DFE60131B11568A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

DBF2BF20DFE60131B11468A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

DBF26040DFE60131B11368A86D17958E.description: Include multimedia components (e.g., graphics, images, music, sound) and visual displays in presentations to clarify information.

DBF1FEE0DFE60131B11268A86D17958E.description: Present claims and findings, sequencing ideas logically and using pertinent descriptions, facts, and details to accentuate main ideas or themes; use appropriate eye contact, adequate volume, and clear pronunciation.

DBF14600DFE60131B11068A86D17958E.description: Delineate a speaker's argument and specific claims, distinguishing claims that are supported by reasons and evidence from claims that are not.

DBF0D400DFE60131B10F68A86D17958E.description: Use their experience and their knowledge of language and logic, as well as culture, to think analytically, address problems creatively, and advocate persuasively

DBF06B40DFE60131B10E68A86D17958E.description: Interpret information presented in diverse media and formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively, orally) and explain how it contributes to a topic, text, or issue under study.

DBF01EB0DFE60131B10D68A86D17958E.description: Seek to understand and communicate with individuals from different perspectives and cultural backgrounds.

DBEFCB60DFE60131B10C68A86D17958E.description: Review the key ideas expressed and demonstrate understanding of multiple perspectives through reflection and paraphrasing.

DBEF71C0DFE60131B10B68A86D17958E.description: Pose and respond to specific questions with elaboration and detail by making comments that contribute to the topic, text, or issue under discussion.

DBEF2630DFE60131B10A68A86D17958E.description: Follow rules for collegial discussions, set specific goals and deadlines, and define individual roles as needed.

DBEED900DFE60131B10968A86D17958E.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation by referring to evidence on the topic, text, or issue to probe and reflect on ideas under discussion.

DBEE8BB0DFE60131B10868A86D17958E.description: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 6 topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.

DBED8920DFE60131B10568A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

DBED3040DFE60131B10468A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

DBECD680DFE60131B10368A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

DBEC2820DFE60131B10168A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

DBEBD790DFE60131B10068A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

DBEB8540DFE60131B0FF68A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

DBEADDD0DFE60131B0FD68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

DBEA79C0DFE60131B0FC68A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for reflection and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

DBE9DD60DFE60131B0FA68A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

DBE99110DFE60131B0F968A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, using search terms effectively; assess the credibility and accuracy of each source; and quote or paraphrase the data and conclusions of others while avoiding plagiarism and following a standard format for citation.

DBE94350DFE60131B0F868A86D17958E.description: Conduct short research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question), drawing on several sources and generating additional related, focused questions that allow for multiple avenues of exploration.

DBE8EE30DFE60131B0F768A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

DBE88940DFE60131B0F668A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and present the relationships between information and ideas clearly and efficiently.

DBE82D00DFE60131B0F568A86D17958E.description: With some guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on how well purpose and audience have been addressed.

DBE7CFE0DFE60131B0F468A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

DBE72A40DFE60131B0F268A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented.

DBE6D700DFE60131B0F168A86D17958E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone.

DBE687A0DFE60131B0F068A86D17958E.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.

DBE63690DFE60131B0EF68A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate and varied transitions to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.

DBE5DF80DFE60131B0EE68A86D17958E.description: Develop the topic with relevant, well-chosen facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples.

DBE55E80DFE60131B0ED68A86D17958E.description: Introduce a topic clearly, previewing what is to follow; organize ideas, concepts, and information into broader categories as appropriate to achieving purpose; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., charts, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

DBE4FC90DFE60131B0EC68A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts, including the narration of historical events, scientific procedures/experiments, or technical processes.

DBE4A4A0DFE60131B0EB68A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from or supports the argument presented.

DBE45390DFE60131B0EA68A86D17958E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style.

DBE40320DFE60131B0E968A86D17958E.description: Use words, phrases, and clauses to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence.

DBE3AE90DFE60131B0E868A86D17958E.description: Support claim(s) with logical reasoning and relevant, accurate data and evidence that demonstrate an understanding of the topic or text, using credible sources.

DBE34AF0DFE60131B0E768A86D17958E.description: Introduce claim(s) about a topic or issue, acknowledge and distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims, and organize the reasons and evidence logically.

DBE2F450DFE60131B0E668A86D17958E.description: Write arguments focused on discipline-specific content.

DBE25150DFE60131B0E468A86D17958E.description: Writing Standards for Literacy in History/Social Studies, Science, and Technical Subjects 6—12

DBE20570DFE60131B0E368A86D17958E.description: Create poetry, stories, plays, and other literary forms (e.g. videos, art work).

DBE1B2F0DFE60131B0E268A86D17958E.description: Recognize and illustrate social, historical, and cultural features in the presentation of literary texts.

DBE160D0DFE60131B0E168A86D17958E.description: Develop a perspective or theme supported by relevant details.

DBE110B0DFE60131B0E068A86D17958E.description: Create and present a text or art work in response to a literary work.

DBE074C0DFE60131B0DE68A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

DBDFAF10DFE60131B0DC68A86D17958E.description: Apply grade 6 Reading standards to literary nonfiction (e.g., "Trace and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, distinguishing claims that are supported by reasons and evidence from claims that are not").

DBDF55F0DFE60131B0DB68A86D17958E.description: Apply grade 6 Reading standards to literature (e.g., "Compare and contrast texts in different forms or genres [e.g., stories and poems; historical novels and fantasy stories] in terms of their approaches to similar themes and topics").

DBDF0500DFE60131B0DA68A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

DBDEB7A0DFE60131B0D968A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources; assess the credibility of each source; and quote or paraphrase the data and conclusions of others while avoiding plagiarism and providing basic bibliographic information for sources.

DBDE6560DFE60131B0D868A86D17958E.description: Conduct short research projects to answer a question, drawing on several sources and refocusing the inquiry when appropriate.

DBDE0E20DFE60131B0D768A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

DBDDBD90DFE60131B0D668A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing as well as to interact and collaborate with others; demonstrate sufficient command of keyboarding skills to type a minimum of three pages in a single sitting.

D70E88D0DFE60131A85368A86D17958E.description: Find probabilities of compound events using organized lists, tables, tree diagrams, and simulation.

D70E2D20DFE60131A85268A86D17958E.description: Develop a probability model (which may not be uniform) by observing frequencies in data generated from a chance process.
comments: For example, find the approximate probability that a spinning penny will land heads up or that a tossed paper cup will land open-end down. Do the outcomes for the spinning penny appear to be equally likely based on the observed frequencies?

D70DE620DFE60131A85168A86D17958E.description: Develop a uniform probability model by assigning equal probability to all outcomes, and use the model to determine probabilities of events.
comments: For example, if a student is selected at random from a class, find the probability that Jane will be selected and the probability that a girl will be selected.

D70DA4C0DFE60131A85068A86D17958E.description: Develop a probability model and use it to find probabilities of events. Compare probabilities from a model to observed frequencies; if the agreement is not good, explain possible sources of the discrepancy.

D70D6200DFE60131A84F68A86D17958E.description: Approximate the probability of a chance event by collecting data on the chance process that produces it and observing its long-run relative frequency, and predict the approximate relative frequency given the probability.
comments: For example, when rolling a number cube 600 times, predict that a 3 or 6 would be rolled roughly 200 times, but probably not exactly 200 times.

D70D1ED0DFE60131A84E68A86D17958E.description: Understand that the probability of a chance event is a number between 0 and 1 that expresses the likelihood of the event occurring. Larger numbers indicate greater likelihood. A probability near 0 indicates an unlikely event, a probability around 1/2 indicates an event that is neither unlikely nor likely, and a probability near 1 indicates a likely event.

D70CDC60DFE60131A84D68A86D17958E.description: Investigate chance processes and develop, use, and evaluate probability models.

D70C9620DFE60131A84C68A86D17958E.description: Use measures of center and measures of variability for numerical data from random samples to draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.
comments: For example, decide whether the words in a chapter of a seventh-grade science book are generally longer than the words in a chapter of a fourth-grade science book.

D70C3D90DFE60131A84B68A86D17958E.description: Informally assess the degree of visual overlap of two numerical data distributions with similar variabilities, measuring the difference between the centers by expressing it as a multiple of a measure of variability.
comments: For example, the mean height of players on the basketball team is 10 cm greater than the mean height of players on the soccer team, about twice the variability (mean absolute deviation) on either team; on a dot plot, the separation between the two distributions of heights is noticeable.

D70BEF50DFE60131A84A68A86D17958E.description: Draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.

D70B9B60DFE60131A84968A86D17958E.description: Use data from a random sample to draw inferences about a population with an unknown characteristic of interest. Generate multiple samples (or simulated samples) of the same size to gauge the variation in estimates or predictions.
comments: For example, estimate the mean word length in a book by randomly sampling words from the book; predict the winner of a school election based on randomly sampled survey data. Gauge how far off the estimate or prediction might be.

D70B4320DFE60131A84868A86D17958E.description: Understand that statistics can be used to gain information about a population by examining a sample of the population; generalizations about a population from a sample are valid only if the sample is representative of that population. Understand that random sampling tends to produce representative samples and support valid inferences.

D70AFD20DFE60131A84768A86D17958E.description: Use random sampling to draw inferences about a population.

D70A6C10DFE60131A84568A86D17958E.description: Solve word problems leading to inequalities of the form px + q > r or px + q < r, where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers. Graph the solution set of the inequality and interpret it in the context of the problem.
comments: For example: As a salesperson, you are paid $50 per week plus $3 per sale. This week you want your pay to be at least $100. Write an inequality for the number of sales you need to make, and describe the solutions.

D70A28D0DFE60131A84468A86D17958E.description: Solve word problems leading to equations of the form px + q = r and p(x + q) = r, where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers. Solve equations of these forms fluently. Compare an algebraic solution to an arithmetic solution, identifying the sequence of the operations used in each approach.
comments: For example, the perimeter of a rectangle is 54 cm. Its length is 6 cm. What is its width?

D709E510DFE60131A84368A86D17958E.description: Use variables to represent quantities in a real-world or mathematical problem, and construct simple equations and inequalities to solve problems by reasoning about the quantities.

D70995B0DFE60131A84268A86D17958E.description: Solve multi-step real-life and mathematical problems posed with positive and negative rational numbers in any form (whole numbers, fractions, and decimals), using tools strategically. Apply properties of operations to calculate with numbers in any form; convert between forms as appropriate; and assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies.
comments: For example: If a woman making $25 an hour gets a 10% raise, she will make an additional 1/10 of her salary an hour, or $2.50, for a new salary of $27.50. If you want to place a towel bar 9 3/4 inches long in the center of a door that is 27 1/2 inches wide, you will need to place the bar about 9 inches from each edge; this estimate can be used as a check on the exact computation.

D7094880DFE60131A84168A86D17958E.description: Solve real-life and mathematical problems using numerical and algebraic expressions and equations.

D708CAB0DFE60131A84068A86D17958E.description: Understand that rewriting an expression in different forms in a problem context can shed light on the problem and how the quantities in it are related.
comments: For example, a + 0.05a = 1.05a means that "increase by 5%" is the same as "multiply by 1.05."

D7086420DFE60131A83F68A86D17958E.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add, subtract, factor, and expand linear expressions with rational coefficients.

D7082390DFE60131A83E68A86D17958E.description: Use properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions.

D707A240DFE60131A83C68A86D17958E.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving the four operations with rational numbers.
comments: Computations with rational numbers extend the rules for manipulating fractions to complex fractions.

D7075FB0DFE60131A83B68A86D17958E.description: Convert a rational number to a decimal using long division; know that the decimal form of a rational number terminates in 0s or eventually repeats.

D7071A50DFE60131A83A68A86D17958E.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide rational numbers.

D706C410DFE60131A83968A86D17958E.description: Understand that integers can be divided, provided that the divisor is not zero, and every quotient of integers (with non-zero divisor) is a rational number. If p and q are integers, then -(p/q) = (-p)/q = p/(-q). Interpret quotients of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

D7066C80DFE60131A83868A86D17958E.description: Understand that multiplication is extended from fractions to rational numbers by requiring that operations continue to satisfy the properties of operations, particularly the distributive property, leading to products such as (-1)(-1) = 1 and the rules for multiplying signed numbers. Interpret products of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

D7061FD0DFE60131A83768A86D17958E.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division and of fractions to multiply and divide rational numbers.

D705DB70DFE60131A83668A86D17958E.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract rational numbers.

D7059590DFE60131A83568A86D17958E.description: Understand subtraction of rational numbers as adding the additive inverse, p - q = p + (-q). Show that the distance between two rational numbers on the number line is the absolute value of their difference, and apply this principle in real-world contexts.

D7054C40DFE60131A83468A86D17958E.description: Understand p + q as the number located a distance |q| from p, in the positive or negative direction depending on whether q is positive or negative. Show that a number and its opposite have a sum of 0 (are additive inverses). Interpret sums of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

D70501C0DFE60131A83368A86D17958E.description: Describe situations in which opposite quantities combine to make 0.
comments: For example, a hydrogen atom has 0 charge because its two constituents are oppositely charged.

D704B240DFE60131A83268A86D17958E.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of addition and subtraction to add and subtract rational numbers; represent addition and subtraction on a horizontal or vertical number line diagram.

D70470F0DFE60131A83168A86D17958E.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of operations with fractions to add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational numbers.

D703EA00DFE60131A82F68A86D17958E.description: Use proportional relationships to solve multistep ratio and percent problems.
comments: Examples: simple interest, tax, markups and markdowns, gratuities and commissions, fees, percent increase and decrease, percent error.

D703A3B0DFE60131A82E68A86D17958E.description: Explain what a point (x, y) on the graph of a proportional relationship means in terms of the situation, with special attention to the points (0, 0) and (1, r) where r is the unit rate.

comments: For example, if total cost t is proportional to the number n of items purchased at a constant price p, the relationship between the total cost and the number of items can be expressed as t = pn.

D702E640DFE60131A82C68A86D17958E.description: Identify the constant of proportionality (unit rate) in tables, graphs, equations, diagrams, and verbal descriptions of proportional relationships.

D702A3D0DFE60131A82B68A86D17958E.description: Decide whether two quantities are in a proportional relationship, e.g., by testing for equivalent ratios in a table or graphing on a coordinate plane and observing whether the graph is a straight line through the origin.

D7025F20DFE60131A82A68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and represent proportional relationships between quantities.

D70217A0DFE60131A82968A86D17958E.description: Compute unit rates associated with ratios of fractions, including ratios of lengths, areas and other quantities measured in like or different units.
comments: For example, if a person walks 1/2 mile in each 1/4 hour, compute the unit rate as the complex fraction <sup>1/2</sup>/<sub>1/4</sub> miles per hour, equivalently 2 miles per hour.

D701D120DFE60131A82868A86D17958E.description: Analyze proportional relationships and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

D7012F90DFE60131A82668A86D17958E.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, volume and surface area of two- and three-dimensional objects composed of triangles, quadrilaterals, polygons, cubes, and right prisms.

D700ED70DFE60131A82568A86D17958E.description: Use facts about supplementary, complementary, vertical, and adjacent angles in a multi-step problem to write and solve simple equations for an unknown angle in a figure.

D700AD20DFE60131A82468A86D17958E.description: Know the formulas for the area and circumference of a circle and use them to solve problems; give an informal derivation of the relationship between the circumference and area of a circle.

D7006D00DFE60131A82368A86D17958E.description: Solve real-life and mathematical problems involving angle measure, area, surface area, and volume.

D7002CB0DFE60131A82268A86D17958E.description: Describe the two-dimensional figures that result from slicing three-dimensional figures, as in plane sections of right rectangular prisms and right rectangular pyramids.

D6FFEA90DFE60131A82168A86D17958E.description: Draw (freehand, with ruler and protractor, and with technology) geometric shapes with given conditions. Focus on constructing triangles from three measures of angles or sides, noticing when the conditions determine a unique triangle, more than one triangle, or no triangle.

D6FFA670DFE60131A82068A86D17958E.description: Solve problems involving scale drawings of geometric figures, including computing actual lengths and areas from a scale drawing and reproducing a scale drawing at a different scale.

D6FF56B0DFE60131A81F68A86D17958E.description: Draw, construct, and describe geometrical figures and describe the relationships between them.

D6FEAB70DFE60131A81D68A86D17958E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.
comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.

D6FE50B0DFE60131A81C68A86D17958E.description: Look for and make use of structure.
comments: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.

Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

D6FCCCE0DFE60131A81868A86D17958E.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.
comments: Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.

Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

D6FC2CB0DFE60131A81668A86D17958E.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
comments: Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.

document.title: New York State P-12 Common Core Learning Standards for English Language Arts & Literacy

DB42A760DFE60131AFA768A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, including those that signal precise actions, emotions, or states of being (e.g., quizzed, whined, stammered) and that are basic to a particular topic (e.g., wildlife, conservation, and endangered when discussing animal preservation).

DB4251F0DFE60131AFA668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of words by relating them to their opposites (antonyms) and to words with similar but not identical meanings (synonyms).

DB41D910DFE60131AFA568A86D17958E.description: Recognize and explain the meaning of common idioms, adages, and proverbs.

DB418ED0DFE60131AFA468A86D17958E.description: Explain the meaning of simple similes and metaphors (e.g., as pretty as a picture) in context.

DB414610DFE60131AFA368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

DB40F9F0DFE60131AFA268A86D17958E.description: Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation and determine or clarify the precise meaning of key words and phrases.

DB40A880DFE60131AFA168A86D17958E.description: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek and Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., telegraph, photograph, autograph).

DB405180DFE60131AFA068A86D17958E.description: Use context (e.g., definitions, examples, or restatements in text) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

DB3FF9C0DFE60131AF9F68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 4 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

DB3F4CD0DFE60131AF9D68A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English (e.g., presenting ideas) and situations where informal discourse is appropriate (e.g., small-group discussion).

DB3E92C0DFE60131AF9B68A86D17958E.description: Choose words and phrases to convey ideas precisely.

DB3E2F00DFE60131AF9A68A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

DB3D9B90DFE60131AF9868A86D17958E.description: Spell grade-appropriate words correctly, consulting references as needed.

DB3D4960DFE60131AF9768A86D17958E.description: Use a comma before a coordinating conjunction in a compound sentence.

DB3CEBB0DFE60131AF9668A86D17958E.description: Use commas and quotation marks to mark direct speech and quotations from a text.

DB3C4730DFE60131AF9468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

DB3BF850DFE60131AF9368A86D17958E.description: Correctly use frequently confused words (e.g., to, too, two; there, their).

DB3BA470DFE60131AF9268A86D17958E.description: Produce complete sentences, recognizing and correcting inappropriate fragments and run-ons.

DB3AEAC0DFE60131AF9068A86D17958E.description: Order adjectives within sentences according to conventional patterns (e.g., a small red bag rather than a red small bag).

DB3A93E0DFE60131AF8F68A86D17958E.description: Use modal auxiliaries (e.g., can, may, must) to convey various conditions.

DB3A4000DFE60131AF8E68A86D17958E.description: Form and use the progressive (e.g., I was walking; I am walking; I will be walking) verb tenses.

DB39EFB0DFE60131AF8D68A86D17958E.description: Use relative pronouns (who, whose, whom, which, that) and relative adverbs (where, when, why).

DB399BF0DFE60131AF8C68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

DB3873D0DFE60131AF8968A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

DB382400DFE60131AF8868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

DB37CA30DFE60131AF8768A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

DB3730F0DFE60131AF8568A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

DB368EE0DFE60131AF8368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

DB3635F0DFE60131AF8268A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

DB3575F0DFE60131AF8068A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

DB3513B0DFE60131AF7F68A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English (e.g., presenting ideas) and situations where informal discourse is appropriate (e.g., small-group discussion); use formal English when appropriate to task and situation.

DB34C4F0DFE60131AF7E68A86D17958E.description: Add audio recordings and visual displays to presentations when appropriate to enhance the development of main ideas or themes.

DB3470D0DFE60131AF7D68A86D17958E.description: Report on a topic or text, tell a story, or recount an experience in an organized manner, using appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details to support main ideas or themes; speak clearly at an understandable pace.

DB33D960DFE60131AF7B68A86D17958E.description: Identify the reasons and evidence a speaker provides to support particular points.

DB338CC0DFE60131AF7A68A86D17958E.description: Paraphrase portions of a text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

DB332830DFE60131AF7968A86D17958E.description: Seek to understand and communicate with individuals from different perspectives and cultural backgrounds.

DB32C740DFE60131AF7868A86D17958E.description: Review the key ideas expressed and explain their own ideas and understanding in light of the discussion.

DB326CC0DFE60131AF7768A86D17958E.description: Pose and respond to specific questions to clarify or follow up on information, and make comments that contribute to the discussion and link to the remarks of others.

DB322490DFE60131AF7668A86D17958E.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions and carry out assigned roles.

DB31DA30DFE60131AF7568A86D17958E.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation and other information known about the topic to explore ideas under discussion.

DB319130DFE60131AF7468A86D17958E.description: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 4 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.

DB309CC0DFE60131AF7168A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

DB305060DFE60131AF7068A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

DB3002A0DFE60131AF6F68A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

DB2F7040DFE60131AF6D68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

DB2F2080DFE60131AF6C68A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

DB2EC430DFE60131AF6B68A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

DB2E1E00DFE60131AF6968A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

DB2DC530DFE60131AF6868A86D17958E.description: Create and present a poem, narrative, play, art work, or literary review in response to a particular author or theme studied in class.

DB2CD250DFE60131AF6668A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

DB2C33A0DFE60131AF6468A86D17958E.description: Apply grade 4 Reading standards to informational texts (e.g., "Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text").

DB2BE6D0DFE60131AF6368A86D17958E.description: Apply grade 4 Reading standards to literature (e.g., "Describe in depth a character, setting, or event in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the text [e.g., a character's thoughts, words, or actions].").

DB2B9940DFE60131AF6268A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

DB2B45E0DFE60131AF6168A86D17958E.description: Recall relevant information from experiences or gather relevant information from print and digital sources; take notes and categorize information, and provide a list of sources.

DB2AECA0DFE60131AF6068A86D17958E.description: Conduct short research projects that build knowledge through investigation of different aspects of a topic.

DB2AA430DFE60131AF5F68A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

DB2A5990DFE60131AF5E68A86D17958E.description: With some guidance and support from adults, use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing as well as to interact and collaborate with others; demonstrate sufficient command of keyboarding skills to type a minimum of one page in a single sitting.

DB2A0D60DFE60131AF5D68A86D17958E.description: With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, and editing.

DB29C0C0DFE60131AF5C68A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.
comments: (Grade-specific expectations for writing types are defined in standards 1—3 above.)

DB290C50DFE60131AF5A68A86D17958E.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from the narrated experiences or events.

DB25C2B0DFE60131AF5068A86D17958E.description: Introduce a topic clearly and group related information in paragraphs and sections; include formatting (e.g., headings), illustrations, and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

DB256CC0DFE60131AF4F68A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information clearly.

DB252590DFE60131AF4E68A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section related to the opinion presented.

DB244990DFE60131AF4B68A86D17958E.description: Introduce a topic or text clearly, state an opinion, and create an organizational structure in which related ideas are grouped to support the writer's purpose.

DB2310C0DFE60131AF4768A86D17958E.description: Develop personal, cultural, textual, and thematic connections within and across genres as they respond to texts through written, digital, and oral presentations, employing a variety of media and genres.

DB2250A0DFE60131AF4568A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

DB1A74E0DFE60131AF4368A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

DB1A1030DFE60131AF4268A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

DB19A270DFE60131AF4168A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

DB1941C0DFE60131AF4068A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

DB184640DFE60131AF3D68A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

DB17B1F0DFE60131AF3B68A86D17958E.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

DB176870DFE60131AF3A68A86D17958E.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

DB171BE0DFE60131AF3968A86D17958E.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

DB1625A0DFE60131AF3668A86D17958E.description: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.

DB15DCF0DFE60131AF3568A86D17958E.description: Read on-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings

DB159320DFE60131AF3468A86D17958E.description: Read on-level text with purpose and understanding.

DB154630DFE60131AF3368A86D17958E.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.
