DB143D40DFE60131AF3068A86D17958E.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.

DB130190DFE60131AF2D68A86D17958E.description: By the end of year, read and comprehend informational texts, including history/social studies, science, and technical texts, in the grades 4—5 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

DB12B990DFE60131AF2C68A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

DB127180DFE60131AF2B68A86D17958E.description: Integrate information from two texts on the same topic in order to write or speak about the subject knowledgeably.

DB122900DFE60131AF2A68A86D17958E.description: Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text.

DB11DE60DFE60131AF2968A86D17958E.description: Interpret information presented visually, orally, or quantitatively (e.g., in charts, graphs, diagrams, time lines, animations, or interactive elements on Web pages) and explain how the information contributes to an understanding of the text in which it appears.

DB112EC0DFE60131AF2768A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast a firsthand and secondhand account of the same event or topic; describe the differences in focus and the information provided.

DB10E1F0DFE60131AF2668A86D17958E.description: Describe the overall structure (e.g., chronology, comparison, cause/effect, problem/solution) of events, ideas, concepts, or information in a text or part of a text.

DB109420DFE60131AF2568A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words or phrases in a text relevant to a grade 4 topic or subject area.

DB0FE510DFE60131AF2368A86D17958E.description: Explain events, procedures, ideas, or concepts in a historical, scientific, or technical text, including what happened and why, based on specific information in the text.

DB0F8B50DFE60131AF2268A86D17958E.description: Determine the main idea of a text and explain how it is supported by key details; summarize the text.

DB0F1DD0DFE60131AF2168A86D17958E.description: Refer to details and examples in a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.

DB0E14C0DFE60131AF1E68A86D17958E.description: Self-select text based upon personal preferences.

DB0D9790DFE60131AF1D68A86D17958E.description: Recognize, interpret and make connections in narratives, poetry, and drama, to other texts, ideas, cultural perspectives, personal events and situations.

DB0CFA80DFE60131AF1B68A86D17958E.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poetry, in the grades 4—5 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

DB0CB0A0DFE60131AF1A68A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

DB0C1A20DFE60131AF1868A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the treatment of similar themes and topics (e.g., opposition of good and evil) and patterns of events (e.g., the quest) in stories, myths, and traditional literature from different cultures.

DB0BC980DFE60131AF1768A86D17958E.description: Make connections between the text of a story or drama and a visual or oral presentation of the text, identifying where each version reflects specific descriptions and directions in the text.

DB0B2A60DFE60131AF1568A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the point of view from which different stories are narrated, including the difference between first- and third-person narrations.

DB0ADB80DFE60131AF1468A86D17958E.description: Explain major differences between poems, drama, and prose, and refer to the structural elements of poems (e.g., verse, rhythm, meter) and drama (e.g., casts of characters, settings, descriptions, dialogue, stage directions) when writing or speaking about a text.

DB0A6F00DFE60131AF1368A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including those that allude to significant characters found in mythology (e.g., Herculean).

DB09AB40DFE60131AF1168A86D17958E.description: Describe in depth a character, setting, or event in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the text (e.g., a character's thoughts, words, or actions).

DB095F30DFE60131AF1068A86D17958E.description: Determine a theme of a story, drama, or poem from details in the text; summarize the text.

DB091350DFE60131AF0F68A86D17958E.description: Refer to details and examples in a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.

DB07F400DFE60131AF0C68A86D17958E.description: Respond to literature by employing knowledge of literary language, textual features, and forms to read and comprehend, reflect upon, and interpret literary texts from a variety of genres and a wide spectrum of American and world cultures.

DB075410DFE60131AF0A68A86D17958E.description: Read and comprehend complex literary and informational texts independently and proficiently.

DB070CF0DFE60131AF0968A86D17958E.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

DB06C330DFE60131AF0868A86D17958E.description: Analyze how two or more texts address similar themes or topics in order to build knowledge or to compare the approaches the authors take.

DB0675E0DFE60131AF0768A86D17958E.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, including the validity of the reasoning as well as the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence.

DB061F30DFE60131AF0668A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate content presented in diverse media and formats, including visually and quantitatively, as well as in words.

DB059010DFE60131AF0468A86D17958E.description: Assess how point of view or purpose shapes the content and style of a text.

DB054480DFE60131AF0368A86D17958E.description: Analyze the structure of texts, including how specific sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text (e.g., a section, chapter, scene, or stanza) relate to each other and the whole.

DB04F780DFE60131AF0268A86D17958E.description: Interpret words and phrases as they are used in a text, including determining technical, connotative, and figurative meanings, and analyze how specific word choices shape meaning or tone.

DB0455C0DFE60131AF0068A86D17958E.description: Analyze how and why individuals, events, and ideas develop and interact over the course of a text.

DB040BE0DFE60131AEFF68A86D17958E.description: Determine central ideas or themes of a text and analyze their development; summarize the key supporting details and ideas.

DB03B8C0DFE60131AEFE68A86D17958E.description: Read closely to determine what the text says explicitly and to make logical inferences from it; cite specific textual evidence when writing or speaking to support conclusions drawn from the text.

document.title: Learning Standards for The Arts
