DF34F460DFE60131B74468A86D17958E.description:
Engage in pre-reading and reading activities to
  • select books, tapes, and poems on the basis of personal choice/interest or teacher-selected criteria, such as a theme/topic
  • predict what might happen next in a story read aloud or independently
  • draw conclusions from a story
  • identify characters, settings, and events in a story
  • retell a story
  • distinguish between what is real and what is imaginary

DF34A3F0DFE60131B74368A86D17958E.description: Comprehend and respond to imaginative texts and performances; interpret, with assistance

DF344770DFE60131B74268A86D17958E.description: Students will read, write, listen, and speak for literary response and expression.

DF33E040DFE60131B74168A86D17958E.description: Select books to meet informational needs, with assistance

DF336E50DFE60131B74068A86D17958E.description: Use a picture dictionary as a resource for vocabulary development

DF332460DFE60131B73F68A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between texts with stories and texts with information

DF32D520DFE60131B73E68A86D17958E.description: Read grade-level informational texts to begin to collect data, facts, and ideas, with assistance

DF327850DFE60131B73D68A86D17958E.description: Locate and use classroom and library media center resources to acquire information, with assistance

DF322B20DFE60131B73C68A86D17958E.description: Students will read, write, listen, and speak for information and understanding.

DF318E30DFE60131B73A68A86D17958E.description: Check accuracy of decoding using context to monitor and self-correct

DF314190DFE60131B73968A86D17958E.description: Decode grade-level words using knowledge of root words, prefixes, suffixes, verb endings, plurals, contractions, and compounds

DF30EE40DFE60131B73868A86D17958E.description: Read common word families by blending the onset (/s/) and the rime (/it/, /at/) in grade-level words (s-it, s-at)

DF3098D0DFE60131B73768A86D17958E.description: Blend sounds using knowledge of letter-sound correspondences in order to decode unfamiliar, but decodable, one-syllable grade-level words

DF304BA0DFE60131B73668A86D17958E.description: Identify and produce letter-sound correspondences, including consonants and short and long vowels

DF2FFB70DFE60131B73568A86D17958E.description: Decoding Including Phonics and Structural Analysis

DF2F9F40DFE60131B73468A86D17958E.description: Segment spoken words into component sounds, manipulating letters to represent each sound of most one-syllable words

DF2F4210DFE60131B73368A86D17958E.description: Blend spoken sounds to form words, manipulating letters to represent each sound of most one-syllable words

DF2EE200DFE60131B73268A86D17958E.description: Count the number of syllables in a word

DF2E4030DFE60131B73068A86D17958E.description: Show familiarity with title and author of grade-level books

DF2D6A00DFE60131B72E68A86D17958E.description: Show interest in reading a range of grade-level children's texts from a variety of genres, such as stories, folktales, fairy tales, poems, and informational texts

DF2CC380DFE60131B72C68A86D17958E.description: Use own perspectives and opinions to comprehend text

DF2C2BD0DFE60131B72A68A86D17958E.description: Summarize main ideas from informational texts

DF2B86E0DFE60131B72868A86D17958E.description: Answer simple questions (such as how? why? what if?) in response to texts

DF2B2E60DFE60131B72768A86D17958E.description: Ask questions in response to texts

DF2ADB30DFE60131B72668A86D17958E.description: Use graphic or semantic organizers to organize and categorize information

DF2A8280DFE60131B72568A86D17958E.description: Work cooperatively with peers (e.g., peer pairs or small groups) to comprehend text

DF2A2C20DFE60131B72468A86D17958E.description: Use comprehension strategies (predict/confirm, reread, self-correct) to clarify meaning of text

DF29BE90DFE60131B72368A86D17958E.description: Read grade-level texts for different purposes

DF291830DFE60131B72168A86D17958E.description: Use a dictionary to learn the meanings of words

DF28C780DFE60131B72068A86D17958E.description: Increase background knowledge by elaborating and integrating new vocabulary and ideas from texts

DF286A00DFE60131B71F68A86D17958E.description: Learn new words indirectly from reading books and other print sources

DF27E8E0DFE60131B71E68A86D17958E.description: Connect words and ideas in books to prior knowledge

DF279490DFE60131B71D68A86D17958E.description: Study root words, prefixes, suffixes, verb endings, and plural nouns to learn new grade-level vocabulary

DF274060DFE60131B71C68A86D17958E.description: Study categories of words (e.g., animals, place names) to learn new grade-level vocabulary

DF26F620DFE60131B71B68A86D17958E.description: Study antonyms, synonyms, and homonyms to learn new grade-level vocabulary

DF265940DFE60131B71968A86D17958E.description: Read grade-level texts with decodable and irregularly spelled words at appropriate speed, accuracy and expression (target benchmark at grade 1: 71 WPM) (Davidson, M., & Towner, J. (2000). Reading Screening Test. Bellingham, WA: Applied Research and Development Center.)

DF260080DFE60131B71868A86D17958E.description: Use punctuation clues to read connected text with expression, accuracy and fluency

DF25AE00DFE60131B71768A86D17958E.description: Sight-read automatically 300–500 words including sight and decodable words (Snow, C. E., Burns, M. S., & Griffin, P. (1998). Preventing reading difficulties in young children. Washington, DC: National Academy Press, p. 81.)

DF255260DFE60131B71668A86D17958E.description: Sight-read automatically grade-level irregularly spelled words

DF24F810DFE60131B71568A86D17958E.description: Sight-read automatically grade-level common, high-frequency words

DF242A50DFE60131B71368A86D17958E.description: Identify parts of a book and their purposes including identification of author, illustrator, title page, table of contents, and chapter headings

DF234B20DFE60131B71068A86D17958E.description: Use computer software to support early reading development

DF22FD10DFE60131B70F68A86D17958E.description: Read aloud with expression and fluency

DF22A910DFE60131B70E68A86D17958E.description: Monitor own reading by applying strategies (e.g., sounding out letters; using context, grammar, and picture clues; and rereading) to determine meaning

DF21FDC0DFE60131B70C68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that words consist of a combination of sounds

DF2164C0DFE60131B70A68A86D17958E.description: Recognize own name and the names of friends and family in print

DF2118E0DFE60131B70968A86D17958E.description: Recognize the singular and plural of frequently used words

DF20CB40DFE60131B70868A86D17958E.description: Point to words in a text or on a chart when read aloud, matching spoken word to print

DF2076B0DFE60131B70768A86D17958E.description: Recognize the different sounds that make up a word

DF202D40DFE60131B70668A86D17958E.description: Use beginning and ending consonants, as well as vowel sounds, to identify words

DF1FE510DFE60131B70568A86D17958E.description: Distinguish the difference between vowels and consonants

DF1F9C30DFE60131B70468A86D17958E.description: Alphabetize high-frequency words according to the first letter

DF1F51C0DFE60131B70368A86D17958E.description: Recognize and identify letters of the alphabet

DF1EADA0DFE60131B70168A86D17958E.description: Follow left-to-right and top to bottom direction when reading

DF1E6390DFE60131B70068A86D17958E.description: Recognize the difference between letters and words

document.title: New York State K-8 Social Studies Framework

10EF0F81CB704D4AAAA41A265BA613DA.description: Students will examine products that are exported from the United States to other markets in the Western Hemisphere, noting how this affects the United States economy.

A961743364B84F188845E7D8CC0EA42D.description: Students will examine products that are imported into markets within the United States based on demand for these products, noting how this affects the United States economy.

01E045A1CB0C472FBB0B017A48C825B4.description: Countries trade with other countries to meet economic needs and wants. They are interdependent.

B49E520A30A7496C91D51C502BE496E0.description: Students will examine why certain products are manufactured in particular places, taking into account the weight, transportation availability, and costs and markets (e.g., soda pop).

BB9FE3F1001440C199811DCB6DF43879.description: Students will identify the major natural resources of the United States, Canada, Mexico, and one Caribbean or one South American country to determine the major industries of those countries in relation to available resources.

55895C1D9C32493FAB6EBFB42AF2AEE7.description: Peoples of the Western Hemisphere have engaged in a variety of economic activities to meet their needs and wants.

A53B68CC400D487383FCF14063B47CB6.description: Students will explore the characteristics of a traditional economy used by the Inuit, the market economy of the United States or Canada, and the command economy of Cuba, noting similarities and differences.

4E00CF4D3B1A4525BE6AC05CCA54AB24.description: Different types of economic systems have developed across time and place within the Western Hemisphere. These economic systems include traditional, market, and command which address the three economic questions: what will be produced, how it will be produced, and who will get what is produced?

FE638914505F4C0990A71C72FCD58243.description: Economics: The people of the Western Hemisphere have developed various ways to meet their needs and wants. Many of the countries of the Western Hemisphere trade with each other as well as with other countries around the world.

829A90B6B3B547AE81AB06A120553F91.description: Students will examine multinational organizations and nongovernmental organizations and their role in promoting cooperation, peace, and cultural understanding.

5D0C8A184ACE4B3C90C9597A19D9FFC3.description: Multinational organizations and nongovernmental organizations in the Western Hemisphere seek to encourage cooperation between nations, protect human rights, support economic development and provide assistance in challenging situations.

785450E4FCA7412792FA18FFCB53E5B8.description: Students will examine at least one group of people such as Native Americans, African Americans, women, or another cultural, ethnic, or racial minority in the Western Hemisphere who have struggled or are struggling for equality and civil rights or sovereignty.

1685EA560BF24E8ABD2A798FD566CB17.description: Across time and place, different groups of people in the Western Hemisphere have struggled and fought for equality and civil rights or sovereignty.

5332915C07634942A823262BC3CB4F27.description: Students will examine the Declaration of Independence, the United States Constitution and Bill of Rights, the British North America Act, and the Canadian Bill of Rights in terms of key values, beliefs, and principles of constitutional democracy.

6C2BB8BECBAE4E7F96FB6F0F5E79DBC1.description: Legal, political, and historic documents define the values, beliefs, and principles of constitutional democracy.

963258DE73E54F4D8E151D8DFC4BFF4D.description: Students will compare and contrast the government structures and functions of the United States government with those of Canada, Mexico, and one other country in either the Caribbean or South America.

54D80471EC2B4E05903C917B79305577.description: Students will examine the foundational documents of the United States government for evidence of the country's beliefs, values, and principles.

5BF14D9AB3414F96A66B31614472FBD1.description: Students will examine the basic structure of the United States federal government, including the president, Congress, and the courts.

8F60855C94F4487E8628E07505A92992.description: Government structures, functions, and founding documents vary from place to place in the countries of the Western Hemisphere.

52D2C4596202466B83FEE4769D8EA386.description: Government: The political systems of the Western Hemisphere vary in structure and organization across time and place.

2291E6B98D804A37AB21F2DE929CE705.description: Students will investigate a current issue that two or more Western Hemisphere countries are facing together. Some examples include environmental issues, immigration, and trade.

CCB37A61EF9A401597A9D4DD8EADC8EF.description: Countries in the Western Hemisphere face a variety of concerns and issues specific to the region.

E58D170D71AA4D5E9DF32E64AAC00E87.description: Students will compare and contrast key cultural characteristics and the contributions associated with the United States with those associated with Canada, Mexico, and a country in either the Caribbean or South America.

4FF7E2ED7280424496734E325FCFCFAB.description: Students will explore key cultural characteristics such as the languages and religions and contributions of the United States, Canada, Mexico, and one Caribbean or one South American country.

1213BAC972B34B629691C0630F5FD277.description: The countries of the Western Hemisphere have varied characteristics and contributions that distinguish them from other countries.

9F13A91464A5485DACF91604EFBFE7D4.description: Comparative Cultures: The countries of the Western Hemisphere are diverse and the cultures of these countries are rich and varied. Due to their proximity to each other, the countries of the Western Hemisphere share some of the same concerns and issues.

F676622DB34E4F27AF7D10491728E557.description: Students will use physical, climate, and vegetation maps in combination with population density, land use, and resource distribution maps to discern patterns in human settlement and types of economic activity.

2790DE3228FA46C3BA91C1DA5C0ECCC0.description: Students will create a political map of the Western Hemisphere noting which countries are in which region and a political map of the United States showing the location of the states.

69FF7340EF034CFB834B91EB20B50AB8.description: Students will map the regions within the Western Hemisphere and locate major physical features within each region.

8D9EE04C2E094B8A9475597A1E01E9CB.description: The physical environment influences human population distribution, land use, and other forms of economic activity.

BCB137456C0745968960DEA5DC4B6455.description:
The Western Hemisphere can be divided into regions. Regions are areas that share common identifiable characteristics such as physical, political, economic, or cultural features. Regions within the Western Hemisphere include:
  • North America (Canada and the United States)
  • Mesoamerica (Mexico and Central America)
  • Caribbean
  • South America

F16E7DD11A6C46C3800B01AE6791E602.description: Physical maps reflect the varied climate zones, landforms, bodies of water, and natural resources of the Western Hemisphere.

91770551764048DD8318EFFB52A05ECC.description: Geography in the Western Hemisphere: The diverse geography of the Western Hemisphere has influenced human culture and settlement in distinct ways. Human communities in the Western Hemisphere have modified the physical environment.

F04AFE4D116D4220BAF73BB5E1533725.description: Students will examine the conditions experienced by enslaved Africans during the Middle Passage.

46DCCC2F7186450994263DF63FA551AC.description: Students will investigate why sugar was brought to the Americas, noting where it was grown and why, and the role of supply and demand.

63DD75DE91BD4BE08A71D9095C58676F.description: Africans were captured, brought to the Americas, and sold as slaves. Their transport across the Atlantic was known as the Middle Passage.

1D2329D0FCE848B9905CA3EF2C71A5EA.description: Students will examine the effect of diseases introduced to the Western Hemisphere.

4FB0D13BBCE449CABCBC087FA04B84F6.description: Students will map the movement of people, plants, animals, and disease between Europe, the Americas, and Africa.

95FB434EA96D415FA3CF6908A21FE585.description: The transatlantic trade of goods, movement of people, and spread of ideas and diseases resulted in cultural diffusion. This cultural diffusion became known as the Columbian Exchange which reshaped the lives and influenced the beliefs of people.

7FD948C47F3A4482900F5FDF1C9EA0E0.description:
Students will examine the European interactions with Native Americans using these examples:
  • Conquests by Cortez and Pizarro and the resulting demographic change
  • French in Canada and the fur trade

D32F45CCDB624B29A20636110343E26C.description: Students will examine the how Native Americans viewed the newcomers.

ACA8EABB2E5548DEB9CE89FC08E54DA4.description: Europeans encountered and interacted with Native Americans in a variety of ways.

578DED7E2E684062BEA7EF02E1542DBE.description: Students will map the key areas of the Western Hemisphere colonized by the English, Dutch, French, Portuguese, and Spanish comparing the location, relative size, and key resources of these regions.

20483E5C39DE4588929DFB9F6A0E82A0.description: Students will investigate explorers from different European countries and map the areas of the Western Hemisphere where they explored including Christopher Columbus, John Cabot, Jacques Cartier, Pedro Cabral, and Vasco Nunez de Balboa.

3BC181ABE4E54E36AA1A95033303A5AE.description: Europeans traveled to the Americas in search of new trade routes, including a northwest passage, and resources. They hoped to gain wealth, power, and glory.

0C1F7C89875B4EEE84649EC6443F4522.description: European Exploration and Its Effects: Various European powers explored and eventually colonized the Western Hemisphere. This had a profound impact on Native Americans and led to the transatlantic slave trade.

AAA9BD145CDB4CAEB8103661B1BFD41D.description: Students will compare and contrast political states of the Maya and the Aztec noting the territories they controlled, the type of rule each had, and how the ruler attempted to unify the people.

062D6E04F0E74370AFF9483FC76D05AB.description: Political states can take different forms such as city-states and empires. A city-state is comprised of a city with a government that controls the surrounding territory, while an empire is a political organization developed when a single supreme authority conquers other geographic and/or cultural regions beyond its initial settlements.

F528A6B09AD345CC8BF82DDD70F88211.description: Students will compare how the Mayas, Aztecs, and Incas adapted to and modified their environment to meet the needs of the people, examining the clothing, farming, shelter, and transportation systems for each.

CBE955A5334748DC90C374D52A98AA83.description: Complex societies and civilizations adapted to and modified their environment to meet the needs of their people.

C9AAB4B4034D424E9EAA2A53BDECB5D4.description: Students will investigate the characteristics of the Mayas, Aztecs, and Incas noting similarities and differences.

33620F06404E4B26A96CEE38F30FB9E1.description: Students will locate the complex societies and civilizations of the Mayas, Aztecs, and Incas on a map and when they occurred.

E8EFB921D94C475C823DCA6AD64D6613.description: Civilizations share certain common characteristics of religion, job specialization, cities, government, language and writing systems, technology, and social hierarchy.

AAEF8E5CDEA34FBAAF9EA4FF74D2F82F.description: Complex Societies and Civilizations: Between 1100 B.C.E. and 1500 C.E, complex societies and civilizations developed in the Western Hemisphere. Although these complex societies and civilizations have certain defining characteristics in common, each is also known for unique cultural achievements and contributions.

74302B4823A34DB687F9B8DE866B1583.description: Students will select one Native American culture group from the United States, one from Canada, and one from the Caribbean region and compare and contrast them by examining how each of these groups adapted to and used the environment and its resources to meet their basic needs, and by examining elements of their culture, including customs, beliefs, values, languages, and patterns of organization and governance.

D3BBE74047444A4A8A0CD7414A9F9BEC.description: Students will examine maps that show the variety of different Native American groups located in the Western Hemisphere, noting there are many different culture groups in many different types of physical, climate, and vegetative regions.
comments: For this document, the term "Native American" is used with the understanding it could say "American Indian."

C14ADE825CC446C996250E45D8FF642B.description: Early peoples living together in settlements developed shared cultures with customs, beliefs, values, and languages that give identity to the group. These early peoples also developed patterns of organization and governance to manage their society.

6890566082AC46ACBB4DD6A100A553A7.description: Human populations that settled along rivers, in rainforests, along oceans, in deserts, on plains, in mountains, and in cold climates adapted to and made use of the resources and environment around them in developing distinct ways of life.

D080CD80D18D4AC5ACB05D036F0C7ACC.description: Students will examine the various theories of the migration routes by which the first humans may have arrived, including the Bering land bridge, using maps and archaeological evidence.

FAFF413B1F6D4EC2A8FDF6D4A4B05315.description: Various forms of scientific evidence suggest that humans came to North America approximately 25,000 to 14,000 years ago and spread southward to South America.

E3B20159F99E443BBE47C2785F620A9F.description: Early Peoples of the Americas: The first humans in the Western Hemisphere modified their physical environment as well as adapted to their environment. Their interactions with their environment led to various innovations and to the development of unique cultures.

comments: Grade 5 Social Studies is based on the history and geography of the Western Hemisphere, including the development of cultures, civilizations, and empires; interaction between societies; and the comparison of the government and economic systems of modern nations. It also incorporates elements of archaeology. The course is divided into seven Key Ideas that cover a time span from prehistory into modern times. Teachers are encouraged to make and teach local connections throughout the course, especially in the examination of citizenship related to modern political and economic issues.

3969571AB2C24193B8ABE1FB72F7273D.description: Develop an understanding of the interdependence of individuals and groups in communities in the Western Hemisphere

2CF8A35812FF442594079C9A20436F96.description: Identify rights and responsibilities of citizens within societies in the Western Hemisphere.

A12B2BB0760743769A5C25DEE97C4FF7.description: Describe the roles of people in power in the Western Hemisphere both historically and currently. Identify ways that current figures can influence people's rights and freedom.

6E35EAD41DCB47C5B6F446CB99AB055B.description: Identify situations with a global focus in which social actions are required and suggest solutions.

44649E04A4084299BF542761C345F594.description: Participate in negotiating and compromising in the resolution of differences and conflict.

410AC9DD5F1A49E78D9E84A6BBE8044A.description: Identify opportunities for and the role of the individual in social and political participation at various times and in various locations in the Western Hemisphere outside the United States.

92DE897867D8409C84997494ECC5B0FD.description: Identify different types of political systems and ideologies used at various times and in various locations in the Western Hemisphere and identify the role of individuals and key groups in those political and social systems.

2F0CD79FBBFF48EE824FF177AE1FE4EC.description: Participate in activities that focus on a localized issue or problem in a country other than the United States in the Western Hemisphere.

77358D81EA2F42B5BFD3846FC13A21FF.description: Demonstrate respect for the rights of others in discussion and classroom debates regardless of whether one agrees with the other viewpoint. Consider alternate views in discussion with teacher support.

65B3EA936D154DD08C6C97863D2963F2.description: Describe government decisions that impact economies in case studies from the Western Hemisphere.

E22C5A6AC7104E12B0B7035FA2E65428.description: Explain the meaning of unemployment, inflation, income, and economic growth in the economy.

1168955B742940B99249206FC1042106.description: Examine the role of job specialization and trade historically and during contemporary times in the Western Hemisphere.

5F038E2D89934EB784A10DAD044EAC81.description: Provide examples of how currency makes exchange easier by comparing a barter economy to a currency-based economy; examine why corporations and labor unions have a role in a market economy.

C76F8AD143594D0E80A5CA41F3B5610E.description: Show examples of various types of resources (human capital, physical capital, and natural resources) required to provide goods and services.

4F41DD99B401413FAD07AB06B26348E7.description: Explain how scarcity necessitates decision making; employ examples from the Western Hemisphere to illustrate the role of scarcity historically and in current events.

F241D873D726427A8A81D562D3949E3E.description: Recognize that boundaries and definitions of location are historically constructed.

4CE398645E60421DA1C86AD3DA8A74C0.description: Describe how human activities alter places and regions in the Western Hemisphere.

7074B9890EF04037B32B43EAC1E58B30.description: Recognize and explain how characteristics (cultural, economic, and physical-environmental) of regions affect the history of societies in the Western Hemisphere.

2EDA17C7687F41C8A5EF39E0058AB070.description: Identify and describe how environments affect human activities and how human activities affect physical environments through the study of cases in the Western Hemisphere.

618B9322EE334082943036CA91661567.description: Distinguish human activities and human-made features from "environments" (natural events or physical features—land, air, and water—that are not directly made by humans) in the Western Hemisphere.

076A394904814FBFA13AEF494C5E7BAA.description: Use location terms and use geographic representations such as maps, photographs, satellite images, and models to describe where places in the Western Hemisphere are in relation to each other, to describe connections among places, and to evaluate the benefits of particular places for purposeful activities.

E8696714174E4EBBA3480F221B9C4838.description: Describe historical developments in the history of the Western Hemisphere with specific references to circumstances of time and place and to connections to broader regional or global processes with teacher support.

EC13FDFF08E14985AA688BB6C731C325.description: Identify how the relationship among geography, economics, and history helps to define a context for events in the study of the Western Hemisphere.

815B6609335A415E84B2B391D9910BC2.description: Describe and compare events in the history of the Western Hemisphere in societies in similar chronological contexts and in various geographical contexts.

285711E13F4A40539321378BCE0837AA.description: Categorize divergent perspectives of an individual historical event.

3E404CCBD7944BA186F17176A3D8EBEF.description: Identify a region in the Western Hemisphere by describing a characteristic that places within it have in common, and then compare it to other regions. Understand how regions can be defined as sharing common characteristics in contrast with other regions.

FD3F78AFF19E483A88D94D04992F2A00.description: Understand the role of periodization as a practice in history and social studies.

32864CFA0B7E4224BCD2033D3EE167B3.description: Recognize and identify patterns of continuity and change in history.

EB522F72922D44888CA9443F24528B08.description: Use periods of time such as decades and centuries to organize a historical narrative; compare histories in different places in the Western Hemisphere utilizing timelines.

DBA8D20466E9452CA591CF4BD639025D.description: Recognize the dynamics of historical continuity and change over periods of time. Identify important turning points in history.

E73AC4662F664CC1AEAE8F357F1461D5.description: Distinguish between long-term and immediate causes and effects of an event from current events or history.

54A02C8E104E4B55BAB607FD04063AA1.description: Identify and classify the relationship between multiple causes and multiple effects.

DC3F062D247144EAA8E9F4CE1402B571.description: Identify causes and effects using examples from current events or grade-level content and historical events

C1AD9EF452184FBC8CD3B9B2E7343AED.description: Employ mathematical skills to measure time in years and centuries. Understand the difference between B.C.E. and C.E. Identify the chronological significance of data presented in time lines.

A0FC7DDA3E3446CEBB33924388EA6944.description: Explain how events are related chronologically to one another in time.

87DC8285E44443B89E1F5565BB12C8A2.description: Recognize arguments on specific social studies topics and identify evidence supporting the argument.

41380AD111A849EE8ECE4090F8FB35AD.description: Identify implicit ideas to draw inference with support.

6D08E52040A545E18C08779CA42B6DFA.description: Identify evidence and explain content, authorship, purpose, and format; identify bias; explain the role of bias and potential audience with teacher support.

8F79379D76C848FD800662BDF3D98B52.description: Recognize and effectively select different forms of evidence used to make meaning in social studies (including primary and secondary sources such as art and photographs, artifacts, oral histories, maps, and graphs).

8BEBB63DBF9E48AB9014DECFD134EA37.description: Develop questions to help identify evidence about topics related to the historical events occurring in the Western Hemisphere that can be answered by gathering, using, and interpreting evidence.

document.title: New York State K-8 Social Studies Framework

0431B89E6F3348C6BD040513FD823CBA.description: Students will identify examples of scarcity.

619CA40ADC3D42F684F791965FD2084C.description: Scarcity is the condition of not being able to have all of the goods and services that a person wants or needs.

comments: In kindergarten, students study "Self and Others". The course is organized into five units of study—Individual Development and Cultural Identity; Civic Ideals and Practices; Geography, Humans, and the Environment; Time, Continuity, and Change; and Economic Systems. These units represent five of the unifying themes of social studies and may be presented in any order. Each unit helps students study themselves in the context of their immediate surroundings. Students will learn about similarities and differences between children, families and communities and about holidays, symbols and traditions that unite us as Americans. Students learn about respect for others, and rights and responsibilities of individuals.

E1E23860DFE60131BC4868A86D17958E.description: Review writing with teachers and peers

E1E1E9C0DFE60131BC4768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate effective use of writer's-craft techniques, such as literary devices, when writing

E1E19AE0DFE60131BC4668A86D17958E.description: Adjust style of writing, including voice and language used, according to purpose and audience

E1E14B50DFE60131BC4568A86D17958E.description: Write for a wide variety of audiences

E1E0F940DFE60131BC4468A86D17958E.description: Review writing independently to address editing concerns

E1E09220DFE60131BC4368A86D17958E.description: Review writing independently in order to revise for focus, development of ideas, organization, and language use

E1E01D80DFE60131BC4268A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of prewriting strategies to plan and organize writing

E1DFADB0DFE60131BC4168A86D17958E.description: Use the writing process (e.g., prewriting, drafting, revising, proofreading, and editing)

E1DF57B0DFE60131BC4068A86D17958E.description: Write, using a variety of media such as print and electronic

E1DF01B0DFE60131BC3F68A86D17958E.description: Select an organizational pattern for writing that effectively communicates the topic and purpose of the text to the intended audience

E1DEAED0DFE60131BC3E68A86D17958E.description: Write for a variety of purposes, selecting a form of writing appropriate to the function of the written communication

E1DE5890DFE60131BC3D68A86D17958E.description: Write on a wide range of topics, both student and teacher selected

E1DDFD60DFE60131BC3C68A86D17958E.description: Engage in a variety of writing activities, both student and teacher initiated, in response to listening to literary and informational texts

E1DDA970DFE60131BC3B68A86D17958E.description: Engage in a variety of writing activities, both student and teacher initiated, to respond to the reading of literary and informational texts

E1DD01D0DFE60131BC3968A86D17958E.description: Use legible print and/or cursive writing

E1DC6520DFE60131BC3768A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of spelling resources, such as dictionaries and spell-check tools, to support correct spelling

E1DC1590DFE60131BC3668A86D17958E.description: Correctly spell words within own writing that have been previously studied or that follow previously studied spelling patterns

E1DAAEE0DFE60131BC3268A86D17958E.description: Use dictionaries, thesauruses, and style manuals

E1DA5910DFE60131BC3168A86D17958E.description: Use signal/transitional words (e.g., in addition, for example, finally, as a result, similarly, and on the other hand) to provide clues to organizational format

E1DA0380DFE60131BC3068A86D17958E.description:
Use correct grammatical construction in
  • parts of speech such as nouns; adjectives and adverbs (comparative/superlative); pronouns (indefinite/nominative/objective); conjunctions (coordinating/subordinating); prepositions and prepositional phrases; and interjections
  • simple/compound/complex sentences, using, correct subject-verb agreement, verb tense, punctuation, and pronouns with clear antecedents

E1D9A870DFE60131BC2F68A86D17958E.description:
Observe the rules of punctuation, capitalization, and spelling, such as
  • punctuation of compound sentences, friendly/business letters, simple dialogue, and exact words from sources (quotations); use italics/underlining for titles
  • capitalization of proper nouns such as key words in literary and/or book titles, languages, and historical events
  • spelling of commonly misspelled words, homonyms, and content-area vocabulary

E1D95630DFE60131BC2E68A86D17958E.description: Use teacher conferences and peer review to revise written work

E1D8FFB0DFE60131BC2D68A86D17958E.description: Use the writing process (e.g., prewriting, drafting, revising, proofreading, and editing)

E1D8A540DFE60131BC2C68A86D17958E.description: Use prewriting activities (e.g., brainstorming, note taking, freewriting, outlining, and paragraphing)

E1D83320DFE60131BC2B68A86D17958E.description: Use tone and language appropriate for audience and purpose

E1D7D050DFE60131BC2A68A86D17958E.description: Determine the intended audience before writing

E1D78000DFE60131BC2968A86D17958E.description: Understand the purpose for writing; the purpose may be to explain, describe, narrate, persuade, or express feelings

E1D66D80DFE60131BC2668A86D17958E.description: Recognize the types of language (e.g., jargon, colloquialisms, informal vocabulary, and email conventions) that are appropriate to social communication

E1D60E20DFE60131BC2568A86D17958E.description: Respect the age, gender, position, and cultural traditions of the writer

E1D5B2E0DFE60131BC2468A86D17958E.description: Share reading experiences to build a relationship with peers or adults; for example, read together silently or aloud with a partner or in small groups

E1D55DD0DFE60131BC2368A86D17958E.description: Students will read, write, listen, and speak for social interaction.

E1D50D70DFE60131BC2268A86D17958E.description:
Evaluate, with assistance, the validity and accuracy of information, ideas, themes, opinions, and experiences in text to
  • identify conflicting information
  • consider the background and qualifications of the writer
  • evaluate examples, details, or reasons used to support ideas
  • identify differing points of view in texts and presentations
  • identify cultural and ethnic values and their impact on content, with assistance
  • identify multiple levels of meaning

E1D4B610DFE60131BC2168A86D17958E.description: Recognize how one's own point of view contributes to forming an opinion about information and ideas

E1D46510DFE60131BC2068A86D17958E.description: Identify different perspectives, such as social, cultural, ethnic, and historical, on an issue presented in one or more than one text

E1D41080DFE60131BC1F68A86D17958E.description: Use established and personal criteria to analyze and evaluate the quality of ideas and information in text

E1D3BA40DFE60131BC1E68A86D17958E.description:
Evaluate information, ideas, opinions, and themes by identifying
  • a central idea and supporting details
  • precise and vague language
  • statements of fact, opinion, and exaggeration
  • missing or unclear information

E1D364F0DFE60131BC1D68A86D17958E.description: Students will read, write, listen, and speak for critical analysis and evaluation.

E1D305D0DFE60131BC1C68A86D17958E.description: Identify social and cultural context and other characteristics of the time period to enhance understanding and appreciation of text, with assistance

E1D26550DFE60131BC1B68A86D17958E.description: Identify poetic elements, such as repetition, rhythm, and rhyming patterns, in order to interpret poetry, with assistance

E1D20D90DFE60131BC1A68A86D17958E.description: Recognize how the author's use of language creates images or feelings, with assistance

E1D1B920DFE60131BC1968A86D17958E.description: Determine how the use and meaning of literary devices, such as symbolism, metaphor and simile, alliteration, personification, flashback, and foreshadowing, convey the author's message or intent, with assistance

E1D15DC0DFE60131BC1868A86D17958E.description: Identify the author's point of view, such as first-person narrator and omniscient narrator, with assistance

E1D10C40DFE60131BC1768A86D17958E.description: Interpret characters, plot, setting, and theme, using evidence from the text, with assistance

E1D0BC00DFE60131BC1668A86D17958E.description: Identify the ways in which characters change and develop throughout a story

E1D06870DFE60131BC1568A86D17958E.description: Recognize how different authors treat similar themes

E1D014B0DFE60131BC1468A86D17958E.description: Recognize how the author uses literary devices, such as simile, metaphor, and personification, to create meaning

E1CFBAB0DFE60131BC1368A86D17958E.description: Identify literary elements, (e.g., setting, plot, character, rhythm, and rhyme) of different genres

E1CF6060DFE60131BC1268A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the same story can be told in different genres (e.g., novels, poems, or plays)

E1CF0FB0DFE60131BC1168A86D17958E.description:
Read aloud from a variety of genres (e.g., plays and poems)
  • use inflection and intonation appropriate to text read and audience

E1CEAE60DFE60131BC1068A86D17958E.description: Select literary texts on the basis of personal needs and interests and read silently for enjoyment for extended periods

E1CDEC50DFE60131BC0E68A86D17958E.description: Read, view, and interpret texts from a variety of genres

E1CD8730DFE60131BC0D68A86D17958E.description: Students will read, write, listen, and speak for literary response and expression.

E1CD2E50DFE60131BC0C68A86D17958E.description: Make, confirm, or revise predictions, with assistance

E1CCC7B0DFE60131BC0B68A86D17958E.description: Draw conclusions and make inferences on the basis of explicit and implied information, with assistance

E1CC6F60DFE60131BC0A68A86D17958E.description: Condense, combine, or categorize new information from one or more sources, with assistance

E1CC1C10DFE60131BC0968A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of structure, content, and vocabulary to understand informational texts, with assistance

E1CBC360DFE60131BC0868A86D17958E.description: Apply thinking skills, such as define, classify, and infer, to interpret data, facts, and ideas from informational texts, with assistance

E1CB6A60DFE60131BC0768A86D17958E.description: Identify main ideas and supporting details in informational texts to distinguish relevant and irrelevant information

E1CB0F70DFE60131BC0668A86D17958E.description: Recognize how new information is related to prior knowledge or experience

E1CAC020DFE60131BC0568A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast information about one topic from multiple sources

E1CA6E30DFE60131BC0468A86D17958E.description: Identify information that is implied rather than stated

E1C9BBF0DFE60131BC0268A86D17958E.description: Identify missing, conflicting, unclear, and irrelevant information

E1C958B0DFE60131BC0168A86D17958E.description: Recognize organizational formats to assist in comprehension of informational texts

E1C8F510DFE60131BC0068A86D17958E.description: Use text features, such as headings, captions, and titles, to understand and interpret informational texts

E1C88F30DFE60131BBFF68A86D17958E.description: Skim material to gain an overview of content or locate specific information

E1C83760DFE60131BBFE68A86D17958E.description: Read the steps of a procedure in order to accomplish a task such as completing a science experiment or installing software

E1C7E690DFE60131BBFD68A86D17958E.description: Read to collect and interpret data, facts, and ideas from multiple sources

E1C791F0DFE60131BBFC68A86D17958E.description: Use the table of contents and indexes to locate information

E1C73A90DFE60131BBFB68A86D17958E.description: Locate and use school and public library resources, with some direction, to acquire information

E1C6E7E0DFE60131BBFA68A86D17958E.description: Students will read, write, listen, and speak for information and understanding.

E1C63C30DFE60131BBF868A86D17958E.description: Recognize at sight a large body of high-frequency words and specialized content vocabulary

E1C5ED40DFE60131BBF768A86D17958E.description: Use word recognition skills and strategies quickly, accurately, and automatically when decoding unfamiliar words

E1C59D30DFE60131BBF668A86D17958E.description: Integrate sources of information to decode unfamiliar words, self-monitor, and self-correct for word-reading accuracy

E1C54BF0DFE60131BBF568A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of a variety of decoding strategies, such as letter-sound correspondence, syllable patterns, decoding by analogy, word structure, use of syntactic (grammar) cues, and use of semantic (meaning) cues, to read unfamiliar words

E1C49A20DFE60131BBF368A86D17958E.description: Engage in independent silent reading for extended periods of time

E1C44830DFE60131BBF268A86D17958E.description: Be familiar with titles and authors of a wide range of literature

E1C3F0C0DFE60131BBF168A86D17958E.description: Read voluntarily for a variety of purposes

E1C38AA0DFE60131BBF068A86D17958E.description: Show interest in reading a wide range of texts, topics, genres, and authors

E1C2C760DFE60131BBEE68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate personal response to grade-level texts through a range of responses, such as writing, drama, and oral presentations

E1C270F0DFE60131BBED68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate comprehension of grade-level texts through a range of responses, such as writing, drama, and presentations

E1C21A60DFE60131BBEC68A86D17958E.description: Participate cooperatively and collaboratively in group discussions of texts

E1C1A4E0DFE60131BBEB68A86D17958E.description: Note and describe aspects of the writer's craft, and explain the role that crafting techniques play in helping the reader comprehend the text

E1C132A0DFE60131BBEA68A86D17958E.description: Use prior knowledge, along with multiple sources of information, to support comprehension, from forming predictions to making inferences and drawing conclusions

E1C0CF30DFE60131BBE968A86D17958E.description: Read grade-level texts and answer literal, inferential, analytic, and evaluative questions

E1C06C40DFE60131BBE868A86D17958E.description: Present a point of view or interpretation of a text, such as its theme or the author's intended message, and support it with relevant details from the text

E1C016A0DFE60131BBE768A86D17958E.description: State or summarize a main idea and support it or elaborate on it with relevant details

E1BFC530DFE60131BBE668A86D17958E.description: Make connections between texts being read to own lives, the lives of others, other texts read in the past, and the world at large

E1BF6640DFE60131BBE568A86D17958E.description: Ask questions to self-monitor comprehension, to clarify understanding, and to focus reading

E1BEF0A0DFE60131BBE468A86D17958E.description: Employ self-monitoring strategies and engage in self-correcting behaviors when comprehension has been disrupted

E1BE6DF0DFE60131BBE368A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of strategies (e.g., summarizing, forming questions, visualizing, and making connections) to support understanding of texts read

E1BDF980DFE60131BBE268A86D17958E.description: Read grade-level texts from a variety of genres, in varying text formats and by different authors, for a variety of purposes

E1BD4410DFE60131BBE068A86D17958E.description: Use a thesaurus to identify synonyms and antonyms

E1BCEFC0DFE60131BBDF68A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of unfamiliar words by using context, dictionaries, glossaries, and other print resources, including electronic resources

E1BC99D0DFE60131BBDE68A86D17958E.description: Use self-monitoring strategies to identify specific vocabulary difficulties that disrupt comprehension, and employ an efficient course of action, such as using a known word base or a resource such as a glossary to resolve the difficulty

E1BC3D50DFE60131BBDD68A86D17958E.description: Acquire new vocabulary by engaging with a variety of texts written by a range of different authors

E1BBC6E0DFE60131BBDC68A86D17958E.description: Use prior knowledge and experience in order to understand ideas and vocabulary found in a variety of texts

E1BB6FD0DFE60131BBDB68A86D17958E.description: Use word structure knowledge, such as roots (e.g., Greek and Latin), prefixes, and suffixes, to determine word meaning

E1BB1EE0DFE60131BBDA68A86D17958E.description: Extend knowledge of word meaning through direct and indirect means

E1BA1E70DFE60131BBD768A86D17958E.description: Maintain a personal reading list to reflect reading goals and accomplishments

E1B9C3B0DFE60131BBD668A86D17958E.description: Read aloud, using inflection and intonation appropriate to text read and to audience

E1B96DF0DFE60131BBD568A86D17958E.description: Apply corrective strategies (e.g., rereading and discussion with teachers, peers, or parents/caregivers) to assist in comprehension

E1B91BC0DFE60131BBD468A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of punctuation to assist in comprehension

E1B8C2E0DFE60131BBD368A86D17958E.description: Identify signal words, such as finally or in addition, that provide clues to organizational formats such as time order

E1B86810DFE60131BBD268A86D17958E.description: Determine the meaning of unfamiliar words by using context clues, a dictionary, or a glossary

E1B80B80DFE60131BBD168A86D17958E.description: Use word recognition and context clues to read fluently

E1B7B4B0DFE60131BBD068A86D17958E.description: Adjust reading rate according to purpose for reading

document.title: New York State 9-12 Social Studies Framework

4F178A664CE74611A8917D072FA845BE.description: Students will examine the economic relationship and the strategic rivalry between the United States and China.

64E5ADBFD8194F7389A988B4A2568AEB.description: Students will investigate the role of multinational corporations and their influence on both the United States economy and on other countries around the world.

22CB3C22072D4BA08CFD54C27EC3A9BF.description: Students will examine the positive and negative consequences of globalization in relation to the United States economy.

93358D3E1B154D43A184DDC727007C71.description: Globalization and advances in technology have affected the United States economy and society.

7E5536BC21354A5FA7F8EFCE0299EBCD.description: Students will evaluate the USA PATRIOT Act, including constitutional issues raised about the violation of civil liberties by the federal government's electronic surveillance programs.

60C15D375DC044FF8537F931F2D9E481.description: Students will examine the decision to invade Iraq based on allegations concerning weapons of mass destruction and trace the course of the war.

106609A2537541108C62DE8938B0538D.description: Students will trace the reactions to the September 11, 2001, attacks, including responses of the American public, the authorization of the War on Terror, the invasion of Afghanistan, and the passage of the USA PATRIOT Act.

8CC57E5DC4534FC99300D131F8AAAA96.description: In response to the terrorist attacks of September 11, 2001, the United States launched the War on Terror which involved controversial foreign and domestic policies.

D8F71E4D68E44C4B83F46F30BA83F66F.description: Students will trace United States foreign policy regarding Bosnia, Rwanda, and Kosovo, exploring the tension between defending human rights and the reluctance to intervene stemming from the Vietnam syndrome.

6A31EFE0540846448FF46F0047E31817.description: Students will examine the decision of President George H. W. Bush to oppose Iraq's invasion of Kuwait. Students will evaluate the positive and negative consequences of the Persian Gulf War.

28D45757C0F440E98FA03E8D28F2B7D7.description: The United States created a coalition to defeat Iraq in the Persian Gulf War (1991), but was reluctant to commit American military power through the rest of the decade.

1B92B2B890F4422D8374EA93B16F0D95.description: The United States in a Globalizing World (1990 – present) The United States' political and economic status in the world has faced external and internal challenges related to international conflicts, economic competition, and globalization. Throughout this time period, the nation has continued to debate and define its role in the world.

695567E55EB44E888D7EA508C7E3C502.description: Students will examine the debates over the role of the government in providing a social safety net including the stability of the Social Security Trust Fund and Medicare Trust Fund, as well as changes under the Affordable Care Act.

ABECFC7636734570B18D18FF80CF9DE3.description: Students will examine the causes of the financial panic of 2008 and the federal government's response to the Great Recession.

08BC8D2967EB4D4EAC42FF6D0FD603E3.description: Students will compare and contrast the economic policies of President Johnson (Great Society) and President Reagan (Reaganomics) regarding the size and role of the federal government.

C514FAB9055F41FB996D0BB2F3E58A3B.description: Varying political philosophies prompted debates over the role of the federal government in regulating the economy and providing a social safety net.

CF97F726BAEF45918E463BA2BD35A445.description: Students will thoroughly investigate at least one of the efforts above.

620B4E388BB64B379257F6C46EBAF296.description:
Students will trace the following efforts in terms of issues/goals, key individuals and groups, and successes/limitations:
  • Modern women's movement (e.g., The Feminine Mystique [1963], National Organization for Women , Equal Pay Act and Title IX, Roe v. Wade)
  • Native Americans (e.g., American Indian Movement, Russell Means, native identity and land claims)
  • Brown Power (Chicano) movement (e.g., Cesar Chavez, United Farm Workers)
  • People with disabilities (e.g. Individuals with Disabilities Education Act [1975], Americans with Disabilities Act [1990] )
  • Rights of accused (e.g., Mapp v. Ohio [1961], Gideon v. Wainwright [1963], Miranda v. Arizona [1966])
  • Immigration (e.g., Immigration Act of 1965, Immigration Act of 1986, continuing debates over immigration reform)
  • Gay Rights and the LGBT movement (e.g., Stonewall Inn riots [1969], efforts for equal legal rights)
  • Environment (e.g., Silent Spring [1962], Clean Air Act of 1970, Clean Water Act of 1972, Endangered Species Act of 1973, Environmental Protection Agency [1970], Reagan's policy)
  • Student rights (e.g., Engel v. Vitale [1962], Tinker v. Des Moines School District [1969], New Jersey v. TLO [1985])

499F965DB3CF40CE9A3C9552B37098B1.description: Individuals, diverse groups, and organizations have sought to bring about change in American society through a variety of methods.

463CF8F93BC14ED3810BBEFB528DC467.description: Students will analyze the significance of key events in the movement including the Montgomery bus boycott, federal intervention at Little Rock, Arkansas, the Birmingham protest, and the March on Washington.

E2D638491E0C42898283C2C72AE4D06B.description: Students will examine judicial actions and legislative achievements during the movement such as Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka (1954), the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Heart of Atlanta Motel, Inc. v. United States (1964) and Voting Rights Act of 1965.

D8D29BEC1D324B6BADF0420950224509.description: Students will examine the role of groups such as the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP), Southern Christian Leadership Conference (SCLC), and Student Non-Violent Coordinating Committee (SNCC) in the movement, their goals and strategies, and major contributions.

C143437AB52D42B5823F18F872E1C06A.description: Students will examine the role and impact of individuals such as Rev. Martin Luther King Jr., Stokely Carmichael, Fannie Lou Hamer, and Malcolm X in the movement and their perspectives on change.

2659BBC29B48493AACA301177C2E7E5E.description: After World War II, long-term demands for equality by African Americans led to the civil rights movement. The efforts of individuals, groups, and institutions helped to redefine African American civil rights, though numerous issues remain unresolved.

2DE9BF246E9E48E48228D34AE629B202.description: Social and Economic Change/Domestic Issues (1945 – present): Racial, gender, and socioeconomic inequalities were addressed by individuals, groups, and organizations. Varying political philosophies prompted debates over the role of the federal government in regulating the economy and providing a social safety net.

4FEA4C58ED9548508543B044B5FC30A0.description: Students will trace factors leading to the fall of the Berlin Wall and the end of the Cold War, including American policies, Soviet economic problems, Soviet efforts at reform, and the loss of Soviet control over Eastern Europe.

6EB18EA78CD841268B780AF63B773CF5.description: A combination of factors contributed to the end of the Cold War including American policies and Soviet economic and political problems that led to the loss of Soviet control over Eastern Europe.

0AAE58CAE66C4AA783F634B9907E1344.description: Students will examine United States foreign policy toward the Middle East, including the recognition of and support for the State of Israel, the Camp David Accords, and the interaction with radical groups in the region.

41B238C9B9CF49588980E5F8CB44CB1B.description: American strategic interests in the Middle East grew with the Cold War, the creation of the State of Israel, and the increased United States dependence on Middle Eastern oil. The continuing nature of the Arab-Israeli dispute has helped define the contours of American policy in the Middle East.

C9FF9F92F41C48DDB1F7F6DE358D475B.description: Students will examine the policy of détente and its effect on the nuclear arms race.

21C00D01233E44C69B1B4AEDB39FB287.description: Students will examine Soviet motives for placing missiles in Cuba and the impact of the Cuban missile crisis on Soviet-American relations leading to the adoption of the Nuclear Test Ban Treaty.

DD912F395051409FB63CEE51820A6905.description: Students will trace the acceleration of the nuclear arms race from the detonation of an atomic bomb by the Soviet Union in 1949 through 1969, including the effect of Sputnik and the Space Race.

C33A742032E54851AA53A87A688F54CA.description: The United States and the Soviet Union engaged in a nuclear arms race that eventually led to agreements that limited the arms buildup and improved United States-Soviet relations.

67DF522761984973A9F34DACDA1B72C5.description: Students will examine the congressional effort to limit presidential power through the War Powers Act.

A005AB5EFAC049279C41010D48BFDD06.description: Students will examine reasons for declining public confidence in government, including America's involvement in Vietnam, student protests, the growing antiwar movement, and the Watergate affair.

5A1264B2F21E4E1EA79EA2B5D224CFCC.description: Students will trace the United States involvement in Vietnam, including President Johnson's decision to escalate the fighting in Vietnam.

E99A0A80225044CCA561F2A0AA125E5F.description: Students will examine the impact of Truman's decision to fight a limited war in defense of South Korea.

99A558376FDD45D0B483110D5AA5E441.description: Students will examine domestic concerns about the spread of communism and the rise of McCarthyism.

051D5F13A86E4915AD4D544CF603BBF4.description: Students will trace United States containment policies including the Truman Doctrine (1947), the Marshall Plan (1948), and the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (1949), and actions taken during the Berlin blockade, and consider how they represent a shift in American foreign policy.

6033CD64C1914D3CB29558AC6F668F79.description: Students will trace key decisions made at wartime conferences as they applied to Poland, Eastern Europe, and postwar Germany, and note how continuing disagreements over these decisions helped bring about the start of the Cold War.

C9AF0653322940C587B1C764F152143F.description: After World War II, ideological differences led to political tensions between the United States and the Soviet Union. In an attempt to halt the spread of Soviet influence, the United States pursued a policy of containment.

D5E9B8C9F8FE44FD914C6194E21DD8E9.description: Cold War (1945 – 1990): In the period following World War II, the United States entered into an extended era of international conflict called the Cold War which influenced foreign and domestic policy for more than 40 years.

FCFE94E33E1442D2828E933DDB24B676.description: Students will investigate the role of Eleanor Roosevelt in creating the United Nations Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

0B9A98A4511A42C2A02262B5D8895F6E.description: Students will examine the contributions of Supreme Court Justice Robert Jackson and his arguments made as Chief Prosecutor for the United States at the Nuremberg War Crimes trials.

C1F454FDF76E4E04A00A502DFE1A9386.description: Students will investigate American officials' knowledge of the Holocaust, evaluating the degree to which intervention may have been possible.

BC72AB1BED164C1F82A6D0D1E92B97DB.description: In response to World War II and the Holocaust, the United States played a major role in efforts to prevent such human suffering in the future.

5B8D9B72443544FAAC9212AA79B9221C.description: Students will examine the contributions of women, African Americans, Native Americans, Asian Americans, Mexican workers, and Mexican Americans to the war effort, as well as the discrimination they experienced in the military and workforce.

556A54F0CA1B4E19A6B090E92FC1B4BF.description: Students will examine the reasons for President Roosevelt's executive order for Japanese removal, the impact of removal on Japanese people living in the United States, and the Supreme Court's decision in Korematsu v. United States (1944).

E203FAB97EBD4229A59C55544D46CCAE.description: Students will examine United States mobilization efforts and wartime production and their effects on unemployment rates.

B5C9E9D534B44B2DB514BC62BCFEFF0A.description: United States entry into World War II had a significant impact on American society.

61D46F1754264B0EB9A4EAF12830355F.description: Students will examine how technological advancements altered the nature of war and the extent of its devastation, including the use of air power over civilian targets and President Truman's decision to use the atomic bomb against the Japanese cities of Hiroshima and Nagasaki.

A4C41D0ECB854FA4B3EA80E4F4FEB886.description: Students will examine President Roosevelt's leadership during World War II, including his role as commander in chief and his diplomatic efforts to maintain the Grand Alliance.

8831B26E6F5A4BB0BB30DBB6CD72273F.description: Students will examine the impact of the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor.

366177EB0E0A41C2A2C485AF0DA137B5.description: Students will trace ongoing negotiations with Japan and United States efforts to stop Japanese aggression without resorting to war and without appeasing Japanese demands.

D4BF994F4EF246E0818710F349858D10.description: Students will examine reasons for the passage of the Neutrality Acts (1935–1937) and consider the national debate as a shift to pro-Allied policies including "cash and carry" and Lend-Lease.

5F012245D3AD404187DD566C988474CC.description: As situations overseas deteriorated, President Roosevelt's leadership helped move the nation from a policy of neutrality to a pro-Allied position and ultimately direct involvement in the war.

C1DD847E5F374E7FA50548359B3773DC.description: World War II (1935 – 1945): The participation of the United States in World War II was a transformative event for the nation and its role in the world.

795B1FA10D364623A8620F3F27C25051.description: Students will evaluate President Roosevelt's leadership during the Depression including key legislative initiatives of the New Deal, expansion of federal government power, and the constitutional challenge represented by his Court packing effort.

2FE9A4E2511F44809C9D68D6740FF74B.description: Students will examine the human and environmental causes of the Dust Bowl and its effects.

E3698D314EEB41B99CA1AB661E4E2B69.description: Students will compare and contrast the responses of Presidents Herbert Hoover and Franklin Roosevelt to the Great Depression.

F360F0E9CC49444C8ED04BD1A714FA7B.description: Students will examine the underlying weaknesses of the economy that led to the stock market crash of 1929 and the Great Depression.

76FA971CA7FE485DA6C5C1098359EA27.description: Students will examine the reasons for economic prosperity during the 1920s.

304347746F8241C99F678D800970B300.description: For many Americans, the 1920s was a time of prosperity. However, underlying economic problems reflected by the stock market crash of 1929 led to the Great Depression. President Franklin D. Roosevelt's responses to the Great Depression increased the role of the federal government.

66AF00BDA7E44FD7930A7B57AD041A2D.description: Students will examine the rise of African American racial pride and Black Nationalism including the role of Marcus Garvey.

DDACE1D1ACE3462C869F9964EA3C15C4.description: Students will examine literary and artistic contributions associated with the Harlem Renaissance and its impact on national culture.

B448EF902EC547678706183419533A02.description: African Americans continued to struggle for social and economic equality while expanding their own thriving and unique culture. African American cultural achievements were increasingly integrated into national culture.

EC1C8A652AA348ED913B0AEEFDD34303.description: Students will examine the key issues related to the Scopes trial.

0DD0C4EC309444088C93D56C43AB5D1C.description: Students will examine the reasons for the resurgence of the Ku Klux Klan.

6908C02B3C2D414D8FF00F8C80247DE4.description: Students will examine change in immigration policy as reflected by passage of the Quota Acts of the 1920s.

C9BAC29DE5AD473E9A66D7A1F6808DFD.description: Students will examine the impact of Prohibition on American society.

31F531EF88634C3289AC9EA602F870C9.description: Students will examine the cultural trends associated with the Roaring Twenties, including women's efforts at self-expression and their changing roles.

525976BDC90F463FB2AFE6B9E8F2C024.description: The 1920s was a time of cultural change in the country, characterized by clashes between modern and traditional values.

52F494120CE944E7B6A69E2C3994FB41.description: Prosperity and Depression (1920 – 1939): The 1920s and 1930s were a time of cultural and economic changes in the nation. During this period the nation faced significant domestic challenges including the Great Depression.

AECFAE31F46E4DDFB9EF354AEE1D2667.description: Students will examine the relationship between postwar recession, fear of radicals, xenophobia, and the Red Scare (1919–1921).

3C7DB6781D7948F6BAA132BC7F364B28.description: Students will examine the Supreme Court decision concerning civil liberties in Schenck v. United States (1919).

2DC72B70EB1D4FC9BEDCEF963601F93A.description: Students will investigate the causes and effects of the Great Migration on American society.

A4B7DED1211C4FC7B1D8738201FEE62A.description: Students will investigate the effects of mobilization on the United States economy, including the role and contributions of women and African Americans in the war effort.

E6EBCB702415481E8369830BB61062B3.description: World War I had important social, political, and economic effects on American society.

09A6D6EAE13C4633B251B8CAADA7A365.description: Students will examine reasons President Wilson was unsuccessful in gaining support for Senate ratification of the Treaty of Versailles.

B13C984CC7BE4ACFBC7D804E1F85EAB1.description: Students will examine Wilson's goals as expressed in the Fourteen Points, his role at the Versailles Peace Conference, and the compromises he was forced to make to gain approval for the League of Nations.

206936F0E44349589869A1ACAD9C529E.description: Students will investigate the reasons for President Wilson's shift from neutrality to involvement in World War I.

D77E162A05E44C69B40EFA8FC378708D.description: While the United States attempted to follow its traditional policy of neutrality at the beginning of World War I, the nation eventually became involved in the war. President Woodrow Wilson led the nation into war with the hope of reforming the international order through his Fourteen Points.

9B60CB3B160C4E0F8A9BDD8895F92E20.description: Students will investigate expanding American influence in the Caribbean and Latin America through the creation of the Panama Canal and the Roosevelt Corollary.

61DA11574B824C588F2556DFBEB28646.description: Students will examine debates between anti-imperialists and imperialists surrounding ratification of the Treaty of Paris of 1898 and annexation of the Philippines.

B9F69998448F474C8CAD8C327EEE5A27.description: Students will investigate the causes and effects of the Spanish-American War, evaluating Spanish, Cuban, and United States interests and actions.

F62A6D77962A44AFA434A7C4822BA513.description: Students will examine factors such as the economic and strategic interests that led the United States to seek foreign markets, resources, and coaling stations, including interest in Hawaii.

BDE348E949C24D88B48123D9587552FD.description: In the late 1800s, various strategic and economic factors led to a greater focus on foreign affairs and debates over the United States' role in the world.

D1B9C8E304584D8DB2F59F9F5FDAB436.description: The Rise of American Power (1890 – 1920): Numerous factors contributed to the rise of the United States as a world power. Debates over the United States' role in world affairs increased in response to overseas expansion and involvement in World War I. United States participation in the war had important effects on American society.

70A3512017F742F49FC0D9236A71268B.description:
Students will trace reform efforts by individuals and the consequences of those efforts including:
  • Jane Addams and Hull House
  • Jacob Riis' How the Other Half Lives
  • New York Governor Theodore Roosevelt and the Tenement Reform Commission
  • Upton Sinclair's The Jungle and the Meat Inspection Act
  • Margaret Sanger and birth control
  • Ida Tarbell's The History of the Standard Oil Company
  • Ida Wells and her writings about lynching of African Americans
  • Booker T. Washington's contributions to education, including Tuskegee Institute
  • W. E. B. Du Bois and the founding of the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP), the publication of The Crisis and the Silent Protest (1917)

871B7E817CA14D988F1CD864492F15F1.description: Students will trace the temperance and prohibition movements leading to the ratification of the 18th amendment (1919).

3E8CF3C9F28F449E9795D48848EA5CCF.description: Students will examine the efforts of the woman's suffrage movement after 1900, leading to ratification of the 19th amendment (1920).

C95DD0A5C5BE437F82A4FDC405740456.description: Students will examine Progressive Era reforms, such as the 16th and 17th amendments (1913) and the establishment of the Federal Reserve System (1913).

FDE0BA7DF2084E03B962148E2C9DB2F9.description: Students will examine the attempts of workers to unionize from 1870 to 1920 in response to industrial working conditions, including the Knights of Labor, the American Federation of Labor, the American Railway Union, the International Ladies Garment Workers' Union, and the International Workers of the World, considering actions taken by the unions and the response to these actions.

D6A82EAA2674482B998B906DF33B3DAD.description: Students will examine problems faced by farmers between 1870 and 1900 and examine the goals and achievements of the Grange Movement and the Populist Party.

85E80866865F417BA8AAF5E7689FF182.description: Students will examine demographic trends associated with urbanization and immigration between 1840 and 1920, including push-pull factors regarding Irish immigration and immigration from southern and eastern Europe.

81BE728D346B44F69FD7B25D357D5526.description: Rapid industrialization and urbanization created significant challenges and societal problems addressed by a variety of reform efforts.

FBCACA8D277A4388BF2EA42D3EDE2F37.description: Students will evaluate the effectiveness of state and federal attempts to regulate business, by examining the Supreme Court decision in Wabash, St. Louis & Pacific R.R. v. Illinois (1886), the Interstate Commerce Act (1887), the Sherman Antitrust Act (1890), and President Theodore Roosevelt's trust-busting role as evidenced in Northern Securities Co. v. United States (1904).

7AA09200296A4F19B36C5D1776B5A0B4.description: Students will examine the growth of industries under the leadership of businessmen such as John D. Rockefeller, Andrew Carnegie, J.P. Morgan, and Henry Ford and analyze their business practices and organizational structures.

FC6C8B38639D4DFB9CBD4DD2C56067D1.description: Students will examine the technological innovations that facilitated industrialization considering energy sources, natural resources, transportation, and communication.

48AEE31D124C403D82EE3990078462AE.description: New technologies and economic models created rapid industrial growth and transformed the United States.

C74E54D8E5554AE3852D6AB9164D85F5.description: Industrialization and Urbanization (1870 – 1920): The United States was transformed from an agrarian to an increasingly industrial and urbanized society. Although this transformation created new economic opportunities, it also created societal problems that were addressed by a variety of reform efforts.

AD867D33F4ED483CA21CDC4AA1189951.description: Students will examine the contributions of Chinese to the national economy and reasons for nativist opposition to their continued immigration (Chinese Exclusion Act of 1882).

0E901ECF7C5B47E6B610C5B8D271851E.description: Students will analyze relevant provisions of the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo as compared with the actual treatment of Mexicans and Mexican Americans in the Southwest, including California, from 1848 to 1900.

87E6886C2019478399B83015A38A3323.description: Racial and economic motives contributed to long-standing discrimination against Mexican Americans and opposition to Chinese immigration.

02FD240BC38744D5B3E093847D3B0582.description: Students will examine the effect of federal policies on Native Americans on the Great Plains including reservation policies, the Dawes Act (1887), and forced acculturation efforts (Carlisle Indian School).

3EF07BC289D845AB8D29347987424178.description: Students will examine the economic impacts of the Homestead Act (1862) and the Pacific Railway Act (1862) on westward expansion.

A57616F710464396AF1CCDC2D391AD25.description: Federal policies regarding westward expansion had positive effects on the national economy but negative consequences for Native Americans.

E13E372657844946979C1BE298D71981.description: Students will examine the exclusion of women from the 14th and 15th amendments and the subsequent struggle for voting and increased property rights in the late 19th century, including the work of Susan B. Anthony.

D2387EC48125400B9DA238D3456EE835.description: The 14th and 15th amendments failed to address the rights of women.

01C310205FDA430980F478C45ADDDDD3.description: Students will examine the impact of the election of 1876 and the compromise of 1877on African Americans.

CF3AF08BEF834553AC66B8004B114CA0.description: Students will examine the ways in which freedmen attempted to build independent lives including activities of the Freedmen's Bureau, creation of educational institutions, and political participation.

76669A128E0A47BBACDB79CC1DEC8587.description: Students will investigate the ways individuals, groups, and government institutions limited the rights of African Americans, including the use of Black Codes, the passage of Jim Crow laws, the Ku Klux Klan, restrictions on voting rights, and Supreme Court cases including the Civil Rights Cases (1883) and Plessy v. Ferguson (1896).

81A7EBEBEE1B4C468BA8101EC0797309.description: Students will examine the 13th, 14th, and 15th amendments and consider the role of Radical Republicans in Reconstruction.

616B4E73D18D4E7CB133A68808B6196F.description: Between 1865 and 1900, constitutional rights were extended to African Americans. However, their ability to exercise these rights was undermined by individuals, groups, and government institutions.

1591D481145740AB9F966AD86961AEAE.description: Post-Civil War Era (1865 – 1900): Reconstruction resulted in political reunion and expanded constitutional rights. However, those rights were undermined and issues of inequality continued for African Americans, women, Native Americans, Mexican Americans, and Chinese immigrants.

80D4746649A241CFA7E3BE8D64A8AA9B.description: Students will analyze the ideas expressed in the Gettysburg Address, considering its long-term impact.

2027D951738D4CBBB56278DE77881ACA.description: Students will examine the expansion of executive and federal power as they relate to the suspension of habeas corpus within the Union and the issuance of the Emancipation Proclamation.

EE014F4960B84CCE952518CFEABDEC46.description: Students will compare the relative strengths of the Union and the Confederacy in terms of industrial capacity, transportation facilities, and military leadership, and evaluate the reasons the North prevailed over the South and the impact of the war.

C394A171D833451A9B0A7F14331E8EED.description: Long-standing disputes over States rights and slavery and the secession of Southern states from the Union sparked by the election of Abraham Lincoln led to the Civil War. After the issuance of the Emancipation Proclamation, freeing the slaves became a major Union goal. The Civil War resulted in tremendous human loss and physical destruction.

973CF2168764454D98F6BC0D7261425E.description: Students will examine the issues surrounding the expansion of slavery into new territories, by exploring the Missouri Compromise, Manifest Destiny, Texas and the Mexican-American war, the Compromise of 1850, the Kansas-Nebraska Act, the Dred Scott decision, and John Brown's raid.

2DEC175156904DA2A967FA882797D965.description: Students will examine the emergence of the women's rights movement out of the abolitionist movement, including the role of the Grimké sisters, Lucretia Mott, and Elizabeth Cady Stanton, and evaluate the demands made at the Seneca Falls Convention (1848).

E25E82E706B4450C994016B2DF64FED2.description: Students will investigate the development of the abolitionist movement, focusing on Nat Turner's Rebellion, Sojourner Truth, William Lloyd Garrison (The Liberator), Frederick Douglass (The Autobiography of Frederick Douglass and The North Star), and Harriet Beecher Stowe (Uncle Tom's Cabin).

D8FC05816B634813A59D081FA81312E3.description: Students will compare different perspectives on States rights by examining the Kentucky and Virginia Resolutions and the nullification crisis.

A1FA23B659DC4487921DBD9277162DC6.description: Different perspectives concerning constitutional, political, economic, and social issues contributed to the growth of sectionalism.

EA26781CDC2C47F896EB157B223DD044.description: Students will examine Jackson's presidency noting the ways it strengthened presidential power yet challenged constitutional principles in the case of Worcester v. Georgia (1832), including the controversy concerning the Indian Removal Act and its implementation.

E1C66AE6405E4C689F3AC7C403F6FBE6.description: Students will examine the market revolution, including technological developments, the development of transportation networks, the growth of domestic industries, the increased demands for free and enslaved labor, the changing role of women, and the rise of political democracy.

69CDB702DA4C4606AB50BDFD3424A347.description: Students will examine how the Louisiana Purchase, the War of 1812, and the Monroe Doctrine strengthened nationalism.

A4A4A8B4D2894FD7B0118AB06338AB22.description: American nationalism was both strengthened and challenged by territorial expansion and economic growth.

22359CF65D824764B2B5F46CA47EAB12.description: Expansion, Nationalism, and Sectionalism (1800 – 1865): As the nation expanded, growing sectional tensions, especially over slavery, resulted in political and constitutional crises that culminated in the Civil War.

CC756A512FE84685B23501132BCFDE1D.description: Students will examine Supreme Court cases, including Marbury v. Madison, McCulloch v. Maryland, and Gibbons v. Ogden, and analyze how these decisions strengthened the powers of the federal government.

4F2E24782EC04A44B01347037D5D5D17.description: Students will examine the tradition of a peaceful transfer of power established in the presidential election of 1800 and compare it to the presidential election of 2000, focusing on the roles of the Electoral College and Congress in 1800 and the Electoral College and the Supreme Court in 2000.

A02B955C36664F8283FBB471E55EC63E.description: Students will examine Hamilton's economic plan, the debate surrounding the plan, and its impact on the development of political parties.

3F5026B900E249359D42E27AE89F37B9.description: Students will identify presidential actions and precedents established by George Washington, including those articulated in his Farewell Address.

84F101A4B3D642EBB3F8CFAB0A4915E6.description: Under the new Constitution, the young nation sought to achieve national security and political stability as the three branches of government established their relationships with each other and the states.
