D9488660DFE60131ABC668A86D17958E.description: Students will use a variety of intellectual skills to demonstrate their understanding of how the United States and other societies develop economic systems and associated institutions to allocate scarce resources, how major decision-making units function in the United States and other national economies, and how an economy solves the scarcity problem through market and nonmarket mechanisms.

D947F030DFE60131ABC468A86D17958E.description: develop and test generalizations and conclusions and pose analytical questions based on the results of geographic inquiry

D947A610DFE60131ABC368A86D17958E.description: analyze geographic information by developing and testing inferences and hypotheses, and formulating conclusions from maps, photographs, computer models, and other geographic representations (Adapted from National Geography Standards, 1994)

D9475C30DFE60131ABC268A86D17958E.description: select and design maps, graphs, tables, charts, diagrams, and other graphic representations to present geographic information

D946FB30DFE60131ABC168A86D17958E.description: locate and gather geographic information from a variety of primary and secondary sources (Taken from National Geography Standards, 1994)

D946A9C0DFE60131ABC068A86D17958E.description: plan, organize, and present geographic research projects

D9464280DFE60131ABBF68A86D17958E.description: Geography requires the development and application of the skills of asking and answering geographic questions; analyzing theories of geography; and acquiring, organizing, and analyzing geographic information. (Adapted from: The National Geography Standards, 1994: Geography for Life)

D945EFB0DFE60131ABBE68A86D17958E.description: explain how technological change affects people, places, and regions

D945AA30DFE60131ABBD68A86D17958E.description: analyze how the forces of cooperation and conflict among people influence the division and control of the Earth's surface (Taken from National Geography Standards, 1994)

D9455AF0DFE60131ABBC68A86D17958E.description: understand the development and interactions of social/cultural, political, economic, and religious systems in different regions of the world

D9450A80DFE60131ABBB68A86D17958E.description: investigate the characteristics, distribution, and migration of human populations on the Earth's surface (Taken from National Geography Standards, 1994)

D944C4A0DFE60131ABBA68A86D17958E.description: describe the physical characteristics of the Earth's surface and investigate the continual reshaping of the surface by physical processes and human activities

D9447880DFE60131ABB968A86D17958E.description: understand how to develop and use maps and other graphic representations to display geographic issues, problems, and questions

D9442A00DFE60131ABB868A86D17958E.description: Geography can be divided into six essential elements which can be used to analyze important historic, geographic, economic, and environmental questions and issues. These six elements include: the world in spatial terms, places and regions, physical settings (including natural resources), human systems, environment and society, and the use of geography. (Adapted from The National Geography Standards, 1994: Geography for Life)

D943DE10DFE60131ABB768A86D17958E.description: Students will use a variety of intellectual skills to demonstrate their understanding of the geography of the interdependent world in which we live—local, national, and global—including the distribution of people, places, and environments over the Earth's surface.

D9431430DFE60131ABB568A86D17958E.description: analyze different interpretations of important events, issues, or developments in world history by studying the social, political, and economic context in which they were developed; by testing the data source for reliability and validity, credibility, authority, authenticity, and completeness; and by detecting bias, distortion of the facts, and propaganda by omission, suppression, or invention of facts (Taken from National Standards for World History)

D942C960DFE60131ABB468A86D17958E.description: plan and organize historical research projects related to regional or global interdependence

D9427410DFE60131ABB368A86D17958E.description: interpret and analyze documents and artifacts related to significant developments and events in world history

D9423000DFE60131ABB268A86D17958E.description: identify historical problems, pose analytical questions or hypotheses, research analytical questions or test hypotheses, formulate conclusions or generalizations, raise new questions or issues for further investigation

D941EAB0DFE60131ABB168A86D17958E.description: The skills of historical analysis include the ability to investigate differing and competing interpretations of the theories of history, hypothesize about why interpretations change over time, explain the importance of historical evidence, and understand the concepts of change and continuity over time.

D941A7D0DFE60131ABB068A86D17958E.description: examine the social/cultural, political, economic, and religious norms and values of Western and other world cultures

D9416490DFE60131ABAF68A86D17958E.description: explain the dynamics of cultural change and how interactions between and among cultures has affected various cultural groups throughout the world

D9412050DFE60131ABAE68A86D17958E.description: analyze the roles and contributions of individuals and groups to social, political, economic, cultural, and religious practices and activities

D940D950DFE60131ABAD68A86D17958E.description: Study of the major social, political, cultural, and religious developments in world history involves learning about the important roles and contributions of individuals and groups.

D94087C0DFE60131ABAC68A86D17958E.description: investigate key events and developments and major turning points in world history to identify the factors that brought about change and the long-term effects of these changes

D9404320DFE60131ABAB68A86D17958E.description: explain the importance of analyzing narratives drawn from different times and places to understand historical events

D93FFCB0DFE60131ABAA68A86D17958E.description: analyze evidence critically and demonstrate an understanding of how circumstances of time and place influence perspective

D93FB440DFE60131ABA968A86D17958E.description: evaluate the effectiveness of different models for the periodization of important historic events, identifying the reasons why a particular sequence for these events was chosen

D93F6A00DFE60131ABA868A86D17958E.description: distinguish between the past, present, and future by creating multiple-tier timelines that display important events and developments from world history across time and place

D93F0BA0DFE60131ABA768A86D17958E.description: Establishing timeframes, exploring different periodizations, examining themes across time and within cultures, and focusing on important turning points in world history help organize the study of world cultures and civilizations.

D93EAFA0DFE60131ABA668A86D17958E.description: analyze changing and competing interpretations of issues, events, and developments throughout world history

D93E6080DFE60131ABA568A86D17958E.description: understand the broad patterns, relationships, and interactions of cultures and civilizations during particular eras and across eras

D93E13A0DFE60131ABA468A86D17958E.description: analyze historic events from around the world by examining accounts written from different perspectives

D93DBE40DFE60131ABA368A86D17958E.description: understand the development and connectedness of Western civilization and other civilizations and cultures in many areas of the world and over time

D93D58D0DFE60131ABA268A86D17958E.description: define culture and civilization, explaining how they developed and changed over time. Investigate the various components of cultures and civilizations including social customs, norms, values, and traditions; political systems; economic systems; religions and spiritual beliefs; and socialization or educational practices

D93D0960DFE60131ABA168A86D17958E.description: The study of world history requires an understanding of world cultures and civilizations, including an analysis of important ideas, social and cultural values, beliefs, and traditions. This study also examines the human condition and the connections and interactions of people across time and space and the ways different people view the same event or issue from a variety of perspectives.

D93CC430DFE60131ABA068A86D17958E.description: Students will use a variety of intellectual skills to demonstrate their understanding of major ideas, eras, themes, developments, and turning points in world history and examine the broad sweep of history from a variety of perspectives.

D93C3860DFE60131AB9E68A86D17958E.description: evaluate the validity and credibility of historical interpretations of important events or issues in New York State or United States history, revising these interpretations as new information is learned and other interpretations are developed. (Adapted from National Standards for United States History)

D93BEFE0DFE60131AB9D68A86D17958E.description: consider different historians' analyses of the same event or development in United States history to understand how different viewpoints and/or frames of reference influence historical interpretations

D93BA650DFE60131AB9C68A86D17958E.description: analyze historical narratives about key events in New York State and United States history to identify the facts and evaluate the authors' perspectives

D93B4800DFE60131AB9B68A86D17958E.description: The skills of historical analysis include the ability to: explain the significance of historical evidence; weigh the importance, reliability, and validity of evidence; understand the concept of multiple causation; understand the importance of changing and competing interpretations of different historical developments.

D93AFE00DFE60131AB9A68A86D17958E.description: understand the interrelationships between world events and developments in New York State and the United States (e.g., causes for immigration, economic opportunities, human rights abuses, and tyranny versus freedom)

D93AB690DFE60131AB9968A86D17958E.description: prepare essays and oral reports about the important social, political, economic, scientific, technological, and cultural developments, issues, and events from New York State and United States history

D93A6B90DFE60131AB9868A86D17958E.description: research and analyze the major themes and developments in New York State and United States history (e.g., colonization and settlement; Revolution and New National Period; immigration; expansion and reform era; Civil War and Reconstruction; The American labor movement; Great Depression; World Wars; contemporary United States)

D93A19A0DFE60131AB9768A86D17958E.description: compare and contrast the experiences of different ethnic, national, and religious groups, including Native American Indians, in the United States, explaining their contributions to American society and culture

D939C2F0DFE60131AB9668A86D17958E.description: Study about the major social, political, economic, cultural, and religious developments in New York State and United States history involves learning about the important roles and contributions of individuals and groups.

D9395640DFE60131AB9568A86D17958E.description: compare and contrast the values exhibited and foreign policies implemented by the United States and other nations over time with those expressed in the United Nations Charter and international law.

D9390DA0DFE60131AB9468A86D17958E.description: analyze the United States involvement in foreign affairs and a willingness to engage in international politics, examining the ideas and traditions leading to these foreign policies

D938C7B0DFE60131AB9368A86D17958E.description: examine how the Constitution, United States law, and the rights of citizenship provide a major unifying factor in bringing together Americans from diverse roots and traditions

D9387E50DFE60131AB9268A86D17958E.description: compare and contrast the experiences of different groups in the United States

D9381E80DFE60131AB9168A86D17958E.description: develop and test hypotheses about important events, eras, or issues in New York State and United States history, setting clear and valid criteria for judging the importance and significance of these events, eras, or issues

D937AED0DFE60131AB9068A86D17958E.description: discuss several schemes for periodizing the history of New York State and the United States

D9375A40DFE60131AB8F68A86D17958E.description: Important ideas, social and cultural values, beliefs, and traditions from New York State and United States history illustrate the connections and interactions of people and events across time and from a variety of perspectives.

D93714C0DFE60131AB8E68A86D17958E.description: describe the evolution of American democratic values and beliefs as expressed in the Declaration of Independence, the New York State Constitution, the United States Constitution, the Bill of Rights, and other important historical documents

D936CE70DFE60131AB8D68A86D17958E.description: analyze the development of American culture, explaining how ideas, values, beliefs, and traditions have changed over time and how they unite all Americans

D9368870DFE60131AB8C68A86D17958E.description: The study of New York State and United States history requires an analysis of the development of American culture, its diversity and multicultural context, and the ways people are unified by many values, practices, and traditions.

D9363AF0DFE60131AB8B68A86D17958E.description: Students will use a variety of intellectual skills to demonstrate their understanding of major ideas, eras, themes, developments, and turning points in the history of the United States and New York.

document.title: New York State P-12 Common Core Learning Standards for English Language Arts & Literacy

DD0B89F0DFE60131B2F768A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases; gather vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

DD0B25E0DFE60131B2F668A86D17958E.description: Distinguish among the connotations (associations) of words with similar denotations (definitions) (e.g., bullheaded, willful, firm, persistent, resolute).

DD0ABC10DFE60131B2F568A86D17958E.description: Use the relationship between particular words to better understand each of the words.

DD0A57A0DFE60131B2F468A86D17958E.description: Interpret figures of speech (e.g. verbal irony, puns) in context.

DD0A0440DFE60131B2F368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

DD09B090DFE60131B2F268A86D17958E.description: Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

DD096000DFE60131B2F168A86D17958E.description: Consult general and specialized reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning or its part of speech.

DD090B30DFE60131B2F068A86D17958E.description: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek or Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., precede, recede, secede).

DD08ADE0DFE60131B2EF68A86D17958E.description: Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence or paragraph; a word's position or function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

DD0850C0DFE60131B2EE68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words or phrases based on grade 8 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

DD07AA00DFE60131B2EC68A86D17958E.description: Use verbs in the active and passive voice and in the conditional and subjunctive mood to achieve particular effects (e.g., emphasizing the actor or the action; expressing uncertainty or describing a state contrary to fact).

DD0752D0DFE60131B2EB68A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

DD064350DFE60131B2E868A86D17958E.description: Use an ellipsis to indicate an omission.

DD05EC20DFE60131B2E768A86D17958E.description: Use punctuation (comma, ellipsis, dash) to indicate a pause or break.

DD059130DFE60131B2E668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

DD053210DFE60131B2E568A86D17958E.description: Recognize and correct inappropriate shifts in verb voice and mood.

DD04E190DFE60131B2E468A86D17958E.description: Form and use verbs in the indicative, imperative, interrogative, conditional, and subjunctive mood.

DD049150DFE60131B2E368A86D17958E.description: Form and use verbs in the active and passive voice.

DD043D70DFE60131B2E268A86D17958E.description: Explain the function of verbals (gerunds, participles, infinitives) in general and their function in particular sentences.

DD03DBD0DFE60131B2E168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

DD026080DFE60131B2DD68A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

DD020330DFE60131B2DC68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

DD01AF20DFE60131B2DB68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

DD010B50DFE60131B2D968A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

DD006320DFE60131B2D768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

DD000D70DFE60131B2D668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

DCFF6940DFE60131B2D468A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

DCFF1070DFE60131B2D368A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

DCFEA7D0DFE60131B2D268A86D17958E.description: Integrate multimedia and visual displays into presentations to clarify information, strengthen claims and evidence, and add interest.

DCFE43A0DFE60131B2D168A86D17958E.description: Present claims and findings, emphasizing salient points in a focused, coherent manner with relevant evidence, sound valid reasoning, and well-chosen details; use appropriate eye contact, adequate volume, and clear pronunciation.

DCFD8640DFE60131B2CF68A86D17958E.description: Delineate a speaker's argument and specific claims, evaluating the soundness of the reasoning and relevance and sufficiency of the evidence and identifying when irrelevant evidence is introduced.

DCFD1930DFE60131B2CE68A86D17958E.description: Use their experience and their knowledge of language and logic, as well as culture, to think analytically, address problems creatively, and advocate persuasively.

DCFCA590DFE60131B2CD68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the purpose of information presented in diverse media and formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively, orally) and evaluate the motives (e.g., social, commercial, political) behind its presentation.

DCFC47B0DFE60131B2CC68A86D17958E.description: Seek to understand other perspectives and cultures and communicate effectively with audiences or individuals from varied backgrounds.

DCFBFAC0DFE60131B2CB68A86D17958E.description: Acknowledge new information expressed by others, and, when warranted, qualify or justify their own views in light of the evidence presented.

DCFBAD60DFE60131B2CA68A86D17958E.description: Pose questions that connect the ideas of several speakers and respond to others' questions and comments with relevant evidence, observations, and ideas.

DCFB5D00DFE60131B2C968A86D17958E.description: Follow rules for collegial discussions and decision-making, track progress toward specific goals and deadlines, and define individual roles as needed.

document.title: New York State 9-12 Social Studies Framework

1561F414571C4AFDB8E246CDEFF3F7C9.description: Students will examine the development of European maritime empires and mercantilism.

0B7DF9784F5D40879126D32636ED23BC.description: Students will explore how shifts in the global trade networks and the use of gunpowder affected the Ottoman Empire.

A8D4EDF02DD849CAA0114E6D7D631EA0.description: Students will explore how new transoceanic routes shifted trade networks (e.g., Indian Ocean, the Silk Road, Trans-Saharan) in the Eastern Hemisphere.

71AD25F95368485BAFB582C18D12ED12.description: The Eastern Hemisphere trade networks were disrupted by the European development of new transoceanic trade across the Indian, Pacific, and Atlantic Oceans. Shifts in global trade networks and the use of gunpowder had positive and negative effects on Asian and European empires.

25CB6E6B5643499A846469C621AE9D4B.description: Students will examine the social, political, and economic impact of the Atlantic slave trade on Africa, including the development of the kingdoms of the Ashanti and Dahomey.

95E401DC3CA74CFDB2F4EDD5F4C7A811.description: Students will investigate the different degrees of social and racial integration and assimilation that occurred under colonizing powers, laying the foundations for complex and varying social hierarchies in the Americas.

F4164F71E4304268A7C8DE1A796FF43B.description: Students will examine the political, economic, cultural, and geographic impacts of Spanish colonization on the Aztec and Inca societies.

D51B7B9C49534C35AFA3DD5AA932B0DA.description: European colonization in the Americas and trade interactions with Africa led to instability, decline, and near destruction of once-stable political and cultural systems.

46CBEF139EF74706A783BEDB1B20C2ED.description: Students will investigate European and African roles in the development of the slave trade, and investigate the conditions and treatment of enslaved Africans during the Middle Passage and in the Americas.

0376D2024C784BEBB29C6DE7F38CAC8B.description: Students will examine how the demand for labor, primarily for sugar cultivation and silver mining, influenced the growth of the trade of enslaved African peoples.

7EB18C4194A641A48B023DBACE0B58D6.description: The decimation of indigenous populations in the Americas influenced the growth of the Atlantic slave trade. The trade of enslaved peoples resulted in exploitation, death, and the creation of wealth.

77520E4CD90441F0888FDF9A23690759.description: Students will contrast the demographic impacts on Europe and China after the introduction of new crops with demographic impacts on the Americas resulting from the Columbian exchange.

2F4D6FE710F8477293CDF1A2075F5E47.description: Students will investigate the population of the Americas before the Encounter and evaluate the impact of the arrival of the Europeans on the indigenous populations.

1EF28A22701E406A9F2E33334F099C3A.description: Students will map the exchange of crops and animals and the spread of diseases across the world during the Columbian exchange.

3868F06CE3354FFBA5ACDAE97DE6027A.description: Transatlantic exploration led to the Encounter, colonization of the Americas, and the Columbian exchange.

DFE0F9EB5B484FE9A4A2BE57AA37BAE3.description: Students will trace major motivations for European interest in exploration and oceanic trade including the influence of Isabella and Ferdinand.

F0ADCF724FF64C27BDA72F8CD7CE1262.description: Students will explore the relationship between knowledge and technological innovations, focusing on how knowledge of wind and current patterns, combined with technological innovations, influenced exploration and transoceanic travel.

C669D698B73141C88112EDE1F049922F.description: Various motives, new knowledge, and technological innovations influenced exploration and the development of European transoceanic trade routes.

0B1EC2A80C3740BC91CC19C32BA6568C.description: Interactions and Disruptions: Efforts to reach the Indies resulted in the encounter between the people of Western Europe, Africa, and the Americas. This encounter led to a devastating impact on populations in the Americas, the rise of the transatlantic slave trade, and the reorientation of trade networks.

4AB07B779D2F4E2A8A1119D428FD835A.description: Students will investigate the context and challenge to authority in the English Civil War and Glorious Revolution.

F884885D0BD243D78DC5BD9D783009F2.description: Students will investigate the Enlightenment by comparing and contrasting the ideas expressed in The Leviathan and The Second Treatise on Government.

B059C1223C184E62B255E076818F17C8.description: The Enlightenment challenged views of political authority and how power and authority were conceptualized.

C29BFDC0B7A644A9970D0DB90E7BF12E.description: Students will examine the Scientific Revolution including the influence of Galileo and Newton.

BDBAC042909C48FDBCFA000F03DDA522.description: The development of the Scientific Revolution challenged traditional authorities and beliefs.

A82A3DAAA5834AF4A1586D1FED629B90.description: Students will investigate autocratic and absolutist rule by comparing and contrasting the reigns of Louis XIV and Peter the Great.

476573A17D454D9E869152632C9EB5FE.description: Students will investigate Russian efforts to remove Mongol and Islamic influence and expand and transform their society.

F85076AC208A4BFD972016CB74A6BFD1.description: Absolutist governments emerged as Western European and Russian monarchs consolidated power and wealth.

6D18BD994D0B4884B7F35E2A0532A7ED.description: Students will trace the discrimination against and persecution of Jews.

47C3CD745A0E469487CEBB80AC4C7A10.description: Students will explore the roles of key individuals including Martin Luther, John Calvin, Elizabeth I, and Ignatius Loyola and the impact they had on the religious and political unity of Europe.

2AF8723371344F1487725BAEC4CF264A.description: The Reformation challenged traditional religious authority, which prompted a counter reformation that led to a religiously fragmented Western Europe and political conflicts. This religious upheaval continued the marginalization of Jews in European society.

ACFB9E8DE6F24C418EE84C9C2088CA44.description: Students will examine political ideas developed during the Renaissance including those of Machiavelli.

CDD02ADA05ED4A15BE14ADA1B2562B4D.description: Students will explore shifts in the Western European Medieval view of itself and the world as well as key Greco-Roman legacies that influenced Renaissance thinkers and artists.

EC25AA92E1C144CA87ECBAB5B3726667.description: Students will investigate technologies and ideas including printing and paper, navigational tools, and mathematics and medical science that diffused to Europe, noting the role of the Islamic caliphates.

C8FBEF2979A14601B52A29EE3655429E.description: The Renaissance was influenced by the diffusion of technology and ideas. The Islamic caliphates played an important role in this diffusion.

783BE67E822443E691AA4F5E40FE8C40.description: Transformation of Western Europe and Russia: Western Europe and Russia transformed politically, economically, and culturally ca. 1400–1750. This transformation included state building, conflicts, shifts in power and authority, and new ways of understanding their world.

5DB6C09C615B44978A66A653D9DB306B.description: Students will investigate the achievements and contributions of the Aztec, Inca, and Songhai empires.

39DB5EDF7D92446E9E0D6A2B9E52A41C.description: Complex societies and civilizations made unique cultural achievements and contributions.

BCF9A597E822424A98AE24E9EBBE9361.description: Students will explore the relationships between religious beliefs and political power in the Aztec and Inca empires.

F8B2925F2A1A44829ABFE8CA47D1375C.description: Students will examine the role of nature and the traditional religious beliefs in the Americas and Africa (e.g., animism) during this period.

66A4A5055F134FE2A6EB3F3361A2CA00.description: Local traditional religions influenced the development of complex societies and civilizations in Africa and the Americas ca. 1325–1600.

415F3480CEB24219B2DA637B940AD670.description: Students will examine the influence of Islam on the growth of trade networks and power relations in the Songhai Empire and in East African city-states.

B1E758FBFA7D4A86A4E1857A67E29249.description: Students will examine the relationships with neighboring peoples in the region considering warfare, tribute, and trade.

1844705C3F474A9E925EA08363F2B01E.description: Students will locate the extent of the Songhai and East African states in Africa and the Aztec and Incan empires in the Americas using an Atlantic Ocean-centered map. Students will examine the adaptations made to the environment by the Aztecs and Incas.

28DE7A4E1A854BB88B3E0C79EFBA9F2A.description: Complex societies and civilizations continued to develop in Africa and the Americas. The environment, the availability of resources, and the use of trade networks shaped the growth of the Aztec, Inca, and Songhai empires and East African city-states. This growth also influenced their economies and relationships with others.

DA21AB1EAC6A4E09897D871F1F57D122.description: Africa and the Americas Pre-1600: The environment, trade networks, and belief systems influenced the development of complex societies and civilizations in Africa and the Americas ca. 1325–1600.

2F9B3D59AB0D4A50AB5031B4F5FC951B.description: Students will examine how the Ottomans interacted with Europeans noting the role of Suleiman the Magnificent.

F85A02276E4D4FACB041FD637F5F47D5.description: Students will examine Ming interactions with European traders and Christian missionaries.

BBCE63811CC442C9B30FC835EF709CED.description: The Ottoman Empire and the Ming Dynasty had different views of the world and their place in it. Islam under the Ottoman Empire and Neo-Confucianism under the Ming Dynasty influenced the political, economic, military, and diplomatic interactions with others outside of their realm.

E2767BF89F924B74BEF04FF0FAA98074.description: Students will analyze how the ethnic and religious composition of the Ottoman Empire and the Ming Dynasty were reflected in their political and societal organization.

445F714E273D49288EF888C1CCF1AD71.description: The dominant belief system and the ethnic and religious composition of the Ottoman Empire and the Ming Dynasty affected their social, political, and economic structures and organization.

771079BF20E14CB0B2763915715C0DA3.description: Students will map the extent of the Ottoman Empire and Ming Dynasty at the height of their power.

1822AB3CA9F14E77A6D4F6A4CE88A54A.description: Students will map the extent of the Muslim, Neo-Confucian, and Christian realms and compare the relative size and power of these realms ca. 1400.

CB40A7E670704096A2E328C030CF9BAC.description: Three belief systems influenced numerous powerful states and empires across the Eastern Hemisphere.

AB6E06DDA6604797BC029569E557AE48.description: The Ottoman Empire and the Ming Dynasty Pre-1600: Islam, Neo-Confucianism, and Christianity each influenced the development of regions and shaped key centers of power in the world between 1368 and 1683. The Ottoman Empire and the Ming Dynasty were two powerful states, each with a view of itself and its place in the world.

4FC99137B20341AB92676C69FF2609DA.description: Students will evaluate the impact of the Black Death on these regions.

5A64195913D2411FA197083D2F7DBC03.description: Students will map the spread of the Black Death (Bubonic Plague) as it was carried westward from Asia to Africa and Europe.

33130136C92E49158CEE27C1FD2B06E8.description: Networks of exchange facilitated the spread of disease, which affected social, cultural, economic, and demographic development.

5C3438C2DA904E29AF97905B8A807670.description: Students will examine the development of Sikhism during this time period in South Asia.

EE31827A83514E91B6A8CC41FCE45A7A.description: Students will investigate the Crusades and the Delhi Sultanate from multiple perspectives.

4C74EB18B1B94C919C7C2FB8D9D9B28C.description: Students will investigate the divisions within Islam (Sunni-Shia) and the Great Schism between Roman Catholic Christianity and Orthodox Christianity and their impacts.

3FB5FF8335C84E0781D1CF6553B6B9AE.description: Internal tensions and challenges grew as disputes over authority and power arose between and among religious and political leaders.

4A65B81FC4D4468B98B18794E8A17A15.description: Social and Cultural Growth and Conflict: During the postclassical era, the growth of transregional empires and the use of trade networks influenced religions and spread disease. These cross-cultural interactions also led to conflict and demographic impacts.

F841B3EABE5B45DE884F24B62908D08B.description: Students will examine feudal Japan tracing the previous arrival of elements of Chinese culture (e.g., Buddhism, writing, poetry, art) and how those elements were adopted in and adapted to Japanese society.

A21C13CB91DE49B9826621D50EBDD368.description: Students will explore the spread and evolution of technology and learning from East Asia to Western Europe via the Middle East (e.g., gunpowder, ship technology, navigation, printing, paper).

698995A4DF964CD3A94C65BDC17DA64B.description: Students will compare and contrast the achievements and innovations of the Tang and Song dynasties with the Abbasid Caliphate.

8A9EA7B57A214E7484D2AACCA6E3D254.description: Periods of stability and prosperity enabled cultural, technological, and scientific achievements and innovations that built on or blended with available knowledge and often led to cultural diffusion.

F21D762ADD204F7BA42F937AA6D7EA00.description: Students will compare and contrast the empire-building processes of the Mongols and the Islamic caliphates, noting important disruptions in other regions.

F9DC868F247042CCBC578381B144008D.description: Students will examine the location and relative size of postclassical states and empires at the height of their power including the Abbasid Caliphate, Byzantine Empire, Mongol Empire, and Song and Tang dynasties, noting relative position, power within their regions and the areas they influenced.

F7A88D641F4E4A20AEAB860030FB6FDB.description: Political states and empires employed a variety of techniques for expanding and maintaining control and sometimes disrupted state building in other regions.

62BFC2292471483AB3333BB36B20933E.description: Students will compare and contrast the institutions in feudal Western Europe and the Byzantine Empire ca. 500 to ca. 1200.

388CE66AA7994DCA82D3C868FB964876.description: Students will examine the political, economic, and social institutions of feudal Western Europe and the Byzantine Empire including the role of Justinian and Theodora during the Middle Ages.

7676C088DAC1400E9B9A4294818FF67F.description: Following the fall of the Roman Empire, divergent societies emerged in Europe.

BE96F312444E4142995507370C21BA23.description: Political Powers and Achievements: New power arrangements emerged across Eurasia. Political states and empires employed a variety of techniques for expanding and maintaining control. Periods of relative stability allowed for significant cultural, technological, and scientific innovations.

B5362E280AA04F71A46B603BE37358EA.description: Students will examine the emergence and expansion of political states along the Mediterranean Sea complex (Byzantine Empire and rise of Ottoman Empire) and Trans-Saharan routes (Ghana and Mali).

BA326182F24E4FDFA5A99A1339CC4884.description: Control of transregional trade and economic growth contributed to the emergence and expansion of political states.

E760438A5A7746A7971A495BF36C18AA.description: Students will examine the travels of Zheng He, Ibn Battuta, and Marco Polo and the influence of their journeys.

EE5CCB4D39FB45E78A5202349E20D9A1.description: Students will examine the diffusion of religious ideas along the Indian Ocean complex, Silk Roads, and Trans-Saharan routes.

59007CF5B74940F38909C9F9D634657D.description: Students will identify trade networks involved in the exchange of enslaved people and explore the nature of slavery during this time period.

CD85B6B59A4744F49840286767229757.description: Students will identify and explain the importance of at least two key resources and/or products and/or luxury items vital to exchanges along the Indian Ocean complex, Mediterranean Sea complex, Silk Roads, and Trans-Saharan routes.

4C5686E5EECB4B56BC31DCC77E1C5D4F.description: Interregional travelers, traders, missionaries, and nomads carried products and natural resources and brought with them enslaved people and ideas that led to cultural diffusion.

93B2171B4FDB44F78F081DD84FB68F80.description: Students will examine the technologies that facilitated and improved interregional travel along the Indian Ocean and Trans-Saharan networks of exchange.

AF87617749A94E9DBE99F5C66F367A5A.description: New technologies facilitated and improved interregional travel during this era by allowing people to traverse previously prohibitive physical landscapes and waterways.

044A2ABBF45D4375ABC4BF4C976C62E8.description: Students will identify the location of the transregional trade networks noting regional connections between the Indian Ocean complex, Mediterranean Sea complex, Silk Roads, and Trans-Saharan routes.

F07A7F636ABC499580CAFA689B426D87.description: Afro-Eurasian transregional trade networks grew across land and bodies of water.

D8D854BAC3F64681BE06B91E53E963A3.description: Rise of Transregional Trade Networks: During the classical and postclassical eras, transregional trade networks emerged and/or expanded. These networks of exchange influenced the economic and political development of states and empires.

BD87F526612547478C4E84D495B27EB0.description: Students will compare and contrast the forces that led to the fall of the Han Dynasty, the Mayan civilization, and the Roman Empire.

0D494EFA278642A8A5867A85DB3915EC.description: Political, socioeconomic, and environmental issues, external conflicts, and nomadic invasions led to the decline and fall of Classical empires.

A6E50AB4D9A9460C8A2D4AF82182E605.description: Students will examine the achievements of Greece, Gupta, Han Dynasty, Maya, and Rome to determine if the civilizations experienced a Golden Age.

E49865F0352B4AB4A2A72784F53EEB1B.description: A period of peace, prosperity, and cultural achievements can be designated as a Golden Age.

2813F16AE40044A6B6C65A6826C409BB.description: Students will compare and contrast how the Mauryan, Qin, and Roman civilizations consolidated and increased power.

7A05F5D8013E42858321489D67E3A0AD.description: Empires used belief systems, systems of law, forms of government, military forces, and social hierarchies to consolidate and expand power.

96C9380DD737496985CD124E2220C9BD.description: Students will investigate how geographic factors encouraged or hindered expansion and interactions within the Greek, Roman, and Mayan civilizations.

10BB7955C70F4EC094F7E20F31BB6A69.description: Students will examine the location and relative size of classical political entities (Greece, Gupta, Han, Maurya, Maya, Qin, Rome) noting the location and size of each in relation to the amount of power held within a region.

6B568A9639914D20BF06FA11C38C5DEF.description: Geographic factors encouraged and hindered a state's/empire's expansion and interactions.

EEA008DD07E640BC921116C847A88606.description: Classical Civilizations: Expansion, Achievement, Decline: Classical civilizations in Eurasia and Mesoamerica employed a variety of methods to expand and maintain control over vast territories. They developed lasting cultural achievements. Both internal and external forces led to the eventual decline of these empires.

732A567ED6BD48958ABA65D2BB129758.description: Students will examine similarities and differences across Hinduism, Buddhism, Judaism, Christianity, Islam, and Confucianism regarding their effect on social order and gender roles.

2969D829A239415E9CD345A957E758AD.description: Belief systems often were used to unify groups of people and affected social order and gender roles.

82A6C2C9947243AEAB5FC795CC59DE8F.description: Students will identify the place of origin, compare and contrast the core beliefs and practices, and explore the sacred texts and ethical codes for Hinduism, Buddhism, Judaism, Christianity, Islam, Confucianism, and Daoism.

A26F0B714338421B8BE978529FC61BB0.description: Belief systems developed beliefs and practices to address questions of origin, the requirements to live a good life, and the nature of the afterlife.

5C9053149F3D468AB45D26BB97143C9E.description: Belief Systems: Rise and Impact: The emergence and spread of belief systems influenced and shaped the development of cultures, as well as their traditions and identities. Important similarities and differences between these belief systems are found in their core beliefs, ethical codes, practices, and social relationships.

D6B3879F8E474A9EA8E74C3A0FCE6936.description: Students will explore the Mesopotamian, Shang, and Indus River valley civilizations by examining archaeological and historical evidence to compare and contrast characteristics and note their unique contributions.

43414A5FA838403FA719044E739AE206.description: Complex societies and civilizations shared common characteristics of religion, job specialization, cities, government, language/writing systems, technology, and social hierarchy, and they made unique contributions.

B4EA589FC49C45B3920B10E4F875CD5B.description: Students will explore how the Mesopotamian, Shang, and Indus River valley civilizations adapted to and modified their environments to meet their need for food, clothing, and shelter.

A5C14D4D89E743F9BCBCAA09020B40C3.description: Complex societies and civilizations adapted to and modified their environment to meet the needs of their population.

08949244A5BC4D7E8D38A1144AA51027.description: Students will analyze the political, social, and economic differences in human lives before and after the Neolithic Revolution, including the shift in roles of men and women.

1ECB44CF6E064A1C9A3BD84BF275E623.description: The Paleolithic Era was characterized by non-sedentary hunting and gathering lifestyles, whereas the Neolithic Era was characterized by a turn to agriculture, herding, and semi-sedentary lifestyles.

16467D8B19904441A056DA839222632F.description: Development of Civilization: The development of agriculture enabled the rise of the first civilizations, located primarily along river valleys; these complex societies were influenced by geographic conditions and shared a number of defining political, social, and economic characteristics.

comments: Grade 9 begins with the Paleolithic Era and the development of the first civilizations, continues with an examination of classical societies, and traces the expansion of trade networks and their global impact. The course emphasizes the key themes of interactions over time, shifts in political power, and the role of belief systems.

B58BCDD6DBB74AB89E22A1CACA847CCD.description: Fulfill social and political responsibilities associated with citizenship in a democratic society and interdependent global community by developing awareness and/or engaging in the political process.

2C629CEFF57E4F9DA707EAF9CAD6021A.description: Work to influence those in positions of power to strive for extensions of freedom, social justice, and human rights.

67D27F6216B04BE6AA42E3E07E7CBDC1.description: Identify situations in which social actions are required and determine an appropriate course of action.

DDD77E70E96B4D719F3FDF942E5C3648.description: Participate in persuading, debating, negotiating, and compromising in the resolution of conflicts and differences.

0E346649F4C246A8874DEC3227C029C2.description: Identify, describe, and contrast the role of the individual in opportunities for social and political participation in different societies.

369CBCE04C7F452DA912652293658EFD.description: Explain differing philosophies of social and political participation and the role of the individual leading to group-driven philosophies.

2A610C802D5B4FE3A2C3A913F5006959.description: Participate in activities that focus on a classroom, school, community, state, or national issue or problem.

74FCEA4120254C3EAE020C3074837A0D.description: Demonstrate respect for the rights of others in discussions and classroom; respectfully disagree with other viewpoints and provide evidence for a counter-argument.

AE0C116CAE1544C4BBE3EFD56C7113BF.description: Analyze government economic policies and the impact on the national and global economy.

1BF4375520A6459A85359E1B2F915A96.description: Use economic indicators to analyze the current and future state of the economy.

395D78E739CC48E7ABF7AAEB1BA39643.description: Describe concepts of property rights and rule of law as they apply to a market economy.

08B3639E0B50403E9A73B64216C0CCCB.description: Evaluate the extent to which competition among sellers and among buyers exists in specific markets.

34A3BCB00A3F4A8E8D60325D17989D96.description: Analyze the ways in which incentives influence what is produced and distributed in a market system.

FB57666060EA4D1A8E44E19A4E9F31B5.description: Use marginal benefits and marginal costs to construct an argument for or against an approach or solution to an economic issue.

044E16C266A348F686DD29DDDC4573A4.description: Characterize and analyze changing interconnections among places and regions.

18D210080B1A44A2AF784B26333FBD69.description: Recognize and analyze how place and region influence the social, cultural, and economic characteristics of civilizations.

8F692F56ABD24BC0BEDDE11FD3F4FA9B.description: Recognize and interpret (at different scales) the relationships among patterns and processes.

44DC1ED9E34249988972CF79FA51C7E2.description: Identify, analyze, and evaluate the relationship between the environment and human activities, how the physical environment is modified by human activities, and how human activities are also influenced by Earth's physical features and processes.

1399E33C1AB7426AB804900A19D3909A.description: Identify, describe, and evaluate the relationships between people, places, regions, and environments by using geographic tools to place them in a spatial context.

EE70D1D78883439FB6A6F64CBF4D1B44.description: Ask geographic questions about where places are located, why their location is important, and how their locations are related to the location of other places and people.

7735FFCB402045179D721D29E7974804.description: Connect historical developments to specific circumstances of time and place and to broader regional, national, or global processes and draw connections to the present (where appropriate).

472E659A17DC4E47B9AF2CB95DA92896.description: Recognize the relationship between geography, economics, and history as a context for events and movements and as a matrix of time and place.

77480F9E6E624DB78B3CDE0A592126C1.description: Describe, compare, and evaluate multiple historical developments (within societies; across and between societies; in various chronological and geographical contexts).

282617A13A8F4C0D81107979EE219754.description: Identify and compare similarities and differences among historical developments over time and in different geographical and cultural contexts.

285DF64EF85142F39A9E14A8C46711C6.description: Identify, compare, and evaluate multiple perspectives on a given historical experience.

CFD769DE5A744038AD2CE5E3B98A6778.description: Identify similarities and differences among geographic regions across historical time periods, and relate differences in geography to different historical events and outcomes.

77B0ABDAA07B4E888C7D8BD0F5B1EB82.description: Describe, analyze, evaluate, and construct models of historical periodization that historians use to categorize events.

4C48D6131EB34BF08FB49CCB56BE6318.description: Relate patterns of continuity and change to larger historical processes and themes.

28E82EE35F9840249103509DA56541DB.description: Recognize that choice of specific periodizations favors or advantages one narrative, region, or group over another narrative, region, or group.

F91950EAD23B407BA55EC33582C2D2E4.description: Recognize, analyze, and evaluate dynamics of historical continuity and change over periods of time and investigate factors that caused those changes over time.

BFA4950199114CA08EE890F5101C4843.description: Distinguish between long-term and immediate causes and multiple effects (time, continuity, and change).

82779AC919AA46EAB521A9C1DA852626.description: Identify, analyze, and evaluate the relationship between multiple causes and effects

B2E70055F57648CB9D8EA236953D0058.description: Identify causes and effects using examples from different time periods and courses of study across several grade levels.

A15569DE6066438DBA6EB10276E4F6EC.description: Articulate how events are related chronologically to one another in time and explain the ways in which earlier ideas and events may influence subsequent ideas and events.

5281FD97478944F0872C83CB2DFC7F0B.description: Create meaningful and persuasive understandings of the past by fusing disparate and relevant evidence from primary and secondary sources and drawing connections to the present.

0F803942B7774A358BE513B2852E6165.description: Deconstruct and construct plausible and persuasive arguments using evidence.

5C76E0F315734ABD9794A43120D8891A.description: Make inferences and draw conclusions from evidence.

228B20B7DA4946138C239771E25BDE6C.description: Describe, analyze, and evaluate arguments of others.

9781E6B2259248FCB3CF4931B24B76A7.description: Analyze evidence in terms of content, authorship, point of view, bias, purpose, format, and audience.

88753FB8A2604F6F8B0562ED5C13400D.description: Identify, describe, and evaluate evidence about events from diverse sources (including written documents, works of art, photographs, charts and graphs, artifacts, oral traditions, and other primary and secondary sources).

5308956497D84D71B74338ADC153DD45.description: Define and frame questions about events and the world in which we live, form hypotheses as potential answers to these questions, use evidence to answer these questions, and consider and analyze counter-hypotheses.

document.title: New York State 9-12 Social Studies Framework

F9EE677737F742F58E7F97BD397A7BAA.description: Trade policies and agreements (tariffs, quotas, embargoes) set the rules for trade between the United States and other nations. Agreeing on such rules is very difficult because each nation has different interests, and each nation has special interests trying to influence the negotiations.

73FB5D07A8C4411DB9A04A7398F17039.description: The Federal Reserve is the government institution responsible for managing the nation's monetary policy including regulating the amount of money in circulation and interest rates.

7A74927D0AE4426ABB2431F0876A9A33.description: The president and Congress determine fiscal policy by establishing the level of spending and taxing in the annual budget. Some tax programs are designed to provide incentives to individuals and businesses that influence private sector spending, saving, and investment.

62C1C784D82945599944B3AA3C631DFD.description: Policy makers establish economic goals related to economic indicators including the Gross National Product (GNP), Gross Domestic Product (GDP), Consumer Price Index (CPI), employment and interest rates, and aggregate supply and demand.

48FF53ACE3F24866A5B0ED7C0A0A24DB.description: The Tools of Economic Policy in a Global Economy: Globalization and increased economic interdependence affect the United States economy significantly. The tools that the policy makers have available to address these issues are fiscal policy, monetary policy, and trade policy.

3202E603CCA946A78B784A352AD80451.description: The degree to which economic inequality reflects social, political, or economic injustices versus individual choices is hotly debated. The role that the government should play in decreasing this gap, including the variety of government programs designed to combat poverty, is debated as well.

7F7B4CDDE14E42119746ED14202E258A.description: A degree of regulation, oversight, or government control is necessary in some markets to ensure free and fair competition and to limit unintended consequences of American capitalism. Government attempts to protect the worker, ensure property rights, and the marketplace as well as to promote income equality and social mobility have had varied results.

70BA111FF0E941A2B46CCAC5560AA803.description: The freedom of the United States economy encourages entrepreneurialism. This is an important factor behind economic growth that can lead to intended consequences (e.g., growth, competition, innovation, improved standard of living, productivity, specialization, trade, outsourcing, class mobility, positive externalities) and unintended consequences (e.g., recession, depression, trade, unemployment, outsourcing, generational poverty, income inequality, the challenges of class mobility, negative externalities.).

B84FBFD55EFA4745B63FFFD72FC1628A.description: The government's evolving role in protecting property rights, regulating working conditions, protecting the right to bargain collectively, and reducing discrimination in the workplace has attempted to balance the power between workers and employers. This role shifts in response to government's need to stimulate the economy balanced against the need to curb abusive business practices.

42DD20CBF53E4204A440CC43618E64BC.description: As the United States has evolved from an agrarian to an industrial to an information economy, the workplace requires a more highly skilled and educated workforce.

B4B2325118584D5BB3B532DB98F577BE.description: The Impacts of American Capitalism in a Global Economy: There are various economic systems in the world. The United States operates within a mixed, free market economy characterized by competition and a limited role of government in economic affairs. Economic policy makers face considerable challenges within a capitalist system, including unemployment, inflation, poverty, and environmental impact. Globalization increases the complexity of these challenges significantly and has exerted strong and transformative effects on workers and entrepreneurs in the United States economy.

CC52F802FB654694B444476B0396EE36.description: Businesses choose what to supply in the product market based on product market prices, available technology, and prices of factors of production. The prices of those factors are determined based on supply and demand in the factor market. The supply and demand of each factor market is directly related to employment. Debates surround various ways to minimize unemployment (frictional, structural, cyclical).

B20BFE0492C14D578D573DE22D4075DF.description: The choices of buyers and sellers in the marketplace determine supply and demand, market prices, allocation of scarce resources, and the goods and services that are produced. Consumers influence product availability and price through their purchasing power in the product market in a perfect world. Product market supply and demand determine product availability and pricing.

2B54AFD694244FDF8A63EF4CFB16CD63.description: Given that the resources of individuals (and societies) are limited, decisions as to what goods and services will be produced and to whom to sell one's resources are driven by numerous factors including a desire to derive the maximum benefit and thus the most efficient allocation of those resources.

1F20FD0034464C5293AABB06F5432A67.description: Individuals and Businesses in the Product and Factor Markets: Free enterprise is a pillar of the United States economy and is based on the principle that individuals and businesses are free to make their own economic choices as they participate in these markets. Individuals buy the goods and services they desire from businesses in the product markets, and they contribute to producing these goods and services by supplying the resources they own to businesses in the factor markets.

35EAEF8FDFD740FB8B6365734DFE2555.description: To be an informed participant in the global economy one must be aware of inflation and have an understanding how international currencies fluctuate in value relative to the United States dollar.

367A0C32A7BA41E4B8F672D6939E355A.description: Managing personal finance effectively requires an understanding of the forms and purposes of financial credit, the impact of personal debt, the role and impact of interest, and the distinction between nominal and real returns. Predatory lending practices target and impact those who are least informed and can least afford such practices. Interest rates reflect perceived risk, so maintaining a healthy credit rating lowers the cost of borrowing.

A06F271BBB284195B778EE4232649613.description: Sound personal finance (money management) practices take into account wealth and income, the present and the future, and risk factors when setting goals and budgeting for anticipated saving and spending. Cost-benefit analysis is an important tool for sound decision making. All financial investments carry with them varying risks and rewards that must be fully understood in order to make informed decisions. Greater rewards generally come with higher risks.

0F551DC5E19043D3B16E8E2835A1F324.description: In making economic decisions in any role, individuals should consider the set of opportunities they have, their resources (e.g., income and wealth), their preferences, and their ethics.

6CECFE799AC14D229BA2E8EE076BB101.description: Individual Responsibility and the Economy: Individuals should set personal financial goals, recognize their income needs and debt obligations, and know how to utilize effective budgeting, borrowing, and investment strategies to maximize well-being.

comments: "Economics, the Enterprise System, and Finance" examines the principles of the United States free market economy in a global context. Students will examine their individual responsibility for managing their personal finances. Students will analyze the role of supply and demand in determining the prices individuals and businesses face in the product and factor markets, and the global nature of these markets. Students will study changes to the workforce in the United States and the role of entrepreneurs in our economy, as well as the impact of globalization. Students will explore the challenges facing the United States free market economy in a global environment and various policy-making opportunities available to government to address these challenges.

A9AB1C9CA9A842C39C3B21502B6176FB.description: Active and engaged citizens must be effective media consumers in order to be able to find, monitor, and evaluate information on political issues. The media have different venues which have particular strengths and serve distinct and shared purposes. Knowing how to critically evaluate a media source is fundamental to being an informed citizen.

4AEC5A38C432453FBCD2C54C7CFBA32B.description: Successful implementation of government policy often requires cooperation among many levels of government as well as other public and private institutions. Conflicts between different levels of government sometimes emerge due to different goals, ideas, and resources regarding creation and implementation of policy.

7A2E264E3723474FA806BF65CBAF5F05.description: On various issues, certain governmental branches and agencies are responsible for determining policy. Those who create public policies attempt to balance regional and national needs, existing political positions and loyalties, and sources of political power.

2264F9796A9643118E2CEA2724097E62.description: Each level of government has its own process of shaping, implementing, amending, and enforcing public policy. Customarily the executive branch will outline its plan and agenda in an executive address to the legislative body.

8523501EE99747BFACB6DB2D59524184.description: Public Policy: All levels of government—local, state, and federal—are involved in shaping public policy and responding to public policy issues, all of which influence our lives beyond what appears in the Constitution. Engaged citizens understand how to find, monitor, evaluate, and respond to information on public policy issues.

E66A1E74D1DC4D269B5B3AD5AA7078D6.description: Citizens participate in civic life through volunteerism and advocacy, including efforts such as contacting elected officials, signing/organizing petitions, protesting, canvassing, and participating in/organizing boycotts.

D2FD256C81E040FAB3ABB413B1631DEF.description: The United States and New York have political party systems, and the political parties represent specific political, economic, and social philosophies. Debate over the role and influence of political parties continues, although they play a significant role in United States elections and politics. The role of political parties and the platforms they represent varies among states in the United States.

A7A24591420A4F14BF440E9B2BB19518.description: In addition to voting, there are many ways in which citizens can participate in the electoral process. These include joining a political organization, donating money, and doing volunteer work on a political campaign.

DF6D68B9A4784E17A468F3606122E2C3.description: Allowing citizens to vote does not ensure that a system is a democracy. Open, safe, and honest elections are essential to a democratic system. Engaged and informed citizens should know the mechanics associated with voting, including when major local, state, and national elections are held, how to register to vote, who currently holds each office, who is running for office, and what the central issues are pertaining to that election.

595D82ECCEEE4B38A2DE9FCC2940DBFE.description: Depending on the level of government and type of election, there are different processes and mechanisms within the United States electoral and representational systems, including the electoral college and winner-take all systems. Advantages and drawbacks of election processes and mechanisms continue to be an issue of ongoing debate in the United States.

832B35896C974B87BCEAA1C4B071A438.description: Political and Civic Participation: There are numerous avenues for engagement in the political process, from exercising the power of the vote, to affiliating with political parties, to engaging in other forms of civic participation. Citizens leverage both electoral and non-electoral means to participate in the political process.

DB8AF636BF1D478BA1FB1B8A6D1974BA.description: Citizens have the right to represent their locality, state, or country as elected officials. Candidates develop a campaign when they decide to seek public office.

5AA944C82404455787C18AAE9A1FB81B.description: Citizens have opportunities to both participate in and influence their communities and country. Citizens contribute to government processes through legal obligations such as obeying laws, paying taxes, serving on juries, and registering for selective service.

10FDDCCA639844C9AE542392BEBC7C88.description: The right to vote, a cornerstone of democracy, is the most direct way for citizens to participate in the government. A citizen must register to vote, and may register as a party member or select the status of independent.

06A0BC27B2024EB9894A793E8D4793D8.description: Citizens should be informed about rights and freedoms, and committed to balancing personal liberties with a social responsibility to others.

06B746981AFF41148226828D64915E81.description: Rights, Responsibilities and Duties of Citizenship: Active, engaged, and informed citizens are critical to the success of the United States representative democracy. United States citizens have certain rights, responsibilities, and duties, the fulfillment of which help to maintain the healthy functioning of the national, state, and local communities.

6FED9983FFA9435BA0316C9C56471B74.description: Freedom of the press is an essential element of a democratic system, and allows for a citizen to receive and interpret information representing different points of view. Freedom of the press has limits, which are intended to protect the rights of individuals and other entities. The degree to which the press is free and impartial in practice is a source on ongoing debate.

248E1AC458F444DFA5344E7AC4E77ED9.description: Rights are not absolute; they vary with legal status, with location (as in schools and workplaces), and with circumstance. The different statuses of United States residency bring with them specific protections, rights, and responsibilities. Minors have specific rights in school, in the workplace, in the community, and in the family. The extension of rights across location, circumstance, age, and legal status is a subject of civic discourse.

C00C75477DB742CD8C751FE3F0232D0B.description: The definition of civil rights has broadened over the course of United States history, and the number of people and groups legally insured of these rights has also expanded. However, the degree to which rights extend equally and fairly to all (e.g., race, class, gender, sexual orientation) is a continued source of civic contention.

EEACEAF0D29E44B3BE112BC34B6FDFCF.description: An independent judicial system is an integral part of the process that interprets and defends citizens' freedoms and rights. Issues pertaining to the flexibility of judicial interpretation and the impartiality of justices in practice are continued sources of public debate.

CD03002622CA4B8CBF408496F81F40A8.description: The Constitution aims to protect, among other freedoms, individual and group rights to freedom of speech, freedom of the press, freedom of assembly, freedom of petition, and freedom of religion. The extent to which these ideals exist in practice and how these protections should be applied in a changing world continues to be an issue of ongoing civic debate.

3D17DD9485354DF4B352117548A3C7D5.description: Equality before the law and due process are two fundamental values that apply to all under the jurisdiction of the United States. While the United States legal system aims to uphold the values of equality before the law, due process, human dignity, freedom of conscience, inalienable rights, and civility, the extent to which the legal system upholds these values in practice is an issue of ongoing civic debate.

3EC70FBA968C49998DC8E431A979646E.description: Civil Rights & Civil Liberties: The United States Constitution aims to protect individual freedoms and rights which have been extended to more groups of people over time. These rights and freedoms continue to be debated, extended to additional people, and defined through judicial interpretation. In engaging in issues of civic debate, citizens act with an appreciation of differences and are able to participate in constructive dialogue with those who hold different perspectives.

475511C2A87543C8AC393D25D31F841E.description: The Constitution includes a clearly defined and intentionally rigorous process for amendment. This process requires state and federal participation and allows the Constitution to evolve and change.

9BEE59D7311D456F9121190AE1DCCE65.description: The powers not delegated specifically in the Constitution are reserved to the states. Though the power and responsibility of the federal government have expanded over time, there is an ongoing debate over this shift in power and responsibility.

EAEB2CD068C9479799288BD2CF9B5D31.description: The rule of law is a system in which no one, including government, is above the law. The United States legal system has evolved over time as the result of implementation and interpretation of common law, constitutional law, statutory law, and administrative regulations.

6E57494401074BA398FEFB001E41D351.description: Limited government is achieved through the separation of powers between three different branches. The system of checks and balances is part of this limited government structure at all levels of government.

AE42B65968774D60B922AFACE68FBC4C.description: The Constitution created a unique political system that distributes powers and responsibilities among three different branches of government at the federal level and between state and federal governments. State constitutions address similar structures and responsibilities for their localities.

75486419A6764AE18A6F3ED57A58B3D4.description: Enlightenment ideas such as natural rights, the social contract, popular sovereignty, and representative government greatly influenced the framers of the Constitution and Bill of Rights.

7F3C2CFB16BA432C8070A8B88C987329.description: Foundations of American Democracy: The principles of American democracy are reflected in the Constitution and the Bill of Rights and in the organization and actions of federal, state, and local government entities. The interpretation and application of American democratic principles continue to evolve and be debated.

comments: This course aims to provide students with opportunities to become engaged in the political process by learning the knowledge and practicing the skills necessary for active citizenship. Content specifications are not included so that the course can adapt to present local, national, and global circumstances, allowing teachers to select flexibly from current events to illuminate key ideas and conceptual understandings. Participation in government and in our communities is fundamental to the success of American democracy.

6AB7DFA2935F4D278652B23D3BBE23AE.description: Fulfill social and political responsibilities associated with citizenship in a democratic society and interdependent global community by developing awareness and/or engaging in the political process.

53335195C139470295D20266F8847C47.description: Work to influence those in positions of power to strive for extensions of freedom, social justice, and human rights.

FBAF8C8BC89747D683EF4B4067F26F9B.description: Identify situations in which social actions are required and determine an appropriate course of action.

730E96A48AA44CF2824127A38AABC6FA.description: Participate in persuading, debating, negotiating, and compromising in the resolution of conflicts and differences.

064DA7078BF74AB7ADBF4CB0860D8B53.description: Identify, describe, and contrast the role of the individual in opportunities for social and political participation in different societies.

B6E65E7F32A4414C92D46B995A671E6D.description: Explain differing philosophies of social and political participation and the role of the individual leading to group-driven philosophies.

F64D158F094D40EA9CF126A37384C3A6.description: Participate in activities that focus on a classroom, school, community, state, or national issue or problem.

45C64572AAD14429BB3B07489329CF48.description: Demonstrate respect for the rights of others in discussions and classroom; respectfully disagree with other viewpoints and provide evidence for a counter-argument.

18FF6A4C542148DDA095A82792925197.description: Analyze government economic policies and the impact on the national and global economy.

A34E908ED8DB461E9AB128CAD0AAFA3B.description: Use economic indicators to analyze the current and future state of the economy.

12BB0FBAEB954CDDB93AEED3A0F7A568.description: Describe concepts of property rights and rule of law as they apply to a market economy.

9A15F42D96BB4500BCCA67261A85B7AA.description: Evaluate the extent to which competition among sellers and among buyers exists in specific markets.

2AE25B4C19354DC08E5C59958E521573.description: Analyze the ways in which incentives influence what is produced and distributed in a market system.

8F9221D2299D40A28698E0ADEC2590A6.description: Use marginal benefits and marginal costs to construct an argument for or against an approach or solution to an economic issue.

F9223474FB624879B06344A3FE142679.description: Characterize and analyze changing interconnections among places and regions.

3569C93D421E40339C461B1ABC76FA77.description: Recognize and analyze how place and region influence the social, cultural, and economic characteristics of civilizations.

6805736110964127A6A4CC52ED73C587.description: Recognize and interpret (at different scales) the relationships among patterns and processes.

2354A79CD63B41D2B9E1EB5BEA5BF639.description: Identify, analyze, and evaluate the relationship between the environment and human activities, how the physical environment is modified by human activities, and how human activities are also influenced by Earth's physical features and processes.

72297DBB0D214F679A957659376BD19F.description: Identify, describe, and evaluate the relationships between people, places, regions, and environments by using geographic tools to place them in a spatial context.

0ADE16D904FD4CA096A6B9806682B48B.description: Ask geographic questions about where places are located, why their location is important, and how their locations are related to the location of other places and people.

84F699069A9B4A30B04A2A912B313389.description: Connect historical developments to specific circumstances of time and place and to broader regional, national, or global processes and draw connections to the present (where appropriate).

7B8589A167314DC7A3AEC539A56F98E5.description: Recognize the relationship between geography, economics, and history as a context for events and movements and as a matrix of time and place.

9F554412D1C84924832867C0D8638689.description: Describe, compare, and evaluate multiple historical developments (within societies; across and between societies; in various chronological and geographical contexts).

DFD2A05298A3464C821EF737115193FB.description: Identify and compare similarities and differences among historical developments over time and in different geographical and cultural contexts.

5C424879514348C9A63F568B05E1950A.description: Identify, compare, and evaluate multiple perspectives on a given historical experience.

B3DCAC272F394B4488EFDCBDED5BC44B.description: Identify similarities and differences among geographic regions across historical time periods, and relate differences in geography to different historical events and outcomes.

F889C88DA1164B9DB2E6970069E3B8FC.description: Describe, analyze, evaluate, and construct models of historical periodization that historians use to categorize events.

C1E79D478B4E431E9B3C0F3EA1C18DA9.description: Relate patterns of continuity and change to larger historical processes and themes.

23FFCFE9C27B4CF297ECE4CA7BDCDE17.description: Recognize that choice of specific periodizations favors or advantages one narrative, region, or group over another narrative, region, or group.

AC2E2F4248DA43419158D762C903A010.description: Recognize, analyze, and evaluate dynamics of historical continuity and change over periods of time and investigate factors that caused those changes over time.

D17AA0B7FE264B33980E4616CA813F8B.description: Distinguish between long-term and immediate causes and multiple effects (time, continuity, and change).

3D784BDD89FE4CB5A8CEEBED13A68E4C.description: Identify, analyze, and evaluate the relationship between multiple causes and effects

B9DF8F1B26CD44F887DFFBFD0367CCC5.description: Identify causes and effects using examples from different time periods and courses of study across several grade levels.

3D0C3F3D481B45E98FBDB95B6404235D.description: Articulate how events are related chronologically to one another in time and explain the ways in which earlier ideas and events may influence subsequent ideas and events.

D6595E96A26F498F90E05B3011B79C57.description: Create meaningful and persuasive understandings of the past by fusing disparate and relevant evidence from primary and secondary sources and drawing connections to the present.

C86B90F86ED24B1DBF1D85975026EAB9.description: Deconstruct and construct plausible and persuasive arguments using evidence.

1098C90991B844B99B8B953A40E19CDE.description: Make inferences and draw conclusions from evidence.

73288BB762A44360899CFB728CB396A7.description: Describe, analyze, and evaluate arguments of others.

7013A19FDEEE4B5FB11439B801FD8DA7.description: Analyze evidence in terms of content, authorship, point of view, bias, purpose, format, and audience.

CDC89A11CFAD4AF28578831A9B8E6B52.description: Identify, describe, and evaluate evidence about events from diverse sources (including written documents, works of art, photographs, charts and graphs, artifacts, oral traditions, and other primary and secondary sources).

886A36379BB04B2FB021FF89A5770D44.description: Define and frame questions about events and the world in which we live, form hypotheses as potential answers to these questions, use evidence to answer these questions, and consider and analyze counter-hypotheses.

document.title: New York State 9-12 Social Studies Framework

3EB0CD8BA38E4DA0BB6ACAB5EA56CA37.description: Students will explore efforts to address human rights violations by individuals and groups including the efforts of Mother Teresa, Aung San Suu Kyi and the Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo.

F3752D1A55C642688376EE5C8017022C.description: Students will examine the policy of apartheid in South Africa and the growth of the anti-apartheid movements exploring Nelson Mandela's role in these movements and in the post-apartheid period.

291C7DA3E2174F5288EB360FD2CE6783.description: Students will examine and analyze roles of perpetrators and bystanders in human rights violations in Cambodia, Rwanda, and Darfur in light of the principles and articles within the UN Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

1551080F96A04A09A77D2E54B6163907.description: Students will examine the atrocities committed under Augusto Pinochet, Deng Xiaoping, and Slobodan Milosevic in light of the principles and articles within the UN Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

D29CA062F2734BE88CEC0395B3993008.description: Historical and contemporary violations of human rights can be evaluated using the principles and articles established within the UN Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

B57DD41D15C44B5FB9A37BC8C42EA2EF.description: Students will explore international organizations that work to maintain peace, stability, and economic prosperity, and to protect nations and people from oppressive governments and political violence.

9897EF277AC3450DA4B0552270163861.description: Students will explore multinational treaties and international court systems that bind countries to adhere to international human rights.

FEDF540362DA4E09AA7D7158347AFFB0.description: Governments, groups, and individuals have responded in various ways to the human atrocities committed in the 20th and 21st centuries.

9A8716CE3C984AEB9545BAB17E7EE57F.description: Students will examine the articles contained in the UN Universal Declaration of Human Rights.
