2A35485FE9254F1CA2E57DA864EB455D.description: Observe and describe cell division at the microscopic level and its macroscopic effects

A8711276B08F46BDADFB89A65A0AEFB6.description: As an individual organism ages, various body structures and functions change.

6C4CEBB2CF9E47B0AA4C2061A1E1F4E2.description: Patterns of development vary among plants. In seed-bearing plants, seeds contain stored food for early development. Their later development into adulthood is characterized by varying patterns of growth from species to species.

F112B1BBBDAF4F66AA6211DDE498E392.description: Patterns of development vary among animals. In some species the young resemble the adult, while in others they do not. Some insects and amphibians undergo metamorphosis as they mature.

96F3CF7E8B06460EB7352760538D6850.description: Various body structures and functions change as an organism goes through its life cycle.

A49A6391BF4C46198BCBDDB88D610543.description: In humans, the fertilized egg grows into tissue which develops into organs and organ systems before birth.

D9F17C6C793F46E186CF69997830E93C.description: Multicellular organisms exhibit complex changes in development, which begin after fertilization. The fertilized egg undergoes numerous cellular divisions that will result in a multicellular organism, with each cell having identical genetic information.

5DC4F35EC41B4A9181A3DD4D48AB97B8.description: Observe and describe developmental patterns in selected plants and animals (e.g., insects, frogs, humans, seed-bearing plants)

09FA79FBF2B84ECF89C77D7C65423F23.description: In sexual reproduction, sperm and egg each carry one-half of the genetic information for the new individual. Therefore, the fertilized egg contains genetic information from each parent.

4FD66A6FF5124D7086C9524D73AEABB1.description: The male sex cell is the sperm. The female sex cell is the egg. The fertilization of an egg by a sperm results in a fertilized egg.

8DA2C8CAA9B34C318C8951F1BDF3A228.description: Explain the role of sperm and egg cells in sexual reproduction

B575356E29FE419EA0072A57F68C7C5B.description: Fertilization and/or development in organisms may be internal or external.

DB7A7254A9CE473CAF2CDDF8F67C42E5.description: Methods of sexual reproduction depend upon the species. All methods involve the merging of sex cells to begin the development of a new individual. In many species, including plants and humans, eggs and sperm are produced.

7FFE57B0D88C4D978766C3D34A734CD0.description: There are many methods of asexual reproduction, including division of a cell into two cells, or separation of part of an animal or plant from the parent, resulting in the growth of another individual.

CE7531856B334B779EECD2B2C008777B.description: Some organisms reproduce asexually. Other organisms reproduce sexually. Some organisms can reproduce both sexually and asexually.

B7BDF6EEEC8C4BEAB625DBA82EA17DBB.description: Observe and describe the variations in reproductive patterns of organisms, including asexual and sexual reproduction

254A43CFE61F4D49BB44721BDD0350D9.description: The continuity of life is sustained through reproduction and development.

DE94A752D9B74992BEE5449BC49C7F4B.description: Although the time needed for change in a species is usually great, some species of insects and bacteria have undergone significant change in just a few years.

88FF988AB1D74E389CEFF6B6B90C75F9.description: Many thousands of layers of sedimentary rock provide evidence for the long history of Earth and for the long history of changing lifeforms whose remains are found in the rocks. Recently deposited rock layers are more likely to contain fossils resembling existing species.

3EEF6AA2BF4F47508B6C5468DB9CD1A4.description: Extinction of a species occurs when the environment changes and the adaptive characteristics of a species are insufficient to permit its survival. Extinction of species is common. Fossils are evidence that a great variety of species existed in the past.

CB718D9AA8654C45B176C50FE5C7D1FB.description: In all environments, organisms with similar needs may compete with one another for resources.

FC1136BEE93F4825BF276430C0F1C682.description: Describe factors responsible for competition within species and the significance of that competition

3CDF6968867E4520AB63D99C48158103.description: Human activities such as selective breeding and advances in genetic engineering may affect the variations of species.

3A2A1A5B450549E08F422223B31E5BC4.description: Changes in environmental conditions can affect the survival of individual organisms with a particular trait. Small differences between parents and offspring can accumulate in successive generations so that descendants are very different from their ancestors. Individual organisms with certain traits are more likely to survive and have offspring than individuals without those traits.

9EF6281FF2914EBCBC4BB9BA2879BF17.description: The processes of sexual reproduction and mutation have given rise to a variety of traits within a species.

32E5E1879C824792A80EDE79BD09CB42.description: Describe sources of variation in organisms and their structures and relate the variations to survival

90E9A4EF8B854506A4946AFFE3107742.description: Individual organisms and species change over time.

E7BFE6D2B13144C7BBE07EA31E9E1B0D.description: The probability of traits being expressed can be determined using models of genetic inheritance. Some models of prediction are pedigree charts and Punnett squares.

46CB8C4161F644BCA852154674C20C9D.description: Some genes are dominant and some are recessive. Some traits are inherited by mechanisms other than dominance and recessiveness.

C291C00C56254069868EBF8EF1B40A8E.description: In all organisms, genetic traits are passed on from generation to generation.

4849A1D1A3694AB49511AC11D71E0DD3.description: Describe simple mechanisms related to the inheritance of some physical traits in offspring

55E2F11BF67A4D04A37860294C12E398.description: In sexual reproduction typically half of the genes come from each parent. Sexually produced offspring are not identical to either parent.

4B9863A30113471EA9E3A8A3E031434B.description: In asexual reproduction, all the genes come from a single parent. Asexually produced offspring are genetically identical to the parent.

A80298CF417F4F7BA000BC436E2208E1.description: Each human cell contains a copy of all the genes needed to produce a human being.

748ED1CB01844AE9B10745253D112F37.description: Each gene carries a single unit of information. Asingle inherited trait of an individual can be determined by one pair or by many pairs of genes. A human cell contains thousands of different genes.

AC4E711CEC26441D84DE9C6F077D3308.description: Hereditary information is contained in genes. Genes are composed of DNA that makes up the chromosomes of cells.

D215C7D9F10A4C31A480AA2C1524D2EA.description: Describe sexual and asexual mechanisms for passing genetic materials from generation to generation

B720C34B4C064CEA82510DB1BD0312AE.description: Organisms inherit genetic information in a variety of ways that result in continuity of structure and function between parents and offspring.

24448220B6EB4608BDE4A34D14356037.description: Disease breaks down the structures or functions of an organism. Some diseases are the result of failures of the system. Other diseases are the result of damage by infection from other organisms (germ theory). Specialized cells protect the body from infectious disease. The chemicals they produce identify and destroy microbes that enter the body.

67E6CE3872E348D786ED5B841FA78B76.description: The male and female reproductive systems are responsible for producing sex cells necessary for the production of offspring.

568CD633C775460486F760702EB1BDC4.description: The nervous and endocrine systems interact to control and coordinate the body's responses to changes in the environment, and to regulate growth, development, and reproduction. Hormones are chemicals produced by the endocrine system; hormones regulate many body functions.

E31405A850D74B5F8CCD1621F15DB83D.description: Locomotion, necessary to escape danger, obtain food and shelter, and reproduce, is accomplished by the interaction of the skeletal and muscular systems, and coordinated by the nervous system.

1CDCA0F947234D6B9C170181C266D042.description: The circulatory system moves substances to and from cells, where they are needed or produced, responding to changing demands.

4B563176D7D24C0985D464D6C96CF678.description: The excretory system functions in the disposal of dissolved waste molecules, the elimination of liquid and gaseous wastes, and the removal of excess heat energy.

A10CC3225A9D4D5DB9B61261A8C82769.description: During respiration, cells use oxygen to release the energy stored in food. The respiratory system supplies oxygen and removes carbon dioxide (gas exchange).

C1591DADC55D47EEAA35F57B38F7F8F5.description: The digestive system consists of organs that are responsible for the mechanical and chemical breakdown of food. The breakdown process results in molecules that can be absorbed and transported to cells.

08F25BC8D3BD42A8B02B2A546AF849B1.description: Tissues, organs, and organ systems help to provide all cells with nutrients, oxygen, and waste removal.

D75D7A378621470CA8E9EECBA3294E41.description: Each system is composed of organs and tissues which perform specific functions and interact with each other, e.g., digestion, gas exchange, excretion, circulation, locomotion, control, coordination, reproduction, and protection from disease.

49C15448A67B4B04B7DB18C46405C5F7.description: Explain the functioning of the major human organ systems and their interactions

D4551ED1E70A483A860DFD8FE8F79A6B.description: Living things are classified by shared characteristics on the cellular and organism level. In classifying organisms, biologists consider details of internal and external structures. Biological classification systems are arranged from general (kingdom) to specific (species).

4D78A3DF0ADE42778CA5B981F74BA935.description: Multicellular animals often have similar organs and specialized systems for carrying out major life activities.

14B9159CD94640E68A34712C6744B22E.description: Many plants have roots, stems, leaves, and reproductive structures. These organized groups of tissues are responsible for a plant's life activities.

81C94F262E914C2BB682957EC538F890.description: Cells are organized for more effective functioning in multicellular organisms. Levels of organization for structure and function of a multicellular organism include cells, tissues, organs, and organ systems.

5BC68936B4DB49E182F9D028181C5C05.description: Some organisms are single cells; others, including humans, are multicellular.

2A8E8008ADA949ACA9E17E4E229EB931.description: Most cells have cell membranes, genetic material, and cytoplasm. Some cells have a cell wall and/or chloroplasts. Many cells have a nucleus.

24C070D2D4444B509D0B79E428704AE2.description: The way in which cells function is similar in all living things. Cells grow and divide, producing more cells. Cells take in nutrients, which they use to provide energy for the work that cells do and to make the materials that a cell or an organism needs.

86670F13C8D146C292874D0A5FD49F0B.description: Living things are composed of cells. Cells provide structure and carry on major functions to sustain life. Cells are usually microscopic in size.

1CA08FFAD8714F0AA41688E58F096DE0.description: Compare and contrast the parts of plants, animals, and one-celled organisms

724E560E16294AA0B4D993B0939F9268.description: Living things are both similar to and different from each other and nonliving things.

E6D01DB8B75542F0A363CD52FDE9D820.description: Simple machines include a lever, a pulley, a wheel and axle, and an inclined plane. A complex machine uses a combination of interacting simple machines, e.g., a bicycle.

5EC6D012EB6F4FAC91BA8F083724E2BB.description: Machines can change the direction or amount of force, or the distance or speed of force required to do work.

2610D2CD8DD942F8937214FFCB624848.description: A machine can be made more efficient by reducing friction. Some common ways of reducing friction include lubricating or waxing surfaces.

7901693E262B4592ABFD8B882AE52946.description: Friction is a force that opposes motion.

40F720DCD999446EB0FF4BE7901B444D.description: Machines transfer mechanical energy from one object to another.

30DDEF3DC8E948BFAFED66B720FD585D.description: Electric currents and magnets can exert a force on each other.

D41009056B9F4FBCAB378B847F97A670.description: Every object exerts gravitational force on every other object. Gravitational force depends on how much mass the objects have and on how far apart they are. Gravity is one of the forces acting on orbiting objects and projectiles.

9721D93FD9144A6986BDE438D160B6BA.description: Observe, describe, and compare effects of forces (gravity, electric current, and magnetism) on the motion of objects

F27ECD88B2C34D9C845C37A07A151B44.description: For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction.

E9128486566F43A8B0B5DB495B95F26B.description: Force is directly related to an object's mass and acceleration. The greater the force, the greater the change in motion.

B56BABF636A6444C8A90CDD6E1C1D913.description: An object's motion is the result of the combined effect of all forces acting on the object. A moving object that is not subjected to a force will continue to move at a constant speed in a straight line. An object at rest will remain at rest.

93A98019ECA04C5398C81252A77A9850.description: The motion of an object can be described by its position, direction of motion, and speed.

ECD2096647444013B2554F8CE256C8F3.description: The motion of an object is always judged with respect to some other object or point. The idea of absolute motion or rest is misleading.

017BC046E92640D0AEC3135BC7B0B80A.description: Describe different patterns of motion of objects

45696818F5A644F1960BBD7B67685AFC.description: Energy and matter interact through forces that result in changes in motion.

CBBBED91C78B4B57804C26F98061632D.description: Energy can change from one form to another, although in the process some energy is always converted to heat. Some systems transform energy with less loss of heat than others.

5A53CCB58B5E44A5BEC09E8228E845FA.description: Energy cannot be created or destroyed, but only changed from one form into another.

2A9E729CC90F4C5EBC4A60DE24454C86.description: Describe situations that support the principle of conservation of energy

ADFF2096555B44D59368C4E7D675AFFC.description: Without direct contact, a magnet attracts certain materials and either attracts or repels other magnets. The attractive force of a magnet is greatest at its poles.

70660AFE936F4CFDBE71FCEE016150BC.description: Without touching them, material that has been electrically charged attracts uncharged material, and may either attract or repel other charged material.

4A4B56694F704329B327612D21CC887B.description: Electrical circuits provide a means of transferring electrical energy.

6B597A90891E4458BF7FBCF2F561F0F5.description: Electrical energy can be produced from a variety of energy sources and can be transformed into almost any other form of energy.

0E7DDBA8557E48A4BA11565AEC7D8915.description: Vibrations in materials set up wave-like disturbances that spread away from the source. Sound waves are an example. Vibrational waves move at different speeds in different materials. Sound cannot travel in a vacuum.

63E4A91497454AB9804F2C03F441BA40.description: Light passes through some materials, sometimes refracting in the process. Materials absorb and reflect light, and may transmit light. To see an object, light from that object, emitted by or reflected from it, must enter the eye.

263AA2E859624B54B9C2D173E7ED5B84.description: Different forms of electromagnetic energy have different wavelengths. Some examples of electromagnetic energy are microwaves, infrared light, visible light, ultraviolet light, X-rays, and gamma rays.

AAE461AA99864BB8AD7BCD784FC7A342.description: Observe and describe the properties of sound, light, magnetism, and electricity

E341A56A9A814FEE84D8EBFDDC2D0418.description: In chemical reactions, energy is transferred into or out of a system. Light, electricity, or mechanical motion may be involved in such transfers in addition to heat.

A6E25C44DCAD4684B49F3DA7DB3FD9F6.description: Observe and describe energy changes as related to chemical reactions

48E0CE1650A64707AC7A60086A5D9190.description: Temperature affects the solubility of some substances in water.

B5DDAF29FB8E45F988D8DDCB32E66C6C.description: Most substances expand when heated and contract when cooled. Water is an exception, expanding when changing to ice.

123438343A334CDDAA44FE57C180F9BA.description: During a phase change, heat energy is absorbed or released. Energy is absorbed when a solid changes to a liquid and when a liquid changes to a gas. Energy is released when a gas changes to a liquid and when a liquid changes to a solid.

CFEFF82AE126459F8919D2C9FC81F96A.description: Heat can be transferred through matter by the collisions of atoms and/or molecules (conduction) or through space (radiation). In a liquid or gas, currents will facilitate the transfer of heat (convection).

5E2467FDA282414198BFA8E4A1675654.description: Heat moves in predictable ways, flowing from warmer objects to cooler ones, until both reach the same temperature.

8E9599F1F00B4D53A9FC782ACD089E85.description: Observe and describe heating and cooling events

AE425395133146F696F97160BD06EA19.description: Energy can be considered to be either kinetic energy, which is the energy of motion, or potential energy, which depends on relative po

C22B79397CD9493DB87CE58DB54BA9A4.description: Different forms of energy include heat, light, electrical, mechanical, sound, nuclear, and chemical. Energy is transformed in many ways.

E3BE2AD23EC64F559E9F55523A7FFC3C.description: Most activities in everyday life involve one form of energy being transformed into another. For example, the chemical energy in gasoline is transformed into mechanical energy in an automobile engine. Energy, in the form of heat, is almost always one of the products of energy transformations.

9F17B48FC36A44F48282CC9A87AACDF3.description: Fossil fuels contain stored solar energy and are considered nonrenewable resources. They are a major source of energy in the United States. Solar energy, wind, moving water, and biomass are some examples of renewable energy resources.

67F8EF86DEC14D24A51F7B2823E72965.description: The Sun is a major source of energy for Earth. Other sources of energy include nuclear and geothermal energy.

C69D49CC5C894426B8709DE4F07F171F.description: Describe the sources and identify the transformations of energy observed in everyday life

4686B6EE31C14257BE2A445A71B2370F.description: Energy exists in many forms, and when these forms change energy is conserved.

1E719FAA29DA4C4290E9C0C09A181040.description: The periodic table is one useful model for classifying elements. The periodic table can be used to predict properties of elements (metals, nonmetals, noble gases).

8CA945BE40704DE98882284C081CCEE8.description: There are more than 100 elements. Elements combine in a multitude of ways to produce compounds that account for all living and nonliving substances. Few elements are found in their pure form.

B7B8242D3322439D8399912CF6EF6BEA.description: The atoms of any one element are different from the atoms of other elements.

A508620B36DA4F069839A71673A7A540.description: Interactions among atoms and/or molecules result in chemical reactions.

B1FF6722453146C7A5FE8AB46B135A61.description: Atoms may join together in well-defined molecules or may be arranged in regular geometric patterns.

805F73C58326480DAD34715081D0CC9B.description: Atoms and molecules are perpetually in motion. The greater the temperature, the greater the motion.

BB114283DCD44EA2B6FA6351C95CBDE3.description: All matter is made up of atoms. Atoms are far too small to see with a light microscope.

2B70E43DF5914E6187E4DF3C2F34BFD2.description: Develop mental models to explain common chemical reactions and changes in states of matter.

D5862EBFD5FE4C43B29A4B88A270B082.description: The Law of Conservation of Mass states that during an ordinary chemical reaction matter cannot be created or destroyed. In chemical reactions, the total mass of the reactants equals the total mass of the products.

B332C300B2334EAEBD5B6906F071F8B6.description: Substances are often placed in categories if they react in similar ways. Examples include metals, nonmetals, and noble gases.

76A81CD627DC47508F52F682224C548E.description: During a chemical change, substances react in characteristic ways to form new substances with different physical and chemical properties. Examples of chemical changes include burning of wood, cooking of an egg, rusting of iron, and souring of milk.

ACD4DF0D48F842CF82B67FBF2DD6990A.description: Mixtures are physical combinations of materials and can be separated by physical means.

738D5905BA3846F1971C92FED9505E05.description: During a physical change a substance keeps its chemical composition and properties. Examples of physical changes include freezing, melting, condensation, boiling, evaporation, tearing, and crushing.

AC635897383340E098AEC9E8C10D2002.description: Distinguish between chemical and physical changes

4B9026B2290040929C92F75C30488CC3.description: Buoyancy is determined by comparative densities.

40C1CE48B82A41F3876B99A7EA6041F0.description: Density can be described as the amount of matter that is in a given amount of space. If two objects have equal volume, but one has more mass, the one with more mass is denser.

DB42C4C6312941309F4640336907E8FB.description: Characteristic properties can be used to identify different materials, and separate a mixture of substances into its components. For example, iron can be removed from a mixture by means of a magnet. An insoluble substance can be separated from a soluble substance by such processes as filtration, settling, and evaporation.

E4B33D9EA8D246EFA9FE0303C1DC7C9C.description: A solid has definite shape and volume. Particles resist a change in position.

5D93A345C7D84CFD8A71B9DFCB5BBD28.description: A liquid has definite volume, but takes the shape of a container.

BCC8A8C0820B445398E6BAC027E001AF.description: Gases have neither a determined shape nor a definite volume. Gases assume the shape and volume of a closed container.

910B7519A7BE45B0922B85D9DE1374CF.description: The motion of particles helps to explain the phases (states) of matter as well as changes from one phase to another. The phase in which matter exists depends on the attractive forces among its particles.

347C8D01AE254CCEAB62CF27E477C1DB.description: Solubility can be affected by the nature of the solute and solvent, temperature, and pressure. The rate of solution can be affected by the size of the particles, stirring, temperature, and the amount of solute already dissolved.

ADBE7EB69461488A93A69CB0318DD934.description: Substances have characteristic properties. Some of these properties include color, odor, phase at room temperature, density, solubility, heat and electrical conductivity, hardness, and boiling and freezing points.

8E0EBFBD96EE4A52B931784633CAFCEC.description: Observe and describe properties of materials, such as density, conductivity, and solubility

8731FC51404944F4B9FE898AC708B270.description: Matter is made up of particles whose properties determine the observable characteristics of matter and its reactivity.

A59A9AE3C79F436DABC7EBE4C2433C7E.description: Substances enter the atmosphere naturally and from human activity. Some of these substances include dust from volcanic eruptions and greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide, methane, and water vapor. These substances can affect weather, climate, and living things.

89AD6AC4C99C472CAA3B794B38DF0B0C.description: Hazardous weather conditions include thunderstorms, tornadoes, hurricanes, ice storms, and blizzards. Humans can prepare for and respond to these conditions if given sufficient warning.

6410C78DBAB44C1AA45334222441B3F9.description: High-pressure systems generally bring fair weather. Low-pressure systems usually bring cloudy, unstable conditions. The general movement of highs and lows is from west to east across the United States.

42D8915FCCBE4C29997A2236EEE74E48.description: Fronts are boundaries between air masses. Precipitation is likely to occur at these boundaries.

682E3F2B6A1E49218E99C7D8850D739E.description: The movement of air masses is determined by prevailing winds and upper air currents.

7D19DC1DDCD64E9F9968B1908F78B90A.description: Most local weather condition changes are caused by movement of air masses.

1E4CFA57F561469A90BC1452351FB6E4.description: Air masses form when air remains nearly stationary over a large section of Earth's surface and takes on the conditions of temperature and humidity from that location. Weather conditions at a location are determined primarily by temperature, humidity, and pressure of air masses over that location.

2E310E3BF2C44F0D8385AA923E724334.description: The uneven heating of Earth's surface is the cause of weather.

9736782891F84D948EAA5A15AEDE7F37.description: Climate is the characteristic weather that prevails from season to season and year to year.

6F4D35F0109C4F999B27B59898FB352C.description: Weather describes the conditions of the atmosphere at a given location for a short period of time.

8C7426B12B60447F977BB287064F2077.description: The rock cycle model shows how types of rock or rock material may be transformed from one type of rock to another.

990A1D5E0E144856BFD3B96316301137.description: Rocks are classified according to their method of formation. The three classes of rocks are sedimentary, metamorphic, and igneous. Most rocks show characteristics that give clues to their formation conditions.

B79B339BFDC04BFEAAD31ED8FE29C1C3.description: Plates may collide, move apart, or slide past one another. Most volcanic activity and mountain building occur at the boundaries of these plates, often resulting in earthquakes.

2A5D338D653447C597175F31EF7A1BDC.description: The Theory of Plate Tectonics explains how the "solid" lithosphere consists of a series of plates that "float" on the partially molten section of the mantle. Convection cells within the mantle may be the driving force for the movement of the plates.

4F4A4222531B4841999815BD142A0E5C.description: Continents fitting together like puzzle parts and fossil correlations provided initial evidence that continents were once together.

674DC719DBD746C9AD6FBC06B8293F44.description: Folded, tilted, faulted, and displaced rock layers suggest past crustal movement.

B33293C51A0D47C2807BC878976ECD74.description: Analysis of earthquake wave data (vibrational disturbances) leads to the conclusion that there are layers within Earth. These layers--the crust, mantle, outer core, and inner core--have distinct properties.

02B47A8E01E741AFB80DDB30DBFDA17B.description: The interior of Earth is hot. Heat flow and movement of material within Earth cause sections of Earth's crust to move. This may result in earthquakes, volcanic eruption, and the creation of mountains and ocean basins.

E3E1C7492D3241A4A5BB621EA2859320.description: Describe volcano and earthquake patterns, the rock cycle, and weather and climate changes

54588B9151E54A74BFEF9BE44B48E5A2.description: Water circulates through the atmosphere, lithosphere, and hydrosphere in what is known as the water cycle.

23BF17896DB640C686E0A2BEA8F30E9D.description: Erosion is the transport of sediment. Gravity is the driving force behind erosion. Gravity can act directly or through agents such as moving water, wind, and glaciers.

28B0927AB3E14A119F56D4EE5EB1C6B7.description: The process of weathering breaks down rocks to form sediment. Soil consists of sediment, organic material, water, and air.

B14BD49779E14A60BF6F3587554397BA.description: The dynamic processes that wear away Earth's surface include weathering and erosion.

9FF18819CDCC48CFA52641019319B2EF.description: Fossils are usually found in sedimentary rocks. Fossils can be used to study past climates and environments.

2C76B53516314BDE8645FCFC5A2268CF.description: Rocks are composed of minerals. Only a few rock-forming minerals make up most of the rocks of Earth. Minerals are identified on the basis of physical properties such as streak, hardness, and reaction to acid.

861062D876674836BAB1E7095723955C.description: The majority of the lithosphere is covered by a relatively thin layer of water called the hydrosphere.

E169E512790B40E5A5754B3087422B57.description: The rock at Earth's surface forms a nearly continuous shell around Earth called the lithosphere.

335C64F8C76949099A7AE7AA86CFC15B.description: As altitude increases, air pressure decreases.

DA50F09D7F1A43269804748C81F4E9DF.description: Nearly all the atmosphere is confined to a thin shell surrounding Earth. The atmosphere is a mixture of gases, including nitrogen and oxygen with small amounts of water vapor, carbon dioxide, and other trace gases. The atmosphere is stratified into layers, each having distinct properties. Nearly all weather occurs in the lowest layer of the atmosphere.

54C3BBAD5EEC47BCA870487265673ECE.description: Explain how the atmosphere (air), hydrosphere (water), and lithosphere (land) interact, evolve, and change

523C557FE2B6479EA6AEDBBEF82202CD.description: Many of the phenomena that we observe on Earth involve interactions among components of air, water, and land.

4783529D98774868AA651362B57D16C3.description: The shape of Earth, the other planets, and stars is nearly spherical.

D55D631B0CA8460D9DC51F15715ED925.description: The tilt of Earth's axis of rotation and the revolution of Earth around the Sun cause seasons on Earth. The length of daylight varies depending on latitude and season.

D7C1C6DA291E40E083E401A022AA40CE.description: The apparent motions of the Sun, Moon, planets, and stars across the sky can be explained by Earth's rotation and revolution. Earth's rotation causes the length of one day to be approximately 24 hours. This rotation also causes the Sun and Moon to appear to rise along the eastern horizon and to set along the western horizon. Earth's revolution around the Sun defines the length of the year as 365 1/4 days.

C694024549D245E38BAF224EB1E44425.description: Moons are seen by reflected light. Our Moon orbits Earth, while Earth orbits the Sun. The Moon's phases as observed from Earth are the result of seeing different portions of the lighted area of the Moon's surface. The phases repeat in a cyclic pattern in about one month.

46B33BD267DF47088501B134C30426A4.description: The latitude/longitude coordinate system and our system of time are based on celestial observations.

64065989289541558D54AF9C25B997E9.description: Most objects in the solar system have a regular and predictable motion. These motions explain such phenomena as a day, a year, phases of the Moon, eclipses, tides, meteor showers, and comets.

D575AEEC8C3945A3BE78695E0EF3D4FA.description: Gravity is the force that keeps planets in orbit around the Sun and the Moon in orbit around the Earth.

D958162493BF4A75BADBFE93C651DE23.description: The Sun and the planets that revolve around it are the major bodies in the solar system. Other members include comets, moons, and asteroids. Earth's orbit is nearly circular.

0E2609F9CC394D26BB651B9D0FDC3A19.description: Other stars are like the Sun but are so far away that they look like points of light. Distances between stars are vast compared to distances within our solar system.

C7A03E803B7B4FD6B10C25EC805C13CA.description: Earth's Sun is an average-sized star. The Sun is more than a million times greater in volume than Earth.

B95634F181D04C3A933D331B055E03BB.description: The Earth and celestial phenomena can be described by principles of relative motion and perspective.

5EFFA18A9BBC4C5299307945D58E7E28.description: Students will understand and apply scientific concepts, principles, and theories pertaining to the physical setting and living environment and recognize the historical development of ideas in science.

73B03C2AE13E4EAE8C96E7DB4B08E988.description: Explain the impact of the use and abuse of electronically generated information on individuals and families

7C5430477E694F7B909165F33161E967.description: Describe applications of information technology in mathematics, science, and other technologies that address needs and solve problems in the community

FEC3F90DD0B74125ADAE4B9CDFC51CFB.description: Use graphical, statistical, and presentation software to presents projects to fellow classmates

A980CC0D0044424695910018309C8964.description: Information technology can have positive and negative impacts on society, depending upon how it is used.

15137001C92E4645BD998F61970C9B5A.description: Understand why electronically stored personal information has greater potential for misuse than records kept in conventional form

8D54CCC235464CD7B5C2DE023DE6A0E4.description: Identify advantages and limitations of data-handling programs and graphics programs

BD4EDEECC3F4438ABDC8D5335C94713C.description: identify and explain sources of error in a data collection

B85EF0E8D7D64E8188F0ADB92D2286AC.description: critically analyze data to exclude erroneous information

631BF696DF0A4B1FB38A3332BDA40792.description: Understand the need to question the accuracy of information displayed on a computer because the results produced by a computer may be affected by incorrect data entry

8D1EEC2F656C4027945D2B74D23D4E3B.description: Knowledge of the impacts and limitations of information systems is essential to its effective and ethical use.

7856D33280854925AE2539B19521D710.description: Use simple modeling programs to make predictions

CBB7FE9CBA6645359CDBA6D55DB4AD8F.description: use the collected data to communicate a scientific concept

26BBAE142C3F44F9B6008FEB169CD67F.description: collect the data, using the appropriate, available tool

107CA12DA2B147C0BEFE3183EC877E26.description: Collect data from probes to measure events and phenomena

8795F18DAF1847A0A276449405A30BBE.description: Systematically obtain accurate and relevant information pertaining to a particular topic from a range of sources, including local and national media, libraries, museums, governmental agencies, industries, and individuals

44D04FD7BC73402BB146C82B8A12D604.description: Use spreadsheets and data-base software to collect, process, display, and analyze information. Students access needed information from electronic data bases and on-line telecommunication services

BAB7945EA9A94BB0A33C0F4A4AC8A341.description: Use a range of equipment and software to integrate several forms of information in order to create good quality audio, video, graphic, and text-based presentations

E7099510FFAE45A18EB233088616B5B8.description: Information technology is used to retrieve, process, and communicate information and as a tool to enhance learning.

922B1DB19CB943C8B7415C2A18596551.description: Students will access, generate, process, and transfer information, using appropriate technologies.

B80E80BE4A724254863599314BB3F2FB.description: In a group setting, test their solution against design specifications, present and evaluate results, describe how the solution might have been modified for different or better results, and discuss tradeoffs that might have to be made

678740B8C9E0454B84F52F493BF8A08B.description: construct a model of the product or process

19E645F7D949437C80738CE796730BC8.description: design and construct a model of the product or process

F38220CFF84B400680D65CEE46BF1B1E.description: Develop plans, including drawings with measurements and details of construction, and construct a model of the solution, exhibiting a degree of craftsmanship

61F726BFC5D44F3E89245D40F13E33E6.description: evaluate alternatives based on the constraints of design

63669100D24048ABB626BF1A4D9033AD.description: Consider constraints and generate several ideas for alternative solutions, using group and individual ideation techniques (group discussion, brainstorming, forced connections, role play); defer judgment until a number of ideas have been generated; evaluate (critique) ideas; and explain why the chosen solution is optimal

A7BEB38FD8EB4E1C959538B1E3E64827.description: use all available information systems for a preliminary search that addresses the need

10C7BB17253541BAA33D9B772F3B49BC.description: Locate and utilize a range of printed, electronic, and human information resources to obtain ideas

4CA5525694224E0285273A638AAB43E2.description: identify a scientific or human need that is subject to a technological solution which applies scientific principles

508543DA03904E41A752D3DFD14E8213.description: Identify needs and opportunities for technical solutions from an investigation of situations of general or social interest.

9E78286093094972B06644FF49AE5FEA.description: Engineering design is an iterative process involving modeling and optimization finding the best solution within given constraints which is used to develop technological solutions to problems within given constraints.

FD1DFC8A1A634C9EAD4EB0F19F30D83F.description: Modify their personal understanding of phenomena based on evaluation of their hypothesis

5CAED33DD1794E4AA2FC50352AC49BB7.description: use and interpret graphs and data tables

831AE890609D4514B311EBD9777920B7.description: suggest improvements and recommendations for further studying

2359519FB00941FA8828A095EA161C7D.description: make predictions based on experimental data

EF5C3917B1474E44AC8995CD543481FB.description: form and defend a logical argument about cause-and-effect relationships in an investigation

5037CCA8944549B0A01C2C2D98ACFB98.description: formulate and defend explanations and conclusions as they relate to scientific phenomena

9FAC7148E9984BD3B4BD7A0E9473A0F5.description: evaluate the original hypothesis in light of the data

81AF90931CF94C7DA070680433270A18.description: identify sources of error and the limitations of data collected

BE4C9B64AB404933898312E6C749B009.description: accurately describe the procedures used and the data gathered

1F87332DFD8E4F649B982EFE6674CBF9.description: Interpret the organized data to answer the research question or hypothesis and to gain insight into the problem

1BA071136CA44667B13410BC8731ED8A.description: generate and use scales, create legends, and appropriately label axes

F66B8960431745FAB1CDFE3EA9A628F0.description: organize results, using appropriate graphs, diagrams, data tables, and other models to show relationships

4DEB62F4FF2A4738864C3B565629B244.description: Design charts, tables, graphs and other representations of observations in conventional and creative ways to help them address their research question or hypothesis

AF835391223D4C4BA07F3A1BA4EE8A29.description: The observations made while testing proposed explanations, when analyzed using conventional and invented methods, provide new insights into phenomena.

ADF88DD753334E2E950B02092A882766.description: Carry out their research proposals, recording observations and measurements (e.g., lab notes, audio tape, computer disk, video tape) to help assess the explanation

91FF47DF2476431A9C735C91702528BE.description: choose appropriate sample size and number of trials

7650978341234E67834D373D26CD7235.description: identify independent variables (manipulated), dependent variables (responding), and constants in a simple controlled experiment

F3C8008BAE424FF790A8F68073E98834.description: design scientific investigations (e.g., observing, describing, and comparing; collecting samples; seeking more information, conducting a controlled experiment; discovering new objects or phenomena; making models)

245DBACFE64B413BAC1E11EE10EE43DC.description: Develop, present, and defend formal research proposals for testing their own explanations of common phenomena, including ways of obtaining needed observations and ways of conducting simple controlled experiments

183ACDCB131B4D4791E38A02C3593D4B.description:
use appropriate tools and conventional techniques to solve problems about the natural world, including:
  • measuring
  • observing
  • describing
  • classifying
  • sequencing

B26BC16A87284F9D9779B10E9E33CCD9.description: design and conduct an experiment to test a hypothesis

27741EAE37124BAB89A52785621524AC.description: conduct an experiment designed by others

ACA2C1BC6AFD4023B2D341AA4257D229.description: Use conventional techniques and those of their own design to make further observations and refine their explanations, guided by a need for more information

31EE44EFD3A243CB8FAF5348A722EFF3.description: Beyond the use of reasoning and consensus, scientific inquiry involves the testing of proposed explanations involving the use of conventional techniques and procedures and usually requiring considerable ingenuity.

481E8456A0354865AC0C4B71539516C0.description: Seek to clarify, to assess critically, and to reconcile with their own thinking the ideas presented by others, including peers, teachers, authors, and scientists

554AB1BBDCB5400888F7FA4EBE803FA5.description: Represent, present, and defend their proposed explanations of everyday observations so that they can be understood and assessed by others

F9E345CC71594DC78CD9CA0F064D9A5A.description: differentiate among observations, inferences, predictions, and explanations

6065CCE9F1C84AE6AB0AF4D25E4C563D.description: propose a model of a natural phenomenon

0A2E6D6C07AD4D20BC4DEC9792C296C6.description: Construct explanations independently for natural phenomena, especially by proposing preliminary visual models of phenomena

8D4019FFEAAA4B49AC4F7ED56599A3D7.description: refine and clarify questions so that they are subject to scientific investigation

488397DFE15D4D6EB6EC677D5910BE18.description: identify appropriate references to investigate a question

3F2C44D39B414B8D9C9380750D14FDD2.description: Formulate questions independently with the aid of references appropriate for guiding the search for explanations of everyday observations

4BB91A065744441F8FD4D88FB346E529.description: The central purpose of scientific inquiry is to develop explanations of natural phenomena in a continuing, creative process.

6A2F9358175A47E598BE61C6281E2872.description: use appropriate scientific tools to solve problems about the natural world

998F5C7185804C5F8DD8B0CB80632A29.description: Apply mathematical knowledge to solve real-world problems and problems that arise from the investigation of mathematical ideas, using representations such as pictures, charts, and tables.

63F827D6592C475C88147836AE586B88.description: Critical thinking skills are used in the solution of mathematical problems.

1F461FF93E1D4EDFB0A0D256B7DB611B.description: Use inductive reasoning to construct, evaluate, and validate conjectures and arguments, recognizing that patterns and relationships can assist in explaining and extending mathematical phenomena.

7EF5D1F03B5C487FA87141E152B6957C.description: Deductive and inductive reasoning are used to reach mathematical conclusions.

0B9C06C370F04278921A145B92B83248.description: apply mathematical equations to describe relationships among variables in the natural world

D42DBDAA87F94813AF86867F1D8A6682.description: identify relationships among variables including: direct, indirect, cyclic, constant; identify non-related material

0F3B2FEC10A5420794CBFB2407E330C2.description: Extend mathematical notation and symbolism to include variables and algebraic expressions in order to describe and compare quantities and express mathematical relationships

A5739DEE6CBE444CBFC306083864A2A0.description: Abstraction and symbolic representation are used to communicate mathematically.

D78FE0CE31F341D18191E45EAB48E0CD.description: Students will use mathematical analysis, scientific inquiry, and engineering design, as appropriate, to pose questions, seek answers, and develop solutions.

document.title: Elementary Science, Intermediate Science, Living Environment, Earth Science, Chemistry, and Physics Core Curriculum

2BFB4F1605964B6BBB3B96B007CFD317.description:
If students participate in an extended, culminating mathematics, science, and technology project, then students should:
  • work effectively
  • gather and process information
  • generate and analyze ideas
  • observe common themes
  • realize ideas
  • present results

25589D1D43944AA9904E0C5C8947D9F7.description: collect, analyze, interpret, and present data, using appropriate tools

BA51D2E8B33841E1AF946976967A8669.description: Solving interdisciplinary problems involves a variety of skills and strategies, including effective work habits; gathering and processing information; generating and analyzing ideas; realizing ideas; making connections among the common themes of mathematics, science, and technology; and presenting results.

9FEBAD9B30014346AD77CC45BCC9BB0E.description: address real-world problems, using scientific methodology

9672F9DB57A24555B4B6387D72279842.description: The knowledge and skills of mathematics, science, and technology are used together to make informed decisions and solve problems, especially those relating to issues of science/ technology/society, consumer decision making, design, and inquiry into phenomena

5D2532223A144D2FA7D11481A173D4F2.description: Students will apply the knowledge and thinking skills of mathematics, science, and technology to address real-life problems and make informed decisions.

024DC721D64144D1B6B98BEEFFB916B9.description: determine optimal solutions to problems that can be solved using quantitative methods

192FE15CF9CD48AE91ABC7E071F92FB4.description: In order to arrive at the best solution that meets criteria within constraints, it is often necessary to make trade-offs.

B511CE01A05C4C63907A74EFE6852704.description: identify and develop models, using patterns in data

90B33EAB99CF484CBB200281BF93D636.description: deduce patterns from the organization and presentation of data

25A5DB91FB6B45D382F04CDD2325693B.description: Search for multiple trends when analyzing data for patterns, and identify data that do not fit the trends.

1FAFE73E63044D5FBFD528633F3F401A.description: predict the behavior of physical systems, using mathematical models such as graphs and equations

BEE406B8C6D24130AA1B9D1355CACDF4.description: Use sophisticated mathematical models, such as graphs and equations of various algebraic or trigonometric functions.

9BF79C057FBA4F74853BEB550F7DD041.description: Identifying patterns of change is necessary for making predictions about future behavior and conditions.

7F65DAC753084DC1BDB31DD37B2F18A2.description: Cite specific examples of how dynamic equilibrium is achieved by equality of change in opposing directions.

0416FEAA4D82435DA0914B6836BA3146.description: Describe specific instances of how disturbances might affect a system's equilibrium, from small disturbances that do not upset the equilibrium to larger disturbances (threshold level) that cause the system to become unstable.

D71AA2CA66324A7AA59F5430F6E86016.description: Equilibrium is a state of stability due either to a lack of change (static equilibrium) or a balance between opposing forces (dynamic equilibrium).

5C4F52D230214CFEA51F1D419FFA30D6.description: simplify calculations by using scientific notation

3C7218E9F7FC4BD6A8517E3FEB3C9776.description: estimate quantitative results, using orders of magnitude

6D965CA752E04CE5AEAD5AA43AE1C6F2.description: Extend their use of powers of ten notation to understanding the exponential function and performing operations with exponential factors.

4CBF78ACC2D74C0D86B859A5DF00758E.description: Describe the effects of changes in scale on the functioning of physical, biological, or designed systems.

FC8AA79A50AA41E3B83A32213ACDF2FB.description: The grouping of magnitudes of size, time, frequency, and pressures or other units of measurement into a series of relative order provides a useful way to deal with the immense range and the changes in scale that affect the behavior and design of systems.

3BB92EB3363B47B188AB6A55A738E70B.description: predict the behavior of a system, using a model

A35095453E174352ADE4E90DC708BF96.description: validate or reject a model based on collated experimental data

AE146B416A824C7D8D371593F293A5C1.description: Compare predictions to actual observations, using test models.

B6693B22A83F450CB3B6B3DF4699C861.description: represent the behavior of real-world systems, using physical and mathematical models

D2C0B7C66F9B44F380858612DA28F09C.description: Find and use mathematical models that behave in the same manner as the processes under investigation.

4DC3DFA5AD004971AB274DB8C2FD927A.description: use observations of the behavior of a system to develop a model

E22F5F6D4EB141FDB46EC0E47C42FFB8.description: Collect information about the behavior of a system and use modeling tools to represent the operation of the system.

550409F3A38C4521A6C2EEA14160872A.description: Revise a model to create a more complete or improved representation of the system.

D6537A9F59CB4F87BFEE8BE94340ECA0.description: Models are simplified representations of objects, structures, or systems used in analysis, explanation, interpretation, or design.

637F6AACB48C418EAC45A90F78AB1334.description: Define boundary conditions when doing systems analysis to determine what influences a system and how it behaves

0454F17129DE43A2983077591297D9B4.description: Through systems thinking, people can recognize the commonalities that exist among all systems and how parts of a system interrelate and combine to perform specific functions.

6961BCBD249D4166B45BB6112EA47360.description: Students will understand the relationships and common themes that connect mathematics, science, and technology and apply the themes to these and other areas of learning.

773D7233D04C459E8AA25D88FBF160DE.description: The fundamental source of all energy in the universe is the conversion of mass into energy.

53F2E715CEDC4414A762C28979FC1321.description: The total of the fundamental interactions is responsible for the appearance and behavior of the objects in the universe.

DF21C9F94206407F809C61B1E84964F6.description: Behaviors and characteristics of matter, from the microscopic to the cosmic levels, are manifestations of its atomic structure. The macroscopic characteristics of matter, such as electrical and optical properties, are the result of microscopic interactions.

CA87F16DC8C447FCA2A6502BFFAF3F58.description:
The Standard Model of Particle Physics has evolved from previous attempts to explain the nature of the atom and states that:
  • atomic particles are composed of subnuclear particles
  • the nucleus is a comglomeration of quarks which manifest themselves as protons and neutrons
  • each elementary particle has a corresponding antiparticle

F6C9CE5BA0714B3084612BAA71457AC9.description: Among other things, mass-energy and charge are conserved at all levels (from subnuclear to cosmic).

05E573F621BD471C8CDFABFC0209FC73.description: On the atomic level, energy and matter exhibit the characteristics of both waves and particles.

0FB82FBF0E424B0BA395ECD1B09887BB.description: The energy of a photon is proportional to its frequency.

9CCAE3F182B848759802D8DF6B8FB7AC.description: On the atomic level, energy is emitted or absorbed in discrete packets called photons.

BCBA343ECD1C4102A1CFA18B8A668888.description: Charge is quantized on two levels. On the atomic level, charge is restricted to multiples of the elementary charge (charge on the electron or proton). On the subnuclear level, charge appears as fractional values of the elementary charge (quarks).

7A11A5590C7F44A0BED64AC3711F5044.description: States of matter and energy are restricted to discrete values (quantized).

BB1EA5F0D89545AAB8FBE6D28DC2E0C1.description: Students can compare energy relationships within an atom's nucleus to those outside the nucleus.

00A0C826608543388DCBDD536D4FCAEB.description: The inverse square law applies to electrical and gravitational fields produced by point sources.

5B8A0F6F784B401B93EB2821786C1658.description: Gravitational forces are only attractive, whereas electrical and magnetic forces can be attractive or repulsive.

7EBA6C4F9FB248779BCA8BAEC48C78C0.description: Field strength and direction are determined using a suitable test particle.
comments: Notes: 1)Calculations are limited to electrostatic and gravitational fields. 2)The gravitational field near the surface of Earth and the electrical field between two oppositely charged parallel plates are treated as uniform.

98250A4891774DF3BF5302FF9E02D153.description: Momentum is conserved in a closed system.
comments: Note: Testing will be limited to momentum in one dimension.

D6CB03E047F64442A7232D0EFC80F9A4.description: According to Newton's Third Law, forces occur in action/reaction pairs. When one object exerts a force on a second, the second exerts a force on the first that is equal in magnitude and opposite in direction.

0A7C1B20D8974D8EB60F9745C0A2B557.description: The impulse imparted to an object causes a change in its momentum.

8B3DDE14101C4FFEA325B7852BF90430.description: Kinetic friction is a force that opposes motion.

48D9C7426457410FA432263BC52FE45E.description: Centripetal force is the net force which produces centripetal acceleration. In uniform circular motion, the centripetal force is perpendicular to the tangential velocity.

F6128B6CADC94B10A29D8F18E19571FF.description: The elongation or compression of a spring depends upon the nature of the spring (its spring constant) and the magnitude of the applied force.

0EF0FD4FA3464220908B8D23BB2AA432.description: Weight is the gravitational force with which a planet attracts a mass. The mass of an object is independent of the gravitational field in which it is located.

DB05D13B8EB34A94B9413553C799E7FB.description: According to Newton's Second Law, an unbalanced force causes a mass to accelerate.

65C0211021E743DCA82CD774880123B2.description: When the net force on a system is zero, the system is in equilibrium.

66ED336A067D46ADA95D54D0D7195BF9.description: According to Newton's First Law, the inertia of an object is directly proportional to its mass. An object remains at rest or moves with constant velocity, unless acted upon by an unbalanced force.

1415558477654A23BCA05BE4EA099097.description: The horizontal displacement of a projectile is dependent upon the horizontal component of its motion and its time of flight.

C7F45824DA6643EBAD26AEDDE645D9EF.description: Aprojectile's time of flight is dependent upon the vertical component of its motion.

3794C64D022C45AF973A66BECF27F84B.description: The path of a projectile is the result of the simultaneous effect of the horizontal and vertical components of its motion; these components act independently.

9ABA6AE309524C42B3377B16FB3E9CC3.description: An object in free fall accelerates due to the force of gravity. Friction and other forces cause the actual motion of a falling object to deviate from its theoretical motion.
comments: Note: Initial velocities of objects in free fall may be in any direction.

C999124884C241F694479DFFB277C63C.description: An object in linear motion may travel with a constant velocity or with acceleration.
comments: Note: Testing of acceleration will be limited to cases in which acceleration is constant.

FA97B204F6AE4517BD90B97B8756D836.description: The resultant of two or more vectors, acting at any angle, is determined by vector addition.

0BB8895D72544E35BFA0465E6B19C7C9.description: A vector may be resolved into perpendicular components.

7C044E1BF22542B1B2A9FAE076DD039B.description: Measured quantities can be classified as either vector or scalar.

F4511415608E41DEAA0B8FD7ABB7952C.description: Students can explain and predict different patterns of motion of objects (e.g., linear and uniform circular motion, velocity and acceleration, momentum and inertia).

C9CD454EF61F4259B31B7E51384FF665.description: Energy and matter interact through forces that result in changes in motion.

6BAE794FDBC64D27BE797FA4956AA2B1.description: When a wave source and an observer are in relative motion, the observed frequency of the waves traveling between them is shifted (Doppler effect).

647582AD8ADE4D2284C0AF5D1F2E4F8C.description: When waves of a similar nature meet, the resulting interference may be explained using the principle of superposition. Standing waves are a special case of interference.

CED91A86836245EE9F3E8D598E03983A.description: Diffraction occurs when waves pass by obstacles or through openings. The wavelength of the incident wave and the size of the obstacle or opening affect how the wave spreads out.

2B96431946254EFFA7D0CBA94B920A74.description: All frequencies of electromagnetic radiation travel at the same speed in a vacuum.

A5E72913C30F458ABB374663D18232EA.description: The absolute index of refraction is inversely proportional to the speed of a wave.

45B6A97D0A164C34A11188ABBD6B1B3F.description: When a wave moves from one medium into another, the wave may refract due to a change in speed. The angle of refraction (measured with respect to the normal) depends on the angle of incidence and the properties of the media (indices of refraction).

2D0F638B11494C278195C1847FC4DD7E.description: When a wave strikes a boundary between two media, reflection, transmission, and absorption occur. A transmitted wave may be refracted.

A8747E94A5D546B18A96E016BB5E4F7D.description: Electromagnetic radiation exhibits wave characteristics. Electromagnetic waves can propagate through a vacuum.

31FC10B3FBB64AC9B8946DE288C7DDB3.description: Resonance occurs when energy is transferred to a system at its natural frequency.

90B7BEE179654682B51F3278D2A55266.description: Waves are categorized by the direction in which particles in a medium vibrate about an equilibrium position relative to the direction of propagation of the wave, such as transverse and longitudinal waves.

D3793695B9F345CCAE74C685E290AE39.description: Mechanical waves require a material medium through which to travel.

C3907D132BC742EB9D82770B4DE729AD.description: The model of a wave incorporates the characteristics of amplitude, wavelength, frequency, period, wave speed, and phase.

4B59908834664DD8AA8626931E28F045.description: Waves carry energy and information without transferring mass. This energy may be carried by pulses or periodic waves.

C88F30B2359D4532937F14EB125BB701.description: An oscillating system produces waves. The nature of the system determines the type of wave produced.

42DBD84F9D8F44F0B202603A53B70AB9.description: Students can explain variations in wavelength and frequency in terms of the source of the vibrations that produce them, e.g., molecules, electrons, and nuclear particles.

7430ACEEEBDF420BA047A0AFC1E26D36.description: Electrical power and energy can be determined for electric circuits.

8293048FC3A14F2395E40C319D77EFC0.description: Circuit components may be connected in series or in parallel. Schematic diagrams are used to represent circuits and circuit elements.

CC2AF42281FA41A5982F88C0F0FD1362.description: A circuit is a closed path in which a current can exist.
comments: Note: Use conventional current.

6603DB012F1148E6811C5E75AC8AB663.description: The factors affecting resistance in a conductor are length, cross-sectional area, temperature, and resistivity.

CFBF014437694E2D867C8988FE3B79A3.description: All materials display a range of conductivity. At constant temperature, common metallic conductors obey Ohm's Law.

9E5D981B44E2449784EBA7516C84AD26.description: Moving electric charges produce magnetic fields. The relative motion between a conductor and a magnetic field may produce a potential difference in the conductor.

DCFB31BAF23C475FA846704B2D72588C.description: Energy may be stored in electric or magnetic fields. This energy may be transferred through conductors or space and may be converted to other forms of energy.

724C258695EC4C888C3FE58B7EC14ECB.description: Power is the time-rate at which work is done or energy is expended.

9930839F902A4F27BF11459688F5E420.description: Work done against friction results in an increase in the internal energy of the system.

A0E9031BB9ED4349BBCC80C4F47BF3D0.description: When work is done on or by a system, there is a change in the total energy of the system.

24E528119ABE4C76A4F256A3C2C17A54.description: In a nonideal mechanical system, as mechanical energy decreases there is a corresponding increase in other energies such as internal energy.

847908FF7FA543A7A2B6F55CBBC44822.description: In an ideal mechanical system, the sum of the macroscopic kinetic and potential energies (mechanical energy) is constant.

F6175D3F0C2248918BC21A91A845E27A.description: Kinetic energy is the energy an object possesses by virtue of its motion.

5AA6CD93AB8346DB9DAC54A7455CCFBB.description: Potential energy is the energy an object possesses by virtue of its position or condition. Types of potential energy include gravitational and elastic.

9782DE60DF9F4091B804871D692734A6.description: Energy may be converted among mechanical, electromagnetic, nuclear, and thermal forms.

BEC6116F36274D06A2D94037A5A78CE6.description: All energy transfers are governed by the law of conservation of energy.

63791005E2014760A6D2B1C321335DA8.description: Students can observe and describe transmission of various forms of energy.
comments: Note: Items with asterisks require quantitative treatment per the Reference Table for Physics. Asterisks following individual words refer to the preceding word or phrase only; asterisks appearing after the final period of a sentence refer to all concepts or ideas presented in the sentence.

E4C3E86CCFF84FD0B0E713B82D7FA139.description: Energy exists in many forms, and when these forms change energy is conserved.

3C072D7D8FDE4E4F908BBB3FF98001B0.description: Students will understand and apply scientific concepts, principles, and theories pertaining to the physical setting and living environment and recognize the historical development of ideas in science.

9A6315F7018B429F9516854E4D24F004.description: Information technology can have positive and negative impacts on society, depending upon how it is used.

943A7319E87E481C9DF6BD3F744975FA.description: Knowledge of the impacts and limitations of information systems is essential to its effective and ethical use.

4728ABA286CA4C9EA1BB6C1D9081792D.description: use software to model and extend classroom and laboratory experiences, recognizing the differences between the model used for understanding and realworld behavior

CC4946CB4D3A46AAA5B78AC6E471896A.description: Model solutions to a range of problems in mathematics, science, and technology using computer simulation software

2B69DD06C9614B55A5C42BB61882FAD7.description: Utilize electronic networks to share information

12419B5C8E4F4A03B0DDC7B188946335.description: use knowledge of physics to evaluate articles in the popular press on contemporary scientific topics

597C3E7533E643AFAC4BAD90A576466D.description: Access, select, collate, and analyze information obtained from a wide range of sources such as research data bases, foundations, organizations, national libraries, and electronic communication networks, including the Internet

1FC1F0B37306412DA3577552B282C428.description: use appropriate technology to gather experimental data, develop models, and present results

1CA7383FA28C4CD093D5ED26136A9648.description: extend knowledge of physical phenomena through independent investigation, e.g., literature review, electronic resources, library research

8A669DB414D244A096FEB0E4935D05CB.description: Prepare multimedia presentations demonstrating a clear sense of audience and purpose.
comments: Note: Multimedia may include posters, slides, images, presentation software, etc.

E8179B038D8645F98EBC336752EA55DD.description: Understand and use the more advanced features of word processing, spreadsheets, and data-base software

4776689DC1E04C86995FB3EFD78FF9A4.description: Information technology is used to retrieve, process, and communicate information as a tool to enhance learning.

D47E54904B9A494A8607780085DF7E0B.description: Students will access, generate, process, and transfer information, using appropriate technologies.

D8EEBEE6061C49DEAF8968EE90AC27CD.description: devise a test of the solution according to the design criteria and perform the test; record, portray, and logically evaluate performance test results through quantitative, graphic, and verbal means. Use a variety of creative verbal and graphic techniques effectively and persuasively to present conclusions, predict impacts and new problems, and suggest and pursue modifications

87460D5918614D8E9DA884567521FB15.description: develop work schedules and working plans which include optimal use and cost of materials, processes, time, and expertise; construct a model of the solution, incorporating developmental modifications while working to a high degree of quality (craftsmanship)

AB4BE205ABF741A28FA4F2C9EB232A43.description: generate creative solutions, break ideas into significant functional elements, and explore possible refinements; predict possible outcomes, using mathematical and functional modeling techniques; choose the optimal solution to the problem, clearly documenting ideas against design criteria and constraints; and explain how human understandings, economics, ergonomics, and environmental considerations have influenced the solution

4992E6874F364889808FDDFA4770E9F2.description: identify, locate, and use a wide range of information resources, and document through notes and sketches how findings relate to the problem

EEAD69D7591544ED8A187AE4A72C5FA4.description: initiate and carry out a thorough investigation of an unfamiliar situation and identify needs and opportunities for technological invention or innovation

06463B4E931C435FBDD1399865A8E01A.description: Students engage in the following steps of a design process:

7AB187948A704D9B8853FE76846468D0.description: Engineering design is an iterative process involving modeling and optimization (finding the best solution within given constraints) which is used to develop technological solutions to problems within given constraints.
comments: Note: The design process could apply to activities from simple investigations to long-term projects.

C5173C0CF7DC4006AB6E310587A85EF7.description: Based on the results of the test and through public discussion, revise the explanation and contemplate additional research.
comments: Note: Public discussion may include lab partners, lab groups, classes, etc.

10CF8293D86C46649DEE9F606EBEAC5B.description: Assess correspondence between the predicted result contained in the hypothesis and the actual result, and reach a conclusion as to whether or not the explanation on which the prediction was based is supported.

B3F85F31287C43B0A7A5458A5116A078.description: examine collected data to evaluate the reliability of experimental results, including percent error, range, standard deviation, line of best fit, and the use of the correct number of significant digits

A44E6D64C39F4BCBBA28C5FDF1C5A877.description: Apply statistical analysis techniques when appropriate to test if chance alone explains the result.

36BE8CD2F70E44E5952F4BAD035A6842.description: identify possible sources of error in data collection and explain their effects on experimental results

238CDB0463F64B61BD3644616E0A7BC8.description: use appropriate methods to present scientific information (e.g., lab reports, posters, research papers, or multimedia presentations)

649046EFD2564986A14D70D0592E0081.description: Use various means of representing and organizing observations (e.g., diagrams, tables, charts, graphs, and equations) and insightfully interpret the organized data.

BB5706AC58FE4F9B87F044965F7535C4.description: The observations made while testing proposed explanations, when analyzed using conventional and invented methods, provide new insights into phenomena.

FFDEE68070CF4CC3B294C03480F575F3.description: Carry out a research plan for testing explanations, including selecting and developing techniques, acquiring and building apparatus, and recording observations as necessary.
comments: Note: This could apply to many activities from simple investigations to long-term projects.

62F216DE087A403999A0D4E1DD905ED3.description: Develop and present proposals including formal hypotheses to test explanations; i.e., predict what should be observed under specific conditions if the explanation is true.

86EC999B55764CDE8686CC17665B53BE.description: Refine research ideas through library investigations, including electronic information retrieval and reviews of the literature, and through peer feedback obtained from review and discussion.

5A8E56DFA4FD47D9AFA4DA4F22C211F5.description: design an experiment to investigate the relationship between physical phenomena

7F598D039A214F828957A847A844EA94.description: Devise ways of making observations to test proposed explanations.

A95478F5C2F040C289D3AE6ACA755D77.description: Beyond the use of reasoning and consensus, scientific inquiry involves the testing of proposed explanations involving the use of conventional techniques and procedures and usually requiring considerable ingenuity.

FC8BBA0BB5FE4BED8E9EC5B2E5A24420.description: evaluate competing explanations and overcome misconceptions

473E05D2C8874E7AAB6232B6362C0656.description: clarify ideas through reasoning, research, and discussion

CD4BEBD172234840AA7759E893C5AC90.description: develop extended visual models and mathematical formulations to represent an understanding of natural phenomena

8C8D8F1EBDEB471DB22BB00577CB21BD.description: The central purpose of scientific inquiry is to develop explanations of natural phenomena in a continuing, creative process.

0993D40F874C40C283468649BF8EA7FC.description: explain the physical relevance of properties of a graphical representation of realworld data, e.g., slope, intercepts, area under the curve

5D9C32DA59D84ACE947612B2A5E7CB56.description: Apply algebraic and geometric concepts and skills to the solution of problems.

EC2940C350CF49AB81F9A4651819FE10.description: Critical thinking skills are used in the solution of mathematical problems.

F0C3B7E59FB3480BAC164F2BD014C34E.description: interpret graphs to determine the mathematical relationship between the variables

47F5093911B4450993AE254FA182A861.description: Use deductive reasoning to construct and evaluate conjectures and arguments, recognizing that patterns and relationships in mathematics assist them in arriving at these conjectures and arguments.

968E33A6CF4E4571B7DA673B09519315.description: Deductive and inductive reasoning are used to reach mathematical conclusions.

FEE1BEC9187245229BF083F99A0D0880.description: use dimensional analysis to confirm algebraic solutions

C8B120892C9746F28B7C5B3D4141F3FF.description: manipulate equations to solve for unknowns

8F99857392CB46C0AD0BD032A1B6DFDC.description: construct graphs of real-world data (scatter plots, line or curve of best fit)

C2F32CC5C2094D5696E691F82073898A.description: represent physical quantities in graphical form

7680E6A687A94C998821F7B8203A2882.description: use scaled diagrams to represent and manipulate vector quantities

9B4E3D4EEF054E0D8E8CC3BED55D23B0.description: Use algebraic and geometric representations to describe and compare data.

B3214DF5EB244A488A5F0BD4DDCA33E5.description: Abstraction and symbolic representation are used to communicate mathematically.

5D20E151440F495D94AE81A297F94C97.description: Students will use mathematical analysis, scientific inquiry, and engineering design, as appropriate, to pose questions, seek answers, and develop solutions.

80594F18558A42199FAB2D5591BF7E84.description:
If students are asked to do a project, then the project would require students to:
  • work effectively
  • gather and process information
  • generate and analyze ideas
  • observe common themes
  • realize ideas
  • present results

4C0EC59D8F17495887CB22688A73D5F8.description: Solving interdisciplinary problems involves a variety of skills and strategies, including effective work habits; gathering and processing information; generating and analyzing ideas; realizing ideas; making connections among the common themes of mathematics, science, and technology; and presenting results.

3AF99218875549BEA41AE6D6EBD7D0D6.description: design an experiment that requires the use of a mathematical concept to solve a scientific problem, e.g., an experiment to compare the density of different types of soda pop

DF18C16ADB004BA28AA93AEDAC4CC95F.description: Explain and evaluate phenomena mathematically and scientifically by formulating a testable hypothesis, demonstrating the logical connections between the scientific concepts guiding the hypothesis and the design of an experiment, applying and inquiring into the mathematical ideas relating to investigation of phenomena, and using (and if needed, designing) technological tools and procedures to assist in the investigation and in the communication of results.

FF284DB120724E2CB9802621F65CBCB4.description: design a potential solution to a regional problem, e.g., suggest a plan to adjust the acidity of a lake in the Adirondacks

2B9F6768B1DD41F692FD308C2213DBF9.description: Design solutions to real-world problems on a community, national, or global scale using a technological design process that integrates scientific investigation and rigorous mathematical analysis of the problem and of the solution

2551E0E103F64C68B875AB24963B6EF2.description: compare and analyze specific consumer products, e.g., antacids, vitamin C

0FD3257D88C94047A264B4D5822D4C61.description: Analyze and quantify consumer product data, understand environmental and economic impacts, develop a method for judging the value and efficacy of competing products, and discuss cost/benefit and risk/benefit tradeoffs made in arriving at the optimal choice

5ECA1446E07A41A3BDCC6821845FD6F2.description: carry out a remedial course of action by communicating the plan to others, e.g., writing and sending "a letter to the editor"

FAEBBC98BEDF4756884C4D1E8FEF1740.description: Analyze science/technology/society problems and issues on a community, national, or global scale and plan and carry out a remedial course of action

4DF58C7D44BD44D5B8D0250938A43928.description: The knowledge and skills of mathematics, science, and technology are used together to make informed decisions and solve problems, especially those relating to issues of science/ technology/society, consumer decision making, design, and inquiry into phenomena.

23C5736F8832474DACDB5DAB9F111A06.description: Students will apply the knowledge and thinking skills of mathematics, science, and technology to address real-life problems and make informed decisions.

BC3D58845B4C43CD942898ACC9A64E99.description: use graphs to identify patterns and interpret experimental data, e.g., heating and cooling curves

926C819BCF2B4F2EB93B7A43236C35C6.description: use graphs to make predictions, e.g., half-life, solubility

7AAA573C2E6441B6A8CFBBC2A1802C63.description: Identifying patterns of change is necessary for making predictions about future behavior and conditions.

DB17F457143C43D1B4747D098CD39C89.description: explain how a system returns to equilibrium in response to a stress, e.g., LeChatelier's principle

189EA469E06949EF932DA62396B37756.description: Cite specific examples of how dynamic equilibrium is achieved by equality of change in opposing directions.

BAF44F3C39674DA09F9DFBBA512E52C1.description: explain how a small change might not affect a system, e.g., activation energy

5B5FB3B827B14DCCBADA75E6EB6FF14E.description: Describe specific instances of how disturbances might affect a system's equilibrium, from small disturbances that do not upset the equilibrium to larger disturbances (threshold level) that cause the system to become unstable.

4D0A47DCD8AB407BB70CAE8E5D19DA4C.description: Equilibrium is a state of stability due either to a lack of change (static equilibrium) or a balance between opposing forces (dynamic equilibrium).

7979240D0B1E489BADCDE32CB6C691DF.description: use powers often to represent a large range of values for a physical quantity, e.g., pH scale

2FF3DD712BDA44F1983899BB5FE2607B.description: Extend the use of powers of ten notation to understanding the exponential function and performing operations with exponential factors.

DB730023C75D431A892D85B35E45FCBC.description: show how microscale processes can resemble or differ from real-world processes, e.g., microscale chemistry

6F325FDED8FB4C89A670BC1036E039CA.description: Describe the effects of changes in scale on the functioning of physical, biological, or designed systems

D1F37437A4D3436EA2650B236C64DD9E.description: The grouping of magnitudes of size, time, frequency, and pressures or other units of measurement into a series of relative order provides a useful way to deal with the immense range and the changes in scale that affect the behavior and design of systems.

8C50C77E6E3442C5BAB0321AC8E606E6.description: compare experimental results to a predicted value, e.g., percent error

F34F138475FB48A2B1ACC516BAAAE3F1.description: Compare predictions to actual observations, using test models.

E766B155B0D04AC98D7E9D00F39EF521.description: show how mathematical models (equations) describe a process, e.g., combined gas law

CC62E17EF3624311A0C584BEAAC2E7F1.description: Find and use mathematical models that behave in the same manner as the processes under investigation.

8CF23B9FEC964B4C98C164A6198A5397.description: show how information about a system is used to create a model, e.g., kinetic molecular theory (KMT)

8FDF5BA19F0241AB86C28D73A84A5070.description: Collect information about the behavior of a system and use modeling tools to represent the operation of the system

BA9C9A62F6014EDAB7FF65B927B1541E.description: show how models are revised in response to experimental evidence, e.g., atomic theory, Periodic Table

8D67C3B14A954D9483A710215EC8FBA5.description: Revise a model to create a more complete or improved representation of the system

C7043B6253324D9B9F470D40E1E90B0C.description: Models are simplified representations of objects, structures, or systems used in analysis, explanation, interpretation, or design.

E1B7976FC81D491B9A648BF196286A93.description: use the concept of systems and surroundings to describe heat flow in a chemical or physical change, e.g., dissolving process

B1A9614E9B3A4C46A36C2A61C7D5E921.description: Through systems thinking, people can recognize the commonalities that exist among all systems and how parts of a system interrelate and combine to perform specific functions.

49986664E817409BB616143F741D3A2E.description: Students will understand the relationships and common themes that connect mathematics, science, and technology and apply the themes to these and other areas of learning.

9E7F5C7FAAD043AC9525E8555993D4EC.description: Energy released during nuclear reactions is much greater than the energy released during chemical reactions.

DAF3973315254E8281FF061F08C7008D.description: Energy released in a nuclear reaction (fission or fusion) comes from the fractional amount of mass that is converted into energy. Nuclear changes convert matter into energy.

676D30F97701440F904BE11B5F7AEC18.description: A change in the nucleus of an atom that converts it from one element to another is called transmutation. This can occur naturally or can be induced by the bombardment of the nucleus with high-energy particles.

49E16DBE929A4174875B8795E27F0B37.description: Compare energy relationships within an atom's nucleus to those outside the nucleus
