F2D2A698DC234348978E9A4B25D3C3AB.description: Interpret a fraction as division of the numerator by the denominator (a/b = a ÷ b). Solve word problems involving division of whole numbers leading to answers in the form of fractions or mixed numbers.

Analyze the effects of various dancer interactions with production elements to intensify and heighten the artistic performance of a work, using dance and production terminology.

AC435A7A05344333AD445B2DC93F4D49.description: Recommend and implement various ways to adapt movements to a performance space. Document the process and progress over time in writing and in other media. Use performance etiquette and performance practices during class, rehearsal and performance. Post-performance, receive, record, and reflect upon notes from the choreographer, and apply corrections to future performances.

58EDFAE8F21F446A8FAD873292635864.description: Dance performance is an interaction between performers, production elements, and audience that heightens and amplifies artistic expression.

4463D235D20040AFB5400EBB807F0058.description: Convey meaning through the presentation of artistic work.

F8CA42CD750D4060BFC228F7C0BBB19E.description: Collaborate with peers to practice and refine dances. Develop group performance expectations, based upon observation and analyses (e.g. view live or recorded professional dancers, and collaboratively develop group performance expectations in response to information gained from observations).

0258D4B1ABDF44EFA9960D9C5108E19C.description: Employ healthful practices in dance and everyday life (e.g. good nutrition, adequate sleep, safe warm-ups). Discuss benefits of practices and how choices enhance performance.

6A5B6FB1F8E04AD1B460CE8E0ACD785D.description: Embody technical dance skills (e.g. functional alignment, coordination, balance, core support, kinesthetic awareness, clarity of movement, weight shifts, flexibility/range of motion). Apply somatic strategies to facilitate the performance of dance skills.

510C04C9DA2348D1A3664E180790757A.description: Dancers use the body-mind principles and develop the body as an instrument for artistry and artistic expression.

58D55D9DE0C1491099B31E6461235070.description: Develop and refine artistic techniques and work for presentation.

EA2C10E038C446FDB5D7D15EC79873A4.description: Compare and contrast movement characteristics from a variety of dance genres or styles. Examine the relationship between the movement dynamics, energy, and music. Discuss specific characteristics and determine what dancers must do to perform them clearly.

8CFA4E4351AC4256B712482DB8F5E18E.description: Vary dance phrasing by using accents and timing variations within a phrase to add interest kinesthetically, rhythmically, and visually.

EC31DECC25434FD684EC1F25F0C2C5D7.description: Expand movement vocabulary of spatial patterns/designs (floor and air). Incorporate and modify shapes and spatial elements from different dance genres and styles for interest and contrast.

35B967B8E571462B81307DEBD47D8709.description: Space, time, and energy are basic elements of dance.

E452EBD0546940F4852EB3143486A47D.description: Select, analyze, and interpret artistic work for presentation.

7B25F10F95BE4DB7947E2B3461AC20C0.description: Investigate a recognized system of documentation to record a dance sequence by using words, symbols, or media technologies.

40753C7D28E44F559B7EBCF4EB396E21.description: Evaluate possible revisions of dance compositions and reconsider artistic criteria, based on self-reflection, and peer and teacher feedback. Explain rationale for choices and how they clarify artistic intent.

1A7927532D3647E08EC12BE55923EE7D.description: Choreographers analyze, evaluate, refine, and document their work to communicate meaning.

FCEBE3D7ACF04B0A8F4BF86187B5B72E.description: Explore the possibilities of producing dance in a variety of venues and for different audiences, using production terminology to explain how production elements (e.g. music, props, costumes, lights, set, video) are handled in different situations. Analyze the impact of production and non-production professionals on the presentation of a dance.

4AD3C69F5C9B48C19E2F30E9BA1AE38E.description: Determine artistic criteria to choreograph a dance study that communicates personal or cultural meaning. Articulate how the artistic criteria inform the choreographic process.

1A6AC74A81C14A0D864D9B71A9509889.description: Use a variety of choreographic devices (e.g. counterpoint, solo vs. group, accumulation)and dance structures (e.g. theme and variation) with some teacher support to develop a dance study with a clear artistic intent. Articulate reasoning for movement, music and structural choices. Observe and describe peers' choreographic process.

8386A92D672C4DDB94A41632A658F191.description: The elements of dance, dance structures, and choreographic structures serve as both a foundation and a departure point for choreographers.

4BEE277ECBA347B981010C190F1402F3.description: Organize and develop artistic ideas and work.

D0C4A9F27F5E4B6D8E4488536A8EEC5D.description: Explore the elements of dance in various movement vocabularies to express an artistic intent in choreography. Explain and discuss the choices made, using genre-specific dance terminology.

E2EACDF089114D4AAFD18A8F596EE78C.description: Compare a variety of stimuli (e.g. music/sound, dance exemplars, literary forms, notation, natural phenomena, personal experiences/recall, world news, or social issues) and make selections to expand movement vocabulary and artistic expression for choreography.

A0741728EA4A4D0E9EC7AB6A18C8CF94.description: Choreographers are inspired by a variety of sources to convey concepts and ideas through movement for artistic expression.

6333A40B7C2C4D978D9D63706BE1C92D.description: Generate and conceptualize artistic ideas and work.

document.title: New York State Learning Standards for the Arts: Dance

E67C2557414040E58440B6E294C983E0.description: Analyze dances from several genres or styles, historical time periods, and/or cultural dance practices. Discuss how the movement characteristics, techniques, choreographic structures and devices, and purpose relate to the ideas and perspectives of the peoples from whom the dances originate. Identify and discuss the political, cultural, and historical significance of the dances and dance artists as related to social movements and change. Explain how this new knowledge has expanded one's dance literacy.

870275875D764555BF689BE8EA232C1F.description: Analyze danceworks or practices from several genres or styles, historical time periods, and/or cultural dance practices. Discuss how the movement characteristics, techniques, choreographic structures and devices, and purpose relate to the ideas and perspectives of the peoples from whom the dance works or practices originate. Identify and discuss the political, cultural, or historical significance of the dance works or practices and dance artists as related to social movements and change.

F6BFC1AD19E644C4A1A05ABE32D7A8F2.description: Formulate reasons for the similarities and differences between dance works or practices from selected genres, geographical locations, and/or historical time periods. Identify changes that the dance works or practices and dance artists have engendered in society.

4744617B3D844257A23F26BBC2870A6A.description: Societal, cultural, historical, and community contexts both influence and are influenced by dance.

49D3E773D30C433B9EEB0529A32F4788.description: Investigate ways that artistic work is influenced by societal, cultural, and historical context and, in turn, how artistic ideas shape cultures past, present, and future.

289CC8F22B914724B2D6D70C8C906994.description: Choose a personally relevant and controversial idea to research through text, interview, web-based resources, and other media. Develop questions and movement problems from the research. Create and perform choreography that addresses these issues. Discuss, orally or in writing, the insights relating to knowledge gained through the research process and personal growth resulting from the creation and performance of this dance.

69494D263AF345F292448363505C4F9E.description: Review original choreographies developed over time with respect to content and context and their relationship to personal knowledge and experiences. Reflect on and analyze the changes in one's personal growth and the variables that contributed to them.

8974672CE6854AFE9F0781158436BBE9.description: Use established research methods and techniques to investigate a topic other than dance. Collaborate with others to identify questions and solve movement problems that pertain to the topic. Create and perform a dance work based upon the research and discussion. Discuss, orally or in writing, the insights relating to knowledge gained through the research process, the synergy of collaboration, and the transfer of learning from this project to other learning situations.

C314C84DBAEE4CDF9AAB3E8855B78A43.description: Analyze a dance work that is related to content learned in other subjects and research its context. Synthesize information learned and share the effect that these new understandings have on one's perspective of the dance work.

C144CEDFBF414B3DAED8815FA7831896.description: Choose a concept from a field other than dance. Conduct research through text, interview, web-based resources, and/or other media. From the research, select relevant ideas and information and create a group dance work. Discuss how the dance work communicates new perspectives or realizations. Compare, orally and in writing, the choreographic process to that of other creative, academic, or scientific procedures.

FC09D299C1664EEC9BC18BB436C1614F.description: Examine the dance works of known choreographers and original classroom work and identify factors in personal experience and knowledge that shape interpretation and creation.

B58BA252BC794D9694B650F0887B1656.description: Personal experiences, knowledge, and contexts are integrated and synthesized to interpret and create dance.

F86245897C8341B4B2ED638BBE8A551A.description: Relate and synthesize knowledge and personal experiences to inspire and inform artistic work.

86B0935F79D543EBA6F9FE964DEEE0E0.description: Apply personal artistic preferences to the critique of dance works and practices. Consider societal and personal values, and a range of artistic expression. Discuss perspectives with peers and justify views. Evaluate and revise criteria by applying insights gained from these considerations and discussions.

D817E8AAB6B349CA94565C335BF490EF.description: Compare and contrast two or more dance works or practices, using criteria to evaluate their overall effectiveness and situating the criteria within a cultural context. Consider societal values and a range of perspectives. Use genre-specific dance terminology.

B214D352FB6A4213B0A6505944D34227.description: Identify and use evaluative criteria to assess the overall effectiveness of dance works or practices. Relate the criteria to their cultural context. Use genre-specific dance terminology.

95C38A8C8A8C483BA32D59159F9EDDF2.description: Criteria for evaluating dance vary across genres, styles, and cultures.

816EC21A90AF45BCBF3AB5CF3B6C97D7.description: Apply criteria to evaluate artistic work.

02AD0D507C474D0BB9873F6E47EDC8C4.description: Analyze and interpret how the elements of dance, execution of dance elements, production elements, and context contribute to artistic expression, meaning, and artistic intent, across different genres, styles, or cultural movement practices. Use genre-specific dance terminology.

E8C2C10CAA84469D833CF4ED89B23D32.description: Analyze, compare, and contrast different dances. Research and discuss artistic intent and meaning. Explain how the relationships among the elements of dance, technique, structures, production elements, and context enhance meaning and support artistic intent, using genre-specific dance terminology.

EDD15D98D2924EDB8B6180E067B86A4A.description: Analyze and discuss how the elements of dance, technique, structure, and context contribute to artistic expression and meaning. Use genre-specific dance terminology.

1E196F83C93C443594677D29D3D118EB.description: Meaningful interpretations of dance consider artistic intent, style, genre, the elements of dance, technique, structure, and context.

C5C9B10F6D0F4C42837E971C8E6B080F.description: Explain how the movements and compositional structures of a dance communicate aesthetic and cultural values in a variety of genres, styles, and cultural movement practices. Use terminology specific to the dance form or practice.

08FB23D3816B41569204CAF585869661.description: Compare, contrast, and analyze dance works from a variety of dance genres and styles and explain how choreographic devices and structures, dynamics, formations and recurring patterns of movement and their relationships create well-structured choreography. Critically examine and evaluate the overall effect that the organization of these components has on different dances. Provide evidence and rationale for critiques.

68039C59FCD84FDDAD34F7028032A9BB.description: Within the cultural context, analyze and compare patterns of movement, and the relationships between them in a variety of genres, styles, and cultural movement practices. Use terminology specific to the dance form or practice.

0E904ADB433A42308F7714E42805705A.description: Compare, contrast, and analyze dance works within a single genre or style, and provide examples of recurring patterns of movement, choreographic devices and structures, and the relationships between them. Critically examine the overall effect that the organization of these components has on different dances. Provide evidence and rationale for critiques.

8EF5498EB5F9498A9D8E8197063F4794.description: Analyze how the elements of dance are used in a variety of genres, styles, and cultural movement practices within their cultural context. Use terminology specific to the dance form or practice.

DC5AFA402A0842648A6041EB57961E83.description: Compare, contrast, and analyze dynamics, patterns of movement, key motifs, and choreographic devices and structures, and their relationships. Explain how they support the structure and artistic expression of the dance. Examine how the dance's structure relates to its effect, and defend an analysis, citing specific evidence.

EFAF03FD68DE43C2A4D1C35C455E565E.description: Dance is perceived and analyzed to comprehend its compositional structure.

C3A3252A633042B48A7AE3136FCB50B3.description: As dancers: Rehearse with production elements to create a performance that is a unified whole during which movement/choreography melds seamlessly with non-movement elements to heighten and amplify artistic expression. As dancers and choreographers: Work collaboratively to produce dance concerts in a variety of venues. As choreographers: Direct the use of production elements that would be necessary to fulfill the artistic intent of the dance works in each of the venues (act as artistic director).

469F650F74CD46B1AF3AAAEB481F8246.description: Demonstrate commitment, dependability, responsibility, and cooperation when preparing for performances. Model performance etiquette and performance practices during class, rehearsal, and performance. Enhance performance by using a broad repertoire of strategies for dynamic projection. Develop a professional portfolio (resume, headshot, etc.) that documents the rehearsal and performance process with fluency in professional dance and production terminology. As choreographers: Give notes that guide the dancers to strengthen their performance and the conveyance of the dance's artistic intent to the audience.

7CC4A12EE9AC4E88B599FE57B1E073C7.description: As dancers: Rehearse with production elements to create a performance during which movement/choreography works with non-movement elements to heighten and amplify artistic expression. As choreographers: Work collaboratively to produce a dance concert on a stage or in an alternative performance venue.

47DBE90512584AB880D8C166515198E8.description: As choreographers and dancers: Demonstrate commitment, dependability, responsibility, and cooperation when preparing for performances. Document the rehearsal and performance process and evaluate methods and strategies using dance and production terminology. Model performance etiquette and performance practices during class, rehearsal, and performance. Implement performance strategies to enhance projection. As dancers: Post-rehearsal, and post-performance, accept notes from the choreographer and apply corrections to future performances.

42652B642BB843978BDCED80DF37B732.description: As dancers: Rehearse with the production elements to create a performance that expresses the choreographer's artistic intent. As choreographers: Evaluate possible designs for the production elements of a performance and select and execute the ideas that would intensify and heighten the artistic intent of the dances.

E7BC5CFA14044737ABF802E8D3794D16.description: Demonstrate commitment, dependability, responsibility, and cooperation when preparing for performances. Document the rehearsal and performance process and evaluate methods and strategies, using dance and production terminology. Demonstrate performance etiquette and performance practices during class, rehearsal, and performance. Post-performance, accept notes from the choreographer and apply corrections to future performances.

C644A0CCC85C448091E0277EB11F681A.description: Dance performance is an interaction between performers, production elements, and audience that heightens and amplifies artistic expression.

312A8C7DF8EF4F31A83AE509A6D91484.description: Convey meaning through the presentation of artistic work.

F305B415ED294A20ADBE45CC5098A103.description: Initiate, plan, and direct rehearsals with attention to technical details and fulfilling artistic expression. Use a range of rehearsal strategies to achieve performance excellence.

1DF6CB11B4524381A89B1098E2713956.description: Research healthful and safe practices for dancers and modify personal practice, based on findings. Discuss how research informs personal practice.

70127856CDD54C50A6F9F357EEF96EB7.description: As dancers: Apply body-mind principles to technical dance skills in complex choreography when performing solo, partnering, or dancing in ensemble works in a variety of dance genres and styles. Self-evaluate performances and discuss and analyze performance ability with others. As choreographers: Work closely with dancers to help them understand and internalize the concepts around which the dance work is built. Discuss and encourage the dancers to embody the meaning of the work within their use of the dance elements and their technique.

9BBAE632C1814E57A8B6B3390D102450.description: Plan and execute collaborative and independent practice and rehearsal processes with attention to technique and artistry informed by personal performance goals. Perform thoughtful and repetitive practice of techniques and skills before and during rehearsal of dances. Apply feedback to daily practice to improve technical and expressive skills. Reflect on personal achievements.

C054734E68AC41168DBD103E6AC06097.description: Apply anatomical principles and healthful practices to a range of technical dance skills for achieving fluency of movement. Follow and reflect upon the implementation of a personal nutrition plan that supports health for everyday life. Know basic first aid for injuries and what to do to help speed and ensure recovery.

AA6A616D0D2A4F21A683E774B2F14305.description: As dancers: Dance with sensibility toward other dancers while executing complex spatial, rhythmic, and dynamic sequences to meet performance goals. Move and dance with sensibility toward self, developing an understanding and awareness of the integration of cognition, body, and expression. Dance "in the moment." As choreographers: Observe and critique the spatial execution by the dancers; give corrections and/or make changes that improve/enhance the communication or expression of the ideas central to the dance.

2949A83BF7FC41F0AFECEA646CAA79D0.description: Collaborate with peers to establish and implement a rehearsal plan to meet performance goals. Use a variety of strategies to analyze and evaluate performances of self and others (e.g. use video recordings or practice to analyze the difference between the way movements look and how they feel to match performance with visual affect). Articulate performance goals and justify reasons for selecting particular practice strategies.

6D1779E4690D4AA9A4F2FA15A5E70A79.description: Develop and apply a plan for healthful practices in dance activities and everyday life including nutrition and injury prevention. Identify and discuss implementation of anatomical principles and nutrition-related practices and reflect upon how they support personal performance goals.

14D17C8DB15A4F9C809B10FAA455A6B1.description: Embody technical dance skills to retain and execute full dance choreographies, continuing to develop somatic strategies.

F2BA5B741F8C4D44BB62E3696F084794.description: Dancers use the body-mind principles and develop the body as an instrument for artistry and artistic expression.

C14BDCF046DA404782A1A43BB4E316C7.description: Develop and refine artistic techniques and work for presentation.

2BB21DE0F3D44EA68CDC4E9E5E70CD5A.description: Modulate dynamics to clearly express artistic intent and musicality while performing dance phrases and choreography. Perform movement sequences expressively by using a broad dynamic range and employ dynamic skills for establishing relationships with other dancers and projecting to the audience.

E70BA293382F4E1496D64B743E3FF245.description: Modulate time factors for artistic interest and expressive acuity. Demonstrate complexity in phrasing with and without musical accompaniment. Use multiple and complex rhythms (e.g., contrapuntal, and/or polyrhythmic) at the same time. Work with and against rhythm of accompaniment or sound environments.

86014A5F2FA64067973C30E648268249.description: Modulate and use the broadest range of movement in space for artistic and expressive clarity. Use inward and outward focus to clarify movement and artistic intent. Establish and break spatial and conceptual relationships with other dancers and audience as appropriate to the dance.

71D1AE253AB94F8496EC61D9608428D4.description: Vary energy and dynamics over the length of a dance phrase. Transition smoothly between dance phrases, paying close attention to movement initiation and energy, and the relation to music (if present). Apply these skills in ways that express the ideas of the choreographer/choreography.

9EDA680D17894EAABE5DC8E1B834F292.description: Perform dance studies and compositions that use time and tempo in unpredictable ways. Use internal rhythms and kinetics as phrasing tools. Apply these skills in ways that express the ideas of the choreographer/choreography.

95FE20EAD69147C885D2414BF2739282.description: Dance alone and with others with spatial intention. Expand partner and ensemble skills to greater ranges and skill levels. Execute complex floor and air sequences with others while maintaining relationships through focus and intentionality. Apply these skills in ways that express the ideas of the choreographer/choreography.

2B6EFBA0AC0D49CCBC1A41162F259ECF.description: Connect energy and dynamics to movements by applying them in and through all parts of the body. Develop whole body awareness so that dance phrases demonstrate variations of energy, dynamics, and musicality.

B4BED37819D84DC8AC3B59E2B06139BC.description: Use syncopation and accent movement related to different tempi. Take rhythmic cues from different aspects of accompaniment. Integrates breath phrasing with metric and kinesthetic phrasing.

701FCF0C96A4431DA17142FA823FB62E.description: Develop partner and ensemble skills that enable contrasting level changes while maintaining a sense of spatial design and relationship. Use space intentionally during dance phrases and through transitions between dance phrases. Establish and break physical and conceptual relationships with others as appropriate to the choreography.

C0D58902EE7D4A5995EE9F71CB97069B.description: Space, time, and energy are basic elements of dance.

E772B856858F4CD69152A55C2662C469.description: Select, analyze, and interpret artistic work for presentation.

13740F495308442889F39D86B4488A0C.description: Document a dance (formations, steps, dynamics, artistic intent, expressions) as a tool to remember ideas and revisions, and for reflection and feedback using systems of dance documentation (e.g. writing, a form of notation symbols, or using media technologies). Peer and self-review will be facilitated by the use of media technologies.

F23383BD32EE4D82B6C974587FF6112C.description: Clarify the artistic intent of a dance by manipulating and refining choreographic devices, dance structures, and artistic criteria, using self-reflection and feedback from others. Document choices made in the revision process and justify how the refinements support artistic intent.

937530168CE444EDAD5279AB514B21B5.description: Research one or more official dance notation systems. Record the formations and dance phrases of the dances created in the class using a system of dance documentation (e.g. writing, a form of notation symbols, or using media technologies), in order to remember phrases, movement ideas, and revisions. Peer and self-review will be facilitated by the use of media technologies.

BA3740B46F094157B5F6B1F70D6B6BA4.description: Clarify the artistic intent of a dance by refining choreographic devices and dance structures, independently or collaboratively, using established artistic criteria, self-reflection and the feedback of others. Analyze and evaluate impact of choices made in the revision process.

EDC21AD152994D6D9358D4A888506656.description: Compare and discuss recognized systems of documentation used to document dance using writing, symbols, or media technologies. Develop a strategy to record sections of a dance in order to remember dance phrases, movement ideas and revision. Peer and self-review will be facilitated by the use of media technologies.

0F7F4C5D97AC4F86A06C909E9D791AA7.description: Clarify the artistic intent of a dance by manipulating choreographic devices and dance structures, based on established artistic criteria and feedback from others. Analyze and evaluate impact of choices made in the revision process.

ADDC80EAAA204DC8B9B9EEEA1CF8A548.description: Choreographers analyze, evaluate, refine, and document their work to communicate meaning.

A42406C47B7E470B9B958BB2FD5A8321.description: Research choreographers who have worked in alternative performance venues, focusing on site-specific pieces, and choreographers who have collaborated with theatre and/or visual and media artists, to create dances that were "outside the box" of the theatrical dance of the time. Using this knowledge, develop a plan for a work or works that are interdisciplinary or site-specific.

D6F91A47CD1F4A45937DCCA644740C16.description: Construct an artistic statement that communicates a personal, cultural and artistic perspective. Discuss how the movement elements, choreographic devices and dance structures serve to support the artistic structures serve to statement. Support the artistic statement.

E0FB30F6A92C47E5AC45409E4FE816F7.description: Demonstrate fluency and personal voice in designing and choreographing original dances. Justify choreographic choices and explain how they are used to intensify artistic intent.

0B6E6BB1174949A6B3F7ADF02D745C55.description: Collaborate with theatre technicians and designers to create a comprehensive integration of movement and production elements that intensifies and heightens the artistic intent of the work. Document the design, and explain the connection between the design, the artistic intent of the dance, and the artistic statement. Using primary and secondary sources, research the role of non-dance theatre professionals in dance productions, and the technical expertise and various processes that are used to design the production elements in performance. Consider traditional and alternative performance venues.

CE3E2637691C404B8EA601EEDEBF6632.description: Develop an artistic statement that communicates a personal aesthetic, motivation, and artistic intent of an original dance study or dance. Discuss how the movement elements, choreographic devices and dance.

A0B00A5F088A4F48A0465C17DCE22133.description: Work individually and collaboratively to design and implement a variety of choreographic processes and devices and dance structures to develop original dances. Analyze how the structure and final composition informs the artistic intent.

01241C8A7A084101BEEA8CF2B50F7F99.description: Refine the process of selecting production elements that intensify and heighten the artistic intent of the work. Inhabit the various roles of lighting, sound, costume designers and/or composers to design a comprehensive integration of movement and production elements. Explain the connection between the design, the artistic intent of the dance, and the artistic statement. Research how professional choreographers in a variety of genres work and have worked with other theatre professionals.

E323E93D6F594AEF8828F6790CC6888C.description: Develop an artistic statement that communicates the artistic intent of an original dance study or dance. Select and demonstrate movements that support the artistic statement.

298147E964B64133B7E7009FF46CCF57.description: Collaborate to design a dance using choreographic processes and devices, and dance structures such as improvisation, observation, abstraction, randomization, rondo, canon, motif, retrograde, etc., to support an artistic intent. Explain how the choreographic devices, dance structures, and movement choices clarify, communicate, or effect the artistic intent.

7791ED1ADB0645498C2C6860506F19C3.description: The elements of dance, dance structures, and choreographic structures serve as both a foundation and a departure point for choreographers.

001D81B2AB7944A69145A22F0D2ADD14.description: Organize and develop artistic ideas and work.

AECD23B90115465886E702D908B53C39.description: Expand personal movement preferences and strengths to discover new and unfamiliar solutions to communicate the artistic intent of an original dance work. Analyze the new and unfamiliar solutions, the use and variation of the elements of dance, and explain why they were effective in expanding artistic intent.

675718070DB9436CAF369490224E92F8.description: Synthesize content generated from stimulus material. Experiment and take risks to discover a personal voice to communicate artistic intent.

ACACE8037E284F30A499EAF23A3B3474.description: Apply personal movement preferences and strengths with the movement vocabulary of several dance styles or genres to choreograph an original dance study or dance work that varies the elements of dance in such a way as to communicate an artistic intent. Compare personal choices to those made

A4CAFC88F460427EBE45949124FD8D66.description: Synthesize content generated from stimulus materials to choreograph dance studies or dance works, using original and codified movement.

351091273BA1487EA27F5F35FCC0233C.description: Experiment with the elements of dance to explore personal movement preferences and strengths, and select movements that challenge skills and build on strengths in an original dance study or dance. View and discuss the dances of a variety of recognized choreographers, to see what choices they have made.

47421B6270F6432C8F65E17D7F507BBD.description: Explore a variety of stimuli for sourcing movement to develop an improvisational or choreographed dance study. Analyze the process and the relationship between the stimuli and the movement.

4423F29BD50A4D31BFA885C187D49031.description: Choreographers are inspired by a variety of sources to convey concepts and ideas through movement for artistic expression.

7AA62255618B4AF6B1338D489A7785E2.description: Generate and conceptualize artistic ideas and work.

document.title: New York State Learning Standards for the Arts: Dance

D39160C808D84574ACF5BB40C42025D7.description: View and perform a dance work or practice from a different culture or context. Discuss the types of movements performed.

AE91CA8584F6472EA8A4873C98ED94B7.description: Societal, cultural, historical, and community contexts both influence and are influenced by dance.

960FB86D0914405F991E4BFEC8399075.description: Investigate ways that artistic work is influenced by societal, cultural, and historical context and, in turn, how artistic ideas shape cultures past, present, and future.

50803B1387A046E4885A478710136564.description: Observe illustrations from a story book. Discuss observations and identify ideas that inspire movement. Perform a dance sequence that portrays the main ideas from the story.

AA6F847EEB904B03A9DE45DD998B6CEA.description: Recognize an emotion expressed or portrayed in a dance work or practice that relates to a familiar experience. Identify and analyze the movements that communicate this emotion.

B3EDF1FA642540418C249657D551BCA2.description: Personal experiences, knowledge, and contexts are integrated and synthesized to interpret and create dance.

074BC911DDE14FB3867A6AA4F49EBE4B.description: Relate and synthesize knowledge and personal experiences to inspire and inform artistic work.

D3BDC4F4BC794C6AAA7828FEDB7E624A.description: Identify and demonstrate several movements in a dance work or practice. Explain what characteristics make the movements interesting.

A13EAC7EE71A493B8AE143BC5594DA79.description: Criteria for evaluating dance vary across genres, styles, and cultures.

865C8AB56A364549B51DDA782E36A936.description: Apply criteria to evaluate artistic work.

156853E6FF1549F981407CAD75C2D195.description: Select movements from a dance that suggest ideas and explain how the movements capture the ideas, using simple dance terminology.

BCDDBB375402445EA78F0187B6B4A51F.description: Demonstrate and describe observed or performed movements originating from diverse dance genres and cultural movement practices.

0045DA339D534FF19AF67886B6493BF3.description: Identify movements that repeat to make a pattern in a dance.

601977EBE55446FDB79B9B865B4EC7EE.description: Dance is perceived and analyzed to comprehend its compositional structure.

9C9F123385594E2A87AF912D3FA76BB8.description: Explore moving with simple props to enhance performance.

F3D7BF5CB47940018097CE42F13A3F30.description: Dance for and with others while maintaining awareness of performance expectations as a dancer (e.g. silence, focus) in both formal and informal settings. Demonstrate audience member expectations (e.g. attention, applause).

68961F4701CE4554BE599CE4578B99C9.description: Repeat and recall movements and spatial formations upon request in preparation for formal and informal sharing.

983953489EEB458B88059C8C48AF624B.description: Move safely in general space during movement explorations, while changing levels and maintaining personal space.

52E4BB1299FD4E5D9F87FC35DA0D425B.description: Demonstrate same side and cross-body locomotor (e.g. gallop, skip) and non-locomotor movements (e.g. swing, twist, stretch), and spatial relationships (e.g., over, under, around, through). 844DEB929E7D4C75B9AB9269023666CC.description: Develop and refine artistic techniques and work for presentation.

C687B32587E745328F37DBEDE1C56179.description: Space, time, and energy are basic elements of dance.

1C84D491371A45BAAD14FE5B4F7E727F.description: Document a short movement sequence (e.g. jump, turn, slide) by drawing a picture, using a symbol, or working with media technology.

2954A7991D1A4C31AC26B87A7B05791E.description: Apply self, peer, and teacher suggestions to revise and complete short sequences based on own movement ideas.

5A398BE7DBBA48FABF1C0CDE07FE1F6D.description: Choreographers analyze, evaluate, refine, and document their work to communicate meaning.

2B8305E5C00446F895380A40AFEF9992.description: Identify and explore production elements (e.g. music/sound, props) that support performances. Describe the job of a dancer, choreographer, and composer.

E0E2DB10F9B84744B571983248163FE2.description: Choose and arrange movements that follow a musical phrase, express an idea or emotion in response to other people, objects, or the environment.

8B090D325A1747D1A68A6705A40032A2.description: Improvise a dance phrase with a clear beginning, middle, and end. Describe the movement choices made, orally or in drawing.

38666C2F44414C44ACB2C9081FFEA869.description: The elements of dance, dance structures, and choreographic structures serve as both a foundation and a departure point for choreographers.

3FD10633D0044E1BB2BEC9C44C407467.description: Organize and develop artistic ideas and work.

677F0FE254CE42AAB63D28D07F92E7D4.description: Explore a variety of locomotor and non-locomotor movements by experimenting with the elements of dance in response to the environment and a range of themes.

96104E8178724A67959174763876E2F5.description: Explore movement elements and skills inspired by a variety of stimuli (e.g. music/sound, text, objects/props, images, symbols, observed dance through video or live performance) and identify the source.

C7AE68CB055343A8B3402AF1463C9C25.description: Generate and conceptualize artistic ideas and work.

document.title: New York State Next Generation Mathematics Learning Standards (K-8)

543279FCC3DA428F8957FAA5FEBE3C7E.description: Compare two decimals to hundredths by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when two decimals refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions.

2F84349C67AE439D880E3C278EAFAD1E.description: Use decimal notation for fractions with denominators 10 or 100.

E76FDF3EFDE744BF9F506C8F1B019F74.description: Express a fraction with denominator 10 as an equivalent fraction with denominator 100, and use this technique to add two fractions with respective denominators 10 and 100.

B1643D3D3D7F448788F92638DE3E86A9.description: Understand decimal notation for fractions, and compare decimal fractions.

19CD7560CF07429AB1DF3FE6381E5B47.description: Solve word problems involving multiplication of a whole number by a fraction.

8AC48AF35FCD4B0F915EF189D6DF5930.description: Understand a multiple of a/b as a multiple of 1/b, and use this understanding to multiply a whole number by a fraction.

784E059C72D346D2B7997DE8083C8971.description: Understand a fraction a/b as a multiple of 1/b.

603BADFFBCA143CDA703D49E736E1AE2.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a whole number by a fraction.

26625808485F4B9EA0F5669FB2FCCA1F.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole and having like denominators.

E8D1974D2A714EBA8E309EF2A862C773.description: Add and subtract mixed numbers with like denominators.

3C653AC657EE40FC871A427C925F2591.description: Decompose a fraction into a sum of fractions with the same denominator in more than one way, recording each decomposition by an equation. Justify decompositions.

D3D37BB176324E29B383F68831C2517B.description: Understand addition and subtraction of fractions as joining and separating parts referring to the same whole.

ABE55D9B930741FE86290E101D7211BB.description: Understand a fraction a/b with a > 1 as a sum of fractions 1/b.

5D3FDA116AB24C6682BB39459A70B5DA.description: Build fractions from unit fractions by applying and extending previous understandings of operations on whole numbers.

6F999B88AF2B43B19D2FD2D3DD4C4216.description: Compare two fractions with different numerators and different denominators. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with symbols >, =, or <, and justify the conclusions.

D2A7095FE3CB4AE5A351D97EF7FECE93.description: Explain why a fraction a/b is equivalent to a fraction a×n/b×n by using visual fraction models, with attention to how the number and size of the parts differ even though the two fractions themselves are the same size. Use this principle to recognize and generate equivalent fractions.

56CD8C04B6FE4DD18F7EE6AF91A4288A.description: Extend understanding of fraction equivalence and ordering.

3C3909A615204F96AB3FCA01FF873594.description: Use place value understanding to round multi-digit whole numbers to any place.

DCD83F6278C64ED5BED40E2704224617.description: Compare two multi-digit numbers based on meanings of the digits in each place, using >, =, and < symbols to record the results of comparisons.

5BB99A38C31347229FF464EF694A3E52.description: Read and write multi-digit whole numbers using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form.

2E297E6319A843AB927B02C69BADC0E2.description: Recognize that in a multi-digit whole number, a digit in one place represents ten times what it represents in the place to its right.

19414E26910249FA911CC670D91C2133.description: Generalize place value understanding for multi-digit whole numbers.

74FB8F4829DC421497DC145005E52F52.description: Find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

2A659A91F258442F863E7D8AB330A6F2.description: Multiply a whole number of up to four digits by a one-digit whole number, and multiply two two-digit numbers, using strategies based on place value and the properties of operations. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

8914FCF9FA434835B76952AFAEBC7A18.description: Fluently add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers using a standard algorithm.

B20166D40BD54262BE63D6D43BB70847.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.

A979B92969F24218B8649AA883E8967D.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

D823122DF7564A58924E8C55F6C43CCC.description: Recognize a line of symmetry for a two-dimensional figure as a line across the figure such that the figure can be folded along the line into matching parts. Identify line-symmetric figures and draw lines of symmetry.

485029CB08EE46E39CBBFD6890FF9EF5.description: Identify and name all quadrilaterals with four right angles as rectangles.

8FAA4FEE87914EBB92168BC4CC097264.description: Identify and name all quadrilaterals with 2 pairs of parallel sides as parallelograms.

AA147D6D4F084AE6A1CCAFB723CEC710.description: Identify and name triangles based on angle size (right, obtuse, acute).

6A3105E7EB7E4D8F974B9B7647D0F407.description: Draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines. Identify these in two-dimensional figures.

46DED46B320C42A79C101D349448CAEB.description: Draw and identify lines and angles, and classify shapes by properties of their lines and angles.

90BD29BCE0F64BE9B272631F6BD42B7D.description: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (½, ¼, 1/8). Solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions by using information presented in line plots.

5D41471562FC4C03AA2BDD7DE30D305E.description: Recognize angle measure as additive. When an angle is decomposed into non-overlapping parts, the angle measure of the whole is the sum of the angle measures of the parts. Solve addition and subtraction problems to find unknown angles on a diagram in real world and mathematical problems.

76FCEBFA62774740BF5B18AF6AA45EE5.description: Measure angles in whole-number degrees using a protractor. Sketch angles of specified measure.

1396CDEDC3174D50A3C28BD4E511EE1F.description: Recognize an angle that turns through n one-degree angles is said to have an angle measure of n degrees.

3FC7CC541D35490EB544FC8145909937.description: Recognize an angle is measured with reference to a circle with its center at the common endpoint of the rays, by considering the fraction of the circular arc between the points where the two rays intersect the circle. An angle that turns through 1/360 of a circle is called a "one-degree angle," and can be used to measure angles.

D104272840FF4CC1911407FCB9C0C3A7.description: Recognize angles as geometric shapes that are formed wherever two rays share a common endpoint, and understand concepts of angle measurement.

27E99A517D174F11B10F67385170B2EA.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of angle and measure angles.

5EBAF4AC674440E492A6CD741C26749D.description: Apply the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real world and mathematical problems.

4C02EC22A3C442EA92B9EABFD0AA488C.description: Represent measurement quantities using diagrams that feature a measurement scale, such as number lines.

DCF79D012D734B119840EF6A9353008E.description: Solve problems involving fractions or decimals, and problems that require expressing measurements given in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit.

BDF7C1FBF5CD40C180BAC6F953CCA7C3.description: Use the four operations to solve word problems involving distances, intervals of time, liquid volumes, masses of objects, and money.

B25FD29A03174C09AED350B45B39F3C3.description:
Know relative sizes of measurement units: ft., in.; km, m, cm
  • Know the conversion factor and use it to convert measurements in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit: ft., in.; km, m, cm; hr., min., sec.
  • Given the conversion factor, convert all other measurements within a single system of measurement from a larger unit to a smaller unit.
  • Record measurement equivalents in a two-column table.

F42EA20320EE45808FC9159F84603029.description: Solve problems involving measurement and conversion of measurements from a larger unit to a smaller unit.

4C86A7AA194A41939112CB758931410A.description: Generate a number or shape pattern that follows a given rule. Identify and informally explain apparent features of the pattern that were not explicit in the rule itself.

34F9A6713E8249EA929F13571B80B262.description: Find all factor pairs for a whole number in the range 1–100. Recognize that a whole number is a multiple of each of its factors. Determine whether a given whole number in the range 1–100 is a multiple of a given one-digit number. Determine whether a given whole number in the range 1-100 is prime or composite.

D57B0CF248FE47DABFAC60577F74313D.description: Gain familiarity with factors and multiples.

12A68BFD463640FCBC0787D7A842F2A2.description: Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.

A8A5F1DB880E476A841DA04C3D60A765.description: Represent these problems using equations or expressions with a letter standing for the unknown quantity.

5C834302B99B437397ADC17F6BADE7B8.description: Solve multistep word problems posed with whole numbers and having whole-number answers using the four operations, including problems in which remainders must be interpreted.

295E2F7F5F83480F8D9D1000730AE5D7.description: Multiply or divide to solve word problems involving multiplicative comparison, distinguishing multiplicative comparison from additive comparison. Use drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.

F9DD6BB796E84832868FB4BE497E0DAE.description: Interpret a multiplication equation as a comparison. Represent verbal statements of multiplicative comparisons as multiplication equations.

3B901BA2E6DA4BD9AFEB28F71A7F1363.description: Use the four operations with whole numbers to solve problems.

12460D4D6F5445578A5F2E5D82FE7CFF.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

995E89F9D27C4433A74ACBFC82D17FE2.description: Look for and make use of structure.

BED542E5C2A0432A88BA3C979DF33847.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

DB2E631E2CA84EB480BAAC0126168263.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: New York State Learning Standards for the Arts: Dance

673655DFD8E5404CAC04B2FE7C44BD48.description: Describe how the movement characteristics and qualities of a dance in a specific dance genre or style communicate the ideas of the culture, historical period, or community from which it originated.

F456BCC8AAE04AE0897E5FCA55E81092.description: Societal, cultural, historical, and community contexts both influence and are influenced by dance.

697866E514DC4042ABFD5D77C8061CB8.description: Investigate ways that artistic work is influenced by societal, cultural, and historical context and, in turn, how artistic ideas shape cultures past, present, and future.

1A404ABCADA44A81975A2090D72731AD.description: Choose a topic, concept, or content from another discipline of study and research how other art forms have expressed the topic. 07C078FBBC6448A09BDA47803D8C0453.description: Compare two dances with contrasting themes. Discuss feelings and ideas evoked by each. Describe how the themes and movements relate to points of view and experiences.

6D3E66569E47427380FDC82F789A7D65.description: Personal experiences, knowledge, and contexts are integrated and synthesized to interpret and create dance.

9B53F9102DF446A888FA248A2DCA2536.description: Relate and synthesize knowledge and personal experiences to inspire and inform artistic work.

A47295C935AC4AD89E71FCFDA3F24372.description: Define the characteristics of a dance that give it a strong overall impression, in relation to the elements of dance in genres, styles, or cultural movement practices. Generate, with peers, criteria for excellence in a dance, considering its cultural context. Use genre-specific dance terminology when appropriate.

B8093061CF59412FB3EB97D6F4DE431A.description: Criteria for evaluating dance vary across genres, styles, and cultures.

CBD0B91E59D34D16BCF2F914C452250A.description: Apply criteria to evaluate artistic work.

483F1D59E2284E349273118E10F18C31.description: Interpret meaning in a dance from its movements and context. Explain how the movements communicate the main idea of the dance, using genre-specific dance terminology when appropriate.

A22DEE093C5842F982CF29379541BEBF.description: Meaningful interpretations of dance consider artistic intent, style, genre, the elements of dance, technique, structure, and context.

13B103EDC05C44DEA6845F358C9A0686.description: Describe, using basic dance terminology, the qualities and characteristics of a dance from one's own cultural movement practice or other dance experiences. Compare them to the qualities and characteristics found in a different dance genre, style, or cultural movement practice.

93042414392B4C34BBA3F20A6B3BDAAA.description: Explain the basic structure of a dance (e.g. ABA) and where choreographic devices (e.g. theme and variation, call and response) appear in the dance.

4475D13EF87B4E8285848651AE594233.description: Dance is perceived and analyzed to comprehend its compositional structure.

3F67BEA7B9CA4725B7D988041AD9435D.description: Explore solutions to adapt to interaction with production elements (e.g. music/sound, props, costumes, sets) to enhance performance of a dance. Observe video recording as a tool to improve performance.

B05AAE16DD0D403D872E97731D4C256A.description: Adapt dance to alternative performance venues by modifying spacing and movements in accordance with the performance space. Document the process in writing. Demonstrate appropriate performer and audience etiquette in informal and formal performances. Post-performance, share peer performance experiences and arrive at group decisions about improving performance.

B144CA1CE5614FCCAE5D7593819A77E6.description: Dance performance is an interaction between performers, production elements, and audience that heightens and amplifies artistic expression.

CDFC76989EC94CACADF99627623980BA.description: Convey meaning through the presentation of artistic work.

A6927D9685FA4C4194BBFA9D0B62C63E.description: Collaborate with peer ensemble members to repeat sequences, synchronize actions, and refine spatial relationships to improve performance quality. Synthesize kinesthetic awareness and constructive feedback to establish personal performance goals in daily class practice and rehearsal.

F14FE9D872EF4EDBB0E1F7EE74197980.description: Demonstration safe body use practices during technical exercises and movement combinations. Discuss how these practices, along with healthful eating habits, promote strength, flexibility, endurance, and injury prevention.

D776EBD11A954129A1252ED18E362288.description: Recall and execute a series of dance phrases, using fundamental dance skills (e.g. alignment, coordination, balance, core support, kinesthetic awareness, clarity of movement).

A5484F5F5E3346408A9C1CD1FC88E2F9.description: Dancers use the body-mind principles and develop the body as an instrument for artistry and artistic expression.

A706A2ACA2054591B2397687FB656FB4.description: Develop and refine artistic techniques and work for presentation.

139362A70C2B477B943D87FB41A7A818.description: Explore a range of movement qualities, including the effect of music on phrasing and dynamics. Generate movement from both central initiation (torso) and peripheral initiation (distal) and analyze the relationship between initiation and energy.

87C2D9EFC3B148FCB65B87963FCDAABE.description: Dance to a variety of rhythms generated from internal and external sources. Perform movement phrases that show the ability to respond to metric and rhythmical changes.

7CD2EDF3286948248230212317250255.description: Integrate static and dynamic shapes and floor and air pathways into dance sequences. Establish relationships with other dancers through focus of eyes and other body parts. Convert inward focus to outward focus for projecting out to far space.

68F6EC8CB60E4418ADC3BA286C9BCE78.description: Space, time, and energy are basic elements of dance.

A2FD02C1EC9E412C9C09D84415765AA0.description: Select, analyze, and interpret artistic work for presentation.

FB2C1D622ED64468A7359CFE5549B1D3.description: Document various stages in the revision of a dance sequence through writing, symbols, or media technology.

4E0EC82AEB5640AE87A0991ECC75FC4B.description: Explore alternate movement revisions, using self, peer, or teacher feedback, to expand choreographic ideas for a dance study that communicates artistic intent. Explain movement choices and refinements.

3B520B521DC4437BA83A5CC90B200D31.description: Choreographers analyze, evaluate, refine, and document their work to communicate meaning.

14BE40DA0DFB474799DC4ADA78163834.description: Identify, explore, and select production elements (e.g. music/sound, props, costumes, lights, set, video) that heighten and intensify the artistry of a dance and are adaptable for various performance spaces. Analyze production and non-production dance jobs.

12164376EDA047AAB718E1D4EB547DF8.description: Develop a dance study by selecting specific movement vocabulary to communicate a main idea. Discuss how the dance communicates the idea non-verbally.

88E75B7F0A3E4E4F8786415E94A5AD69.description: Apply a variety of choreographic devices (e.g. addition, subtraction) to expand choreographic possibilities and develop a main idea. Explain reasoning for movement choices.

60E41256249943318CF9C8C557F8C8AB.description: The elements of dance, dance structures, and choreographic structures serve as both a foundation and a departure point for choreographers.

1CB91E0FB85F4539A082A9CF37854E19.description: Organize and develop artistic ideas and work.

A08BB7EEB1284C96870BA76D9A76D289.description: Construct and solve multiple movement problems by using the elements of dance to develop choreographic content. Describe the process of creation and the solutions, using genre-specific vocabulary when appropriate.

D0EFB1A8A3B54C9F8D2038B3898329A4.description: Build content for choreography, using a variety of stimuli (e.g. music/sound, dance exemplars, literary forms, notation, ideas and images, own experiences, objects/props, natural phenomena, world news and social issues).

1C0C4F6BA5BF46D8A25A57F0D4DC6CFE.description: Choreographers are inspired by a variety of sources to convey concepts and ideas through movement for artistic expression.

E0CE635ABE564023903EE7A40D18DD16.description: Generate and conceptualize artistic ideas and work.

B6AEDFA674584DEFB359352A1B3814F9.description: Theater artists allow awareness of relationships between self and others to influence and inform their work.

C967E8AFF3ED4B4AA476BAA282B307BE.description: Use a prop or costume to enhance a guided drama experience.

2B6B003264924FE8940AF9A9B497EB87.description: Collaborate on a scene in a guided drama experience.

73C7D24F44FF4785B15F6D251EF6E813.description: Theater artists apply criteria to investigate, explore, and assess drama and theater work.

00CBD396BA1440FA8AA61B69942CC1C6.description: Apply criteria to evaluate artistic work.

0316E24AD59143D1B36E3CA5147A74EF.description: Contribute to group guided drama experiences and informally share with peers.

6E458592EDE14C8280E1BEA94C4DDC3C.description: Theater artists share and present stories, ideas, and envisioned worlds to explore the human experience.

FCB1CB96066146F88F9651BD1DD55FAE.description: Convey meaning through the presentation of artistic work.

C6DC5BAB52484EC6A8E990985F2345C3.description: Explore technical elements in a guided drama experience.

783A569783E848B38D4439515A2FB3EE.description: Develop and refine artistic techniques and work for presentation.

73E5CEFA36AA48E3991023CDFFFCF2E0.description: Alter voice and body to expand and articulate nuances of a character in a guided drama experience.

7A1D0FDDBD6E4025832DC20BA0CC4F09.description: The essence of theater is storytelling.

86EF83EFE24843FEA23FFA4FC3E546CC.description: Independently generate multiple representations of a single object.

A06DDB0D53B14D1E9DDD625FFC2C6827.description: Use and adapt sounds and movements in a guided drama experience.

3DDA9512D1E641149A25BA794AE305D4.description: Recognize and correct inappropriate verb shifts.

ECA42CDA13CE4D7BBBD07803390D5C33.description: Form and use verbs in the active and passive voice.

78E0A219983846E4BDD9F7D3A4D2ABAB.description: Explain the function of verbals (gerunds, participles, infinitives).

BDB0DA9A57CA444D943313FA015869C5.description: Use simple, compound, complex, and compound-complex sentences to signal differing relationships among ideas.

7ADDAE71E772445A8EB3E8241F2E08F3.description: Place phrases and clauses within a sentence, recognizing and correcting misplaced and dangling modifiers.

19C98F3735514DE388FB15AB3FCB763A.description: Explain the function of phrases and clauses in general, as well as in specific sentences.

D98FB3658F4A4D0EACF5AE642C8ACB97.description: Recognize and correct pronouns that have unclear or ambiguous antecedents.

0958455F81A3412C9371F25FBC60DB2A.description: Recognize and correct inappropriate shifts in pronoun number and person.

A13358107EEA479DA9922226A9D1A8B6.description: Ensure that pronouns are in the proper case (subjective, objective, and possessive).

31B74EB4C4844653BA5EFD6C131E945C.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of academic English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

413FF7B6527C4C33831C8F69F068FA51.description: Conventions of Academic English/Language for Learning

8F242F885BE64DDDAEB973957A3FA2BE.description: Acquire and accurately use general academic and content-specific words and phrases; apply vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

824B041A17DF4A3894D442B8F3A76C52.description: Distinguish among the connotations of words with similar denotations (e.g., bullheaded, willful, firm, persistent, resolute).

DB71E6C792E94D07AB76B848F7C6E601.description: Use the relationship between particular words to better understand each of the words.

04FA58FFA44649D48136D195ABAF6E2E.description: Interpret figures of speech including irony and puns in context.

5DED3DF2380C4B2CABDC4EB7CCBEEEE5.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

5FE51FBECF124EBE901C871C2F1F6968.description: Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

9B8CAA498D8B45CC981564647854C290.description: Consult general and specialized reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses) to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning or its part of speech.

A6471693FE914C5DB971768A28CBDD5D.description: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek or Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., precede, recede, secede).

57C8569E1CA448A9A4CCE827D69E2EDB.description: Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence or paragraph; a word's position or function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

1A30ED0CD1654BF6B7C4C0079BA29E27.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

7F7D4ED5C75D4C079DD9C2BADEFD93FD.description: Use verbs in the active and passive voice and in the conditional and subjunctive mood to achieve particular effects (e.g., emphasizing the actor or the action; expressing uncertainty or describing a state contrary to fact).

4EB967BB93094182978CFBD5EF8CEADA.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

06F8231563EE4BC0A88055D971413FFE.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

7D58958007E14503930ED05FEB7C3D95.description: Integrate digital media and/or visual displays in presentations to clarify information, strengthen claims and evidence, and add elements of interest to engage the audience.

EDA071063F7B4495AB112D98CBC3C343.description: Present claims and findings, emphasizing salient points in a focused, coherent manner with relevant evidence, valid reasoning, and well-chosen details; use appropriate eye contact, adequate volume, and clear enunciation.

CAB5FA1F2E9F462FBF89EEA1E862F911.description: Delineate a speaker's argument and specific claims, evaluating for sound reasoning, and the relevance and sufficiency of the evidence; identify when irrelevant evidence is introduced.

6ACEEB75673045E18D8D2E9DBCC8B5BC.description: Analyze the purpose of information presented in diverse formats (e.g., including visual, quantitative, and oral) and evaluate the motives (e.g., social, commercial, political) behind its presentation.

929395270D32436E8199F6587B171DE1.description: Acknowledge new information expressed by others, and, when warranted, qualify or justify personal views in light of the evidence presented.

2FA08FD43E344510B8755FC81D620CE9.description: Pose questions that connect the ideas of several speakers and respond to others' questions and comments with relevant evidence, observations, and ideas.

D8141F64B73942B08176C506AA36C552.description: Follow norms for collegial discussions and decision-making, track progress toward specific goals and deadlines, and define individual roles as needed.

07A79F7EA8FA4F64A308A44946A8A636.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read or researched material under study; draw on that preparation by referring to evidence on the topic, text, or issue to probe and reflect on ideas under discussion.

7A968869096F49EE96EEBFC6625D5D71.description: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions with diverse partners; express ideas clearly and persuasively, and build on those of others.

AF9414C1AA5C4A5BB9CFE521F386445C.description: Gather relevant information from multiple sources; assess the credibility and accuracy of each source; quote or paraphrase the data and conclusions of others; avoid plagiarism and follow a standard format for citation.

A7A064F7794B478198870F4FDC09743A.description: Conduct research to answer questions, including self-generated questions, drawing on multiple sources, refocusing the inquiry when appropriate. Generate additional related questions that allow for multiple avenues of exploration.

3A223788A4C04A8CB98EA7528A03DA28.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

F5AFF4E975DC40B1A498AF713FAB2615.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research. Apply grade 8 Reading standards to both literary and informational text, where applicable.

0535D125EB2A4C3989CFEC9CE656D775.description: Create a poem, story, play, art work, or other response to a text, author, theme or personal experience; explain divergences from the original text when appropriate.

9E84D46C550945FFA571128517704683.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from and reflects on what is experienced, observed, or resolved over the course of the narrative.

C37CC7F1436C4D2890A6CD18B8D80B1D.description: Use precise words and phrases, relevant descriptive details, and sensory language to capture the action and convey experiences and events.

2F25A6E67CC94C06B739612621093ABD.description: Use a variety of transitional words, phrases, and clauses to convey sequence, signal shifts from one time frame or setting to another, and show the relationships among experiences and events.

42B5AC3D078D4A9DAE1C4BD28C519F79.description: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, description, and reflection to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.

C323B69C229F45C3988A496784881E33.description: Engage the reader by establishing a point of view and introducing a narrator and/or characters.

D095C19C4700483C98712808E78BA863.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective techniques, relevant descriptive details and clear sequencing.

7295B17BC86A473ABEB43F2F5B105586.description: Establish and maintain a style appropriate to the writing task.

235474F4689E49C18B94F9E9A9CCA975.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that explains the significance of the information presented.

E7EEA954D4FD4BC58556B786930E7F08.description: Use appropriate and varied transitions to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.

C005F06F98EB4613AE12C95DE615BD34.description: Use precise language and content-specific vocabulary to explain a topic.

8258B48C8D1B4C51A619379AED80B494.description: Develop a topic with relevant facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples; include formatting, graphics, and multimedia when useful to aid comprehension.

DA2FDC01138141098E0B5E4EDB0B812D.description: Introduce a topic clearly, previewing what is to follow; organize ideas, concepts, and information, using strategies such as definition, classification, comparison/contrast, and cause/effect.

2D3974289D2F48639BDBA8AF335FD93C.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas, concepts, and information through the selection, organization, and analysis of relevant content.

75A27F8C9F074B6DAEF07138B757D794.description: Maintain a style and tone appropriate to the writing task.

C6176DE8714A4DD1AE37FD7CD450BE1E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that explains the significance of the argument presented.

CD4EBE5B11774B49A4A7DDD2CBAD73E8.description: Use appropriate and varied transitions to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.

222E02C3E9B245C8AD59EC4BF2039E7F.description: Use precise language and content-specific vocabulary to argue a claim.

499F4152FD144057BD0E87FF1087BFB5.description: Support claim(s) with logical reasoning and relevant evidence, using credible sources while demonstrating an understanding of the topic or text.

920ADB9DC85D4815B624B9949C26E7D7.description: Introduce a precise claim, acknowledge and distinguish the claim(s) from a counterclaim, and organize the reasons and evidence logically.

982DE9DF8B7E4D1CA7F3B0D4216AF778.description: Write arguments to support claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence.

143B689B70CD492EA40C4F64035A2AF1.description: Choose and develop criteria in order to evaluate the quality of texts. Make connections to other texts, ideas, cultural perspectives, eras, and personal experiences.

3D76C25A41B84DE68A479807A5A8E518.description: Trace and evaluate an argument and specific claims in a text, assessing whether the reasoning is valid and the evidence is relevant and sufficient and recognizing when irrelevant evidence is introduced.

E7A8ACD0E5EE4A80A8020FEB009AF6A6.description: Evaluate the advantages and disadvantages of using different media-- text, audio, video, stage, or digital-- to present a particular subject or idea and analyze the extent to which a production remains faithful to or departs from the written text.

6E32C82D031046CA95C56519281113C0.description: In literary texts, analyze how the differences between the point of view, perspectives of the characters, the audience, or reader create effects such as mood and tone. In informational texts, analyze how the author addresses conflicting evidence or viewpoints.

B67AAFCB6CE44540843D148710D78BB5.description: In literary texts, and informational texts, compare and contrast the structures of two or more texts in order to analyze how the differing structure of each text contributes to overall meaning, style, theme or central idea.

D03D571985C0404687BFC8C083B2C590.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative and connotative meanings. Analyze the impact of specific word choices on meaning, tone, and mood, including words with multiple meanings.

C2616FBAB2854996A6893739288B5E2A.description: In literary texts, analyze how particular lines of dialogue or events propel the action, reveal aspects of a character, or provoke a decision. In informational texts, analyze how individuals, events, and ideas are introduced, relate to each other, and are developed.

8FC628A4C91240A0893ACCA0A2AAF708.description: Determine one or more themes or central ideas of a text and analyze their development over the course of the text; summarize a text.

18EFB5B7FB94406E9D93459FF0A468F6.description: Cite textual evidence to strongly support an analysis of what the text says explicitly/implicitly and make logical inferences.
